Release notes

Sourced from github.com/vapor/jwt-kit's releases.

5.1.1 - Fix crash when verifying corrupted token

What's Changed

Fix crash when verifying corrupted token by @​ptoffy in #217

Fix #213

This patch was released by @​ptoffy

Full Changelog: https://github.com/vapor/jwt-kit/compare/5.1.0...5.1.1

5.1.0 - Add FirebaseAuth identity token

What's Changed

Add FirebaseAuth identity token by @​petrpavlik in #207

  • Add support for Firebase Auth by introducing FirebaseAuthIdentityToken.
  • Fix some unit tests not being run. Probably a regression cause by migration to the new testing framework.

Adding support for Firebase Authentication was okayed by @​ptoffy, see here vapor/jwt#159.

I’ll also follow up with a PR for https://github.com/vapor/jwt once this is merged in.

This patch was released by @​ptoffy

Full Changelog: https://github.com/vapor/jwt-kit/compare/5.0.1...5.1.0

title: Add support to import passwords & bookmarks from Safari on iOS 18.2 and above
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1142021229838617/1208707884599800
Tech Design URL:
CC:

**Description**:
Allow users to import their Safari data from both the Bookmarks and Passwords screen + CSV password files from Google Password Manager

**Optional E2E tests**:
- [ ] Run macOS PIR E2E tests
	Check this to run the Personal Information Removal end to end tests. If updating CCF, or any PIR related code, tick this.

**Steps to test this PR**:
Note: Test data for importing can be found here: https://app.asana.com/0/1142021229838617/1209387060206740
1. Testing on iOS 18.2 or above, disable Sync and delete any saved passwords or bookmarks (this can be done via the respective debug screens).
2. From the empty Passwords screen confirm the correct UI is presented as per [figma](https://www.figma.com/design/dCEDJ0tfWY0towtX34bgXB/Support-CSV-import-to-mobile?node-id=914-11345&t=itue6y6EUYuN1Hl2-1) and that both buttons take users to the correct respective screen
3. Tap `Import Passwords` and select a .zip file containing both passwords & bookmarks. If using the test file noted above, the preview counts should be 11 passwords & 29 bookmarks
4. Complete the import and confirm the success screen data matches the preview
5. Unzip the zip file and repeat the import flow by importing just the passwords.csv, confirm the preview prompt is not presented and you are taken straight to the success screen.
6. Tap the `Sync & Back Up Data` button and confirm you are correctly taken to the Sync screen
7. Go back to the Passwords screen and confirm the correct buttons are presented from the overflow menu and their actions are correct.
8. Delete all bookmarks and go to the Bookmarks screen
9. From the empty screen main button, repeat the import flow from Step 3 confirming all data is correct
10. Attempt importing the bookmarks.html from the unzipped folder and confirm no preview prompt is presented
11. Tap the `Sync & Back Up Data` button and confirm you are correctly taken to the Sync screen
12. Go back to the Bookmarks screen and confirm the overflow menu buttons behave correctly
13. Quickly regression test on simulator or device running iOS 18.1 or earlier, confirming the Passwords empty screen and overflow do not have the new import UI
14. Repeat this same test from the Bookmarks screen where the `Import HTML File` button should immediately launch the document picker

title: Sync: Don't send unexpected disable pixel on 401
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209370736592296

**Description**:

I added a pixel - sync_was_disabled_unexpectedly - to fire when sync was disabled for a reason other than a user explicitly switching it off. This has been firing quite regularly.

However, there are still potentially reasons that we would expect to happen during normal use (e.g a user deleting their account from another device resulting in a 401).

This prevents this pixel from firing in the cases that we know about and are by design.

**Steps to test this PR**:
1. Enable sync on one device (from any branch)
2. Build this branch on another device
3. Sync to the first device
4. On the first device, "Turn Off and Delete Server Data..."
5. Check that the second device does **not** send the `sync_was_disabled_unexpectedly` Pixel

title: Update Condition for Creating a New Window from a Dragged Tab
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209434873980812

### Description
We received the following feedback:

> Just now I was trying to drag a tab out of the window and even if I brought it to the very tippy top of my screen (see screenshot) it would just bounce back into the existing window. I had to make the window smaller. It just seems unnecessary. Do we have control over this? 
> I notice on Chrome it’s waaaaaaay more responsive — as soon as I pulled a tab several pixels upward it created a new window.

To address this I’ve implemented the following:
* Added a check for `isDroppedAboveTabBar` that triggers when the drop point is more than 10 points above the tab bar
* Now we will create a new window if either:
** The tab is dropped above the tab bar (new condition)
** The tab is dropped far away from the tab bar (existing condition)

### Testing Steps
1. Launch browser
2. Create multiple tabs and drag them left and right to rearrange them. Ensure this functions as expected, and new windows are not created
3. Now drag a tab slightly up above the window. Ensure a new window is created from the dragged tab

### Impact and Risks
* Impacts tab functionality

#### What could go wrong?
* Dragged tabs don’t function as expected

title: Updated logic to resolve /pro redirect
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/414709148257752/1207974891378353
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209309164544658 
CC: @federicocappelli 

### Description
First part of "Make it easier to test changes to in-app purchase funnels" aimed at implementing dynamic rules for resolving subscription URL for `/pro` redirects. Additionally the interception criteria has been expanded to also include `duck.co` domain when internal user mode is enabled.

### Testing Steps
Please verify preexisting and updated rules for creation of destination URL are implemented correctly as described in TD both on iOS and macOS. 
- In some of the cases the resulting target URL may make no sense (nothing is deployed) but the purpose is to verify URL building logic. 
- Also if run in the staging environment the end url will be appended with `environment` parameter.

1. Navigating to `https://duckduckgo.com/pro` redirects to native purchase flow with `https://duckduckgo.com/subscriptions`
2.  Navigating to `https://subdomain.duckduckgo.com/pro` redirects to native purchase flow with `https://subdomain.duckduckgo.com/subscriptions`
3.  Navigating to `https://duckduckgo.com:1234/pro` redirects to native purchase flow with `https://duckduckgo.com:1234/subscriptions` 
4. Navigating to `https://duckduckgo.com/pro?origin=test` redirects to native purchase flow with `https://duckduckgo.com/subscriptions?origin=test` 
5. Navigating to `https://subdomain.duckduckgo.com:1234/pro?foo=bar#fragment` redirects to native purchase flow with `https://subdomain.duckduckgo.com:1234/subscriptions?foo=bar#fragment`
6. When internal user mode is disabled navigating to `https://duck.co/pro` does not trigger redirect.
7.  When internal user mode is enabled navigating to `https://duck.co/pro` does trigger redirect to `https://duckduckgo.com/subscriptions`
8.  When internal user mode is enabled navigating to `https://subdomain.duck.co:1234/pro?foo=bar#fragment` does trigger redirect to `https://subdomain.duckduckgo.com:1234/subscriptions?foo=bar#fragment`


### Impact and Risks
See: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209375523991341

#### What could go wrong?
- current `duckduckgo.com/pro` redirect stops working
- during redirect we omit the `origin` attribution parameter

title: Pixels for importing passwords & bookmarks Safari data
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1201645688934642/1208707884599803


### Description
Adds new pixels for the safari data import flows for passwords & bookmarks

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
**Import Flow**
1. Start by ensuring all saved passwords & bookmarks have been deleted and that Sync is disabled.
2. Go to the Passwords Management screen and verify that the Import Password button is visible and that pixel `autofill_import_passwords_import_button_shown` fires
3. Tap the Import Password button and verify pixel `autofill_import_passwords_import_button_tapped` fires
4. Verify the Import Instructions screen appears and pixel `import_instructions_displayed` fires with parameter `source=passwords`
4. Tap the toggle between Safari/Chrome instructions and verify pixel `import_instructions_toggled` fires
5. Tap the Select File button and verify pixel `import_instructions_file_button_tapped` fires with parameter `source=passwords`
6. Select different file types and verify corresponding pixels:
   - Select a ZIP file: `import_instructions_file_selected-zip` fires with `source=passwords`
   - Select a CSV file: `import_instructions_file_selected-csv` fires with `source=passwords`
7. Tap back to exit the screen and verify pixel `import_instructions_cancelled` fires with `source=passwords`
8. Go back into the import screen and select a zip file containing bookmarks & passwords
9. Verify the preview prompt appears and pixel `import_preview_prompt_displayed` fires with `source=passwords`
10. Tap Cancel and verify pixel `import_preview_prompt_dismissed` fires with `source=passwords`
11. Select the zip file again and this time tap Continue and verify pixel `import_preview_prompt_confirmed` fires with `source=passwords`
12. Complete a password import with a valid file containing multiple passwords
12. Verify the result screen appears and pixel `import_result_displayed` fires with `source=passwords`
14. Verify pixel `import_result_passwords_success` fires with:
   - `saved_credentials=lots` (or appropriate bucket based on count)
   - `skipped_credentials=none` (or appropriate bucket if duplicates exist)
   - `source=passwords`
15. Verify pixel `import_result_bookmarks_success` fires with:
  - `bco=<COUNT>`
  -  `source=passwords`
15. Since Sync is not enabled:
   - Verify the sync button appears and pixel `import_result_sync_button_shown` fires with `source=passwords`
   - Tap the sync button and verify pixel `import_result_sync_button_tapped` fires with `source=passwords`
17. Go to the Passwords Management screen and verify the Import Password button is not visible and the pixel `autofill_import_passwords_import_button_shown` does not fire
18. From the overflow menu select Import Password and verify pixel `autofill_import_passwords_overflow_menu_tapped` fires
19. Repeat Steps 1 - 18 starting from the Bookmarks screen, confirming the bookmark equivalent pixels fire and that the parameter is `source=bookmarks` during the import flow. 

**Error Cases**
1. Attempt to import a malformed csv file (see [asana](https://app.asana.com/0/1201645688934642/1208707884599803/f) for test data files)
2. Verify pixel `import_result_passwords_parsing` fires with `source=passwords`
3. Attempt to import a malformed html file (see [asana](https://app.asana.com/0/1201645688934642/1208707884599803/f) for test data files)
4. Verify pixel `import_result_bookmarks_parsing` fires with `source=bookmarks` as well as legacy pixel `m_bi_e`
5. Attempt to import a corrupted ZIP file (see [asana](https://app.asana.com/0/1201645688934642/1208707884599803/f) for test data files)
6. Verify pixel `import_result_unzipping` fires with appropriate source parameter based on import type

title: Post app delegate work - cleanup of and old code and make auto clear visually smoother
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1208832732122405
CC: @dus7 

### Description
1. Remove old migration code
2. Make autoclearing smoother, by removing overlay if there is no work to be done

### Testing Steps
1. Enable Data Clearing in Settings after 5 minutes
2. Change the code inside AutoClear 
```
        case .delay5min:
            return elapsedTime > 5 * 60
```
to:
```
        case .delay5min:
            return elapsedTime > 10
```
3. Open any site and go to background for at least 10 seconds.
4. In App Switcher notice you cannot see app content, because of BlankSnapshotVC
5. Reopen app and notice the content is gone.
6. Open any site again and go to background for less than 10 secs (so autoclearing doesn't happen)
7. Again, in App Switcher notice you cannot see app content, because of BlankSnapshotVC
8. Reopen app and notice the content loads almost immediately (there is no glitch, with some intermediary screen blinking)

### Impact and Risks
Medium

#### What could go wrong?
1/ Make sure the autoclearing still works (especially the one that doesn't require app restart)

title: AuthV2 / iOS app Auth V1 + V2
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1205842942115003/1209170372758738/f
CC: @miasma13 

### Description

This PR implements the use of AuthV2 in the IOS app.

The good:
-  AuthV2 is fully integrated into the iOS app.
- The authentication still uses V1 but V2 is configured and added behind an informal feature flag. (see `isAuthV2Enabled`)
- NetworkProtection doesn't import Subscription anymore and instead uses shared protocols like `BSK/Common/SubscriptionTokenHandling.swift`

The bad
- We now have some code duplication, especially in the settings UI, all will be removed alongside AuthV1
- I introduced "bridge" protocols (see `SubscriptionAuthV1toV2Bridge`) for aligning AuthV1 and AuthV2 behaviours, all will be removed alongside AuthV1
- The code is not very clean, I prioritised risk reduction and changes minimisation over code cleanness, all will be improved when we remove AuthV1
- There are some ugly force unwrap for optional vars that shouldn't really be optional like `let subscriptionManagerV1: (any SubscriptionManager)?` and `let subscriptionManagerV2: (any SubscriptionManagerV2)?`, all will be removed with AuthV1 but for now they are needed for allowing the coexistence of Auth v1 and v2

### Testing Steps
1. Subscription should work as usual, no feature changes are expected.

### Impact and Risks

High impact, we can break Subscription + VPN

title: Implement deleting history by range in History View
body:
<!--

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/72649045549333/1209328755192083

### Description
This change allows to delete history items by range in History View. A native dialog is added to confirm history
deletion. The deletion defaults to burning, which additionally clears website data, but it can be adjusted to only
delete history entries.

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Launch the app from Xcode, set internal user flag and override `historyView` flag in Debug Menu so that it's enabled. Open main menu one more time to allow cmd+y shortcut to load.
2. Open history view (cmd+y) and verify that it's empty.
3. Visit a few websites, go back to the history view and refresh it.
4. Verify that you see the "Today" range apart from "All".
5. Click the trash icon next to the "Today" range and verify that it displays the delete dialog.
6. Cancel the dialog and verify that history is not deleted.
7. Repeat step 5 and delete history. Verify that history entries are gone.
8. Visit a website where you can log in to an account. Go to history view and delete history with burning. Verify that you're logged out of the account.
9. Populate fake history via Debug Menu -> History -> Add 10 visits each day. Refresh history view.
10. Try deleting various ranges and verify that data is properly counted in the dialog[0] and then properly deleted.\
11. Repeat step 9 as needed and use the "Delete All" button (note that "Delete All" while filtering the view by a search phrase is not implemented yet). Verify that it works the same as deleting the currently active range.

[0] – please note that multiple visits to the same URL on a single day are conflated into 1 entry on the screen and only visible items are counted and reported to the user in the delete dialog, while upon deletion, all visits are deleted whatsoever.


### Impact and Risks
<!--

title: Default values for native app feature flags
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1200194497630846/1209432750561445
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1202926619870900/1209523442095784
CC:

### Description

The current implementation of FeatureFlagger in BSK requires all feature flags to be explicitly defined in both the codebase and the privacy configuration service, which is used to remotely control feature flags at runtime. Over time, this leads to an accumulation of legacy flags within the privacy configuration, increasing maintenance overhead and complexity.

Introducing a new feature flag type: Failsafe. A Failsafe flag would be enabled by default in the codebase and would not have an explicit equivalent in the privacy configuration service on launch. However, it could be remotely disabled via the privacy configuration if necessary.

I've added some example flags for demonstrative purposes but would be happy to remove them if the reviewer thinks that's best.

### Testing Steps 
**macOS**
1. Go to Debug -> Feature Flag Overrides
2. Look for the two feature flags named `failsafeExample*`
3. Make sure their default values are on

**iOS**
1. Go to Settings -> All debug options -> Feature Flags
2. Look for the two feature flags named `failsafeExample*`
3. Make sure their default values are on

### Impact and Risks

Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
In later PRs if someone accidentally defaults a feature to on
**Mitigation**: All FeatureFlag / Experiment FeatureFlag definitions default to `false` so the developer has to consciously set this.

### Quality Considerations
See https://app.asana.com/0/481882893211075/1209556022249884/f

body:

### Stack PR

- https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/255
   - https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/113  -- 👈 You're here
       - https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/157

### Description

Adds a feature flag to enable support to run the VPN as a System Extension.

You can enable and disable the feature flag from the debug menu.

Behavior is:
- If the feature flag is off, the user will have the app extension as usual.
- If the feature flag is on, then:

   - New installs will get the system extension.

- Test the App Store build and:

- Test uninstalling the VPN in all above scenarios.

title: Create SAD and ATT banner vs popover experiment
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/45878998844068/1209518320481653
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description
**SAD** =  Set As Default
**ATT** = Add To Taskbar/Dock

The following work adds a one-time popover or banner that we will show to users. The plan is to measure which is more effective in adding to the dock and setting it as default.

Given that we want to measure the impact of the popover, banner, or nothing (control), we will fire experiment pixels when one of these actions occurs.

Some notes:
- The popover should only be shown in one window, while the banner should be shown in all windows (and if it is closed in one, it should be closed in all windows at the same time)
- Neither of the options should be shown again if they are dismissed. The local flag override marks the prompt as not shown for testing purposes so we can test it.
- To be eligible for the experiment, you need to have completed onboarding, not be a new user (more than a week after the first launch), and not have the browser in the dock or as the default browser.

**Screenshots**

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6668869b-ea2a-4d9a-bddd-2ee939bb9e28)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfb6a6ad-e4a4-4d4a-8de6-9cd9f265748f)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28c9eeca-580a-48aa-8f32-bc8ea596aea1)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e18fdb93-dfdb-4888-9dfb-eadcf38ab589)

### Testing Steps

There are two ways of testing this: 

1. The first one is using the local overrides and selecting either the popover or banner. To use it, go to the Debug Menu -> Feature Flag Overrides and select the `popoverVsBanner` experiment.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6c38712-8533-4b28-9904-6b349e6311a4)

3. The second one uses the following JSON file: https://www.jsonblob.com/api/1344683245740154880. That adds the experiment to test:

```json
"setAsDefaultAndAddToDock": {
      "state": "enabled",
      "exceptions": [],
      "features": {
        "popoverVsBannerExperiment": {
          "state": "enabled",
          "cohorts": [
            {
              "name": "control",
              "weight": 1
            },
            {
              "name": "popover",
              "weight": 1
            },
            {
              "name": "banner",
              "weight": 1
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "hash": "0fe5af5a94e036bf5d78076df6dd771b"
    }
```

You must manually override the Privacy Config with the JSON Blob URL, which should enroll you in the feature. This one is more random, given that for testing a particular cohort, you will need to change the weight in the JSON.

To replace the URL tap `Set custom configuration URL` in the debug menu above:

![Screenshot 2025-02-28 at 3 28 29 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/979195ec-6f1a-4033-8268-441bf30ebfb0)

### Impact and Risks
**Low**: This will be handled by a feature flag, so if there is any problem or complaint, we can just kill it. It is also a popover and a banner that can be dismissed.

#### What could go wrong?
- The feature is not working as expected and is damaging retention; Solution -> We can remove the feature flag.
- Showing the prompt more than once. Solution -> We are storing a flag, so we don’t do this.

title: Optimise autofill device authentication checks
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/414709148257752/1209362950606365
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description
`AutofillSettingStatus` refactored to cache a users device authentication status (i.e. do they have a passcode set on their device which is a requirement for the autofill feature) while the app is in foreground instead of constantly querying every time a check is required. This should greatly reduce the number of times LAcontext().canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication, error: &error) is called which is currently the source of an increased hang rate and occasional crashes.

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Prerequisites: Testing on device which has (at a minimum) a passcode set + wnsure there are some passwords saved and that `Save and autofill passwords` is enabled.
2. In `AutofillSettingStatus` set a breakpoint at line 44 `return LAContext().canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication, error: &error)`
3. Launch the app and load a webpage. Confirm the breakpoint only hits once
4. Visit [autofill.me](http://autofill.me/form/login-simple), enter new credentials and save them when prompted
5. Minimise the app, go to system Settings and disable the passcode on the device
6. Come back to the app, reload the tab and go back to the `autofill.me` login screen. Confirm the breakpoint hits again (but just once)
7. Confirm that you are not prompted to fill the login that was saved in step 5 and that there is no key icon in the login fields
8. Go to the Passwords screen and confirm you are presented with a screen stating that a passcode is required (and that no passwords are shown)
9. Re-enable a passcode on your device and return to the app
10. Reload the `autofill.me` login webpage and confirm that autofill prompts are back

title: Initialize dock customizer after first launch date is set
body:
Task/Issue URL:https://app.asana.com/0/1204006570077678/1209486069724547
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description
The blue notification dot in the more options menu was shown in a fresh install. The problem was that the blue dot was checking if two days had passed since the `firstLaunchDate`, but for new users, the `DockCustomizer` was being created before its initialization, and the default value of it was a month ago, causing the check to return true.

![Screenshot 2025-03-04 at 4 25 56 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fff2cf06-fce5-4b2e-bf6a-f14c422b6e67)

The fix moves the initialization of the `DockCustomizer` just after the `firstLaunchDate` is initialized.


### Testing Steps

1. Run `./clean-app.sh debug` to set the state as fresh
2. Run the application
3. The blue dot shouldn’t be present
4. Go to the `DockCustomizer` class and in the `startTimer` function, reduce the timer from `12 * 60 * 60`, to just one. This is just to make the check every one second
5. Run the app again
6. Run `defaults delete com.duckduckgo.macos.browser.debug first.app.launch.date` This will set the first launch date a month from here.
7. Check if the notification appears
8. Open multiple windows, it will appear there too
9. Open and close the more options menu, it should disappear from all windows.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

#### What could go wrong?
I do not foresee problems.

### Quality Considerations
This is pretty straightforward.

title: Mobile App forces refresh of tab content after some time, resulting in a lost page in low-no signal environments/lost page progress in others
body:
App version: 7.158.0.3
Device model: Iphone X
iOS/macOS version: 16.7.10

Steps to reproduce the bug: Return to a previously loaded tab after some time
Expected behaviour: Does not refresh a static website when undesired
Actual behaviour: Refreshes tab regardless of content and internet connectivity

When returning to a tab that may have been dormant for as little as 10 minutes, the browser treats it as though it were a social media feed and refreshes the content regardless of internet connectivity. This regularly results in lost content that was entirely loaded seconds ago, often hitting static websites with large data requirements for photos multiple times. Even in environments with good signal, it still results in losing progress along the page, with some pages now containing thousands of words this becomes tiresome to return to an article later in the day.

This is a completely unnecessary feature and doesn't seem to have a matching setting to disable at will.

title: [iOS] Onbording - Show "Try a Search” and “Visit Site" only once
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1142021229838617/1209605043831313

### Description

Show "Try a Search” & “Visit Site” Dax dialogs only once during the onboarding flow. 

### Testing Steps

To show the Dax dialogs again after they have been prompted:
1. Ensure you’re logged in as internal user.
2. Then open Settings → All debug options → Onboarding → Reset Dax Dialog State
3. Open a new tab, to see “Try a Search Dialog”.

**Scenario 1: Showing “Try a Search” & “Visit a Site" only once when opening new tabs.**
1. Wait for “Try a search” dialog is shown on new tab page.
2. Open a new tab.
3. “Visit a site” dialog should be shown.
4. Opean a new tab.
5. No dialog should be displayed on new tab page.

**Scenario 2: Showing “Try a Search” & “Visit a Site" only once when restarting the app.**
1. Wait for “Try a search” dialog is shown on new tab page.
2. Close and reopen the app.
3. “Visit a site” dialog should be shown.
4. Close and reopen the app.
5. No dialog should be displayed on new tab page.

**Scenario 3: Hide “Visit a site” on page reload.**
1. Wait for “Try a search” dialog is shown on new tab page.
2. Tap Surprise Me.
3. Wait for dialog to appear and tap the “Got It” button.
4. "Try visit a site" contextual dialog should appear.
5. Reload the page.
6. The dialog should dismiss.

**Scenario 4: Hide “Visit a site” on re-launch.**
1. Wait for “Try a search” dialog is shown on new tab page.
2. Tap Surprise Me.
3. Wait for dialog to appear and tap the “Got It” button.
4. "Try visit a site" contextual dialog should appear.
5. Close and re-open the app.
6. The website should reload and no dialog should appear.

**Scenario 5: Do not show “Visit site” contextually if users already seen the “Visit Site” on new tab page.**
1. Wait for “Try a search” dialog is shown on new tab page.
2. Open a new tab.
3. “Visit a site” dialog should be shown.
4. Search for “baby ducklings”.
5. Wait for performed search dialog to appear and tap the “Got It” button.
6. The dialog should hide since the user already was prompted with visit site in new tab page. 
7. Navigate to another website and continue the onboarding process.
8. Ensure onboarding can be completed per usual flow.

**Smoke Test onboarding flow.**
Smoke test onboarding to see if there any issues.

title: iOS: Privacy Pro Promotion Onboarding Experiment
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209578913377688

### Description
This PR adds the core implementation of the Privacy Pro Onboarding experiment. Note that at this point the related experiment design is still under review. This means that it’s possible our metrics (Pixels) will change. If this occurs I will follow-up with another PR.

### Test Setup ###
1. Fake a `treatment` cohort experiment -> Add `return .treatment` as the first line in `OnboardingPrivacyProPromoExperiment.getCohortIfenabled`

### Testing Steps
#### Test 1 ####
1. Delete the app from the simulator
2. Run the app
3. Proceed through onboarding to the ‘High Five’ step, tap ‘High Five'
4. Ensure you see the new Privacy Pro promotion dialog which nearly matches [this design](https://app.asana.com/0/0/1208678682266319) (Note: On iOS the bottom button has not outline as shown in design)
5. Tap ‘Learn More'
6. Ensure the Privacy Pro paywall is displayed
7. Navigate back to the new tab page
8. Ensure the promotion is gone
9. Open a new tab
10. Ensure no promotion is displayed

#### Test 2 ####
1. Delete the app from the simulator
2. Run the app
3. Proceed through onboarding to the ‘High Five’ step, tap ‘High Five'
4. Ensure you see the new Privacy Pro promotion dialog which nearly matches [this design](https://app.asana.com/0/0/1208678682266319) (Note: On iOS the bottom button has not outline as shown in design)
5. Tap ’Skip'
6. Ensure the promotion is dismissed
7. Open a new tab
8. Ensure no promotion is displayed

#### Test 3 ####
1. Fake a `control` cohort experiment -> Add `return .control` as the first line in `OnboardingPrivacyProPromoExperiment.getCohortIfenabled`
2. Repeat steps 1-3 of test 1
3. Ensure no promotion is displayed

### Impact and Risks
Low: Internally flagged experiment

title: iOS: Fix pixel values for subscription related errors
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1203936086921904/1209499063210750
CC:

### Description
We noticed that the 2 Privacy Pro pixels are badly reported due to having their values switched.

### Testing Steps
[iOS only]
Since it may be hard to reproduce real error cases to test the pixels, in `SubscriptionPagesUseSubscriptionFeature` you can add to one of the methods a forced `setTransactionError(...)` call that should trigger the pixel being sent.

1. Ensure that for `setTransactionError(.accountCreationFailed)` error a `.privacyProPurchaseFailureAccountNotCreated` pixel is being fired with a value of `m_privacy-pro_app_subscription-purchase_failure_account-creation`

3. Ensure that for `setTransactionError(.missingEntitlements)` error a `.privacyProPurchaseFailureBackendError` pixel is being fired with a value of `m_privacy-pro_app_subscription-purchase_failure_backend`


### Impact and Risks
Low: Wrong pixel values

Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1206226850447395/1209527858891474
CC:

### Description

This PR adopts changes done in `DesignResourcesKit` (https://github.com/duckduckgo/DesignResourcesKit/pull/11) package and migrates iOS code to use color resources from DRK.

Notable changes: 
* Colors are removed from `DuckUI`. Gaps in colors are filled with values from DRK.
* Color definitions from `UIColorsExtensions` are removed and translated to existing colors in DRK.
* `DeprecatedColors.xcassets` is removed and affected areas migrated to use values DRK.
* Colors from asset catalogs used in IB files were changed to `systemPurple` in order to make it obvious if they're not updated properly. Outlets were added to use colors from DRK in the code.

Note: when possible I used [this figma](https://www.figma.com/design/GzGKD6gR24AHoUqVykX1ah/📱-iOS-%26-iPadOS-Components?node-id=11479-26726&m=dev) file with all the sub-sections to find a matching color in DesignSystem.

    5. OmniBar message (CPM notification)
    6. Passwords & autofill
    7. Downloads progress and list
    8. Remote message 
    9. Unified feedback (breakage feedback)
    10. Voice search
    11. VPN settings tutorial

### Impact and Risks

title: Authv2 subscription recovery
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1205842942115003/1209568624984667
CC: @miasma13 

### Description

Major improvements:
- OAuthClient is now an actor, this mitigates an issue where multiple get/refresh token attempts were made in parallel and caused useless API calls and creation of multiple tokens.
- Full implementation of `DeadTokenRecoverer`, class in charge of automatically recovering a subscription in case of expired refresh token.
- Solved an issue where, in case of no connection at the app startup, StorePurchaseManagerV2 / availableProducts were not updated and every subsequent purchase attempt failed. Now the products are updated every time requested, if not previously available.
- `currentSubscriptionFeatures()` and `subscriptionManager.isFeatureAvailableForUser(...)` can now propagate an error correctly, this improved all entitlements check allowing the SubscriptionManager to detect fetch error and distinguish between a real lack of entitlements or a simple network failure (example: `macOS/DuckDuckGoVPN/DuckDuckGoVPNAppDelegate.swift`)

### Testing Steps

No-connection tests:
- subscribe to privacy pro
- kill the app
- disable connection (airplane mode on)
- open the app
- re-enable connection
- All should work as expected, a part [this bug](https://app.asana.com/0/1205842942115003/1209608044788440)

get Subscription failures
- subscribe to privacy pro
- while in the app, disable connection
- navigate the app settings and the subscription sub pages, all subscription entitlements shouldn't change and the subscription status shouldn't change

title: Remember last used folder when adding a bookmark
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

⚠️ If you're an external contributor, please file an issue before working on a PR. Discussing your changes beforehand will help ensure they align with our roadmap and that your time is well spent.
-->

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1201048563534612/1207897464675448

### Description:
This change updates the behavior of “Add Bookmark” popover shown from the address bar.
It will now remember the folder used last time a bookmark was added.  The implementation
reuses BookmarkFoldersStore by adding the ability to store last used folder for single bookmark
save dialog.

### Testing Steps
This is the change in a nutshell:
![demo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e39bc848-a8be-43b0-82f6-51c968797596)

1. Launch the app and open a website
2. Bookmark the website using the bookmark icon in the address bar or cmd+d shortcut
3. Verify that it created the bookmark in the root bookmarks folder.
4. Pick a different folder in the popover or create a new one to store the bookmark there.
5. Open another website and bookmark it the same way. Verify that the bookmark is created by default in the folder picked in the previous step.
6. Open bookmark manager and delete the folder picked in step 4.
7. Bookmark another website and verify that the bookmark is created in the root bookmarks folder.
8. Open Bookmarks Manager.
9. Create a new bookmark in some folder. Then open a non-bookmarked website and bookmark it from the address bar icon. Verify that it defaults to the folder you’ve used for making a bookmark in the Bookmarks Manager.
10. Move a bookmark to a different folder in Bookmarks Manager. Then repeat testing from step 9.
11. Move a folder to a different folder in Bookmarks Manager. Then repeat testing from step 9.

### Impact and Risks
Low: no UI and copy changes, just the logic for remembering last used folder.

#### What could go wrong?
If a folder was deleted, the lookup would fail and the setting would be ignored.

### Quality Considerations
No edge cases or performance considerations apply. I took time to add some unit tests to the popover view model also covering areas unrelated to this change.

title: Per-window Pinned Tabs
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

⚠️ If you're an external contributor, please file an issue before working on a PR. Discussing your changes beforehand will help ensure they align with our roadmap and that your time is well spent.
-->

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1148564399326804/1208198115490419
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1148564399326804/1209368276431904

### Description
We are enhancing the pinned tabs mechanism, allowing them to be specific to individual windows in addition to being shared across all application windows
The behavior of pinned tabs can be adjusted in General Settings
New users will have per-window pinned tabs as the default setting.
Users currently using shared pinned tabs will keep this behavior. However, after pinning another tab, they will see a discovery dialog introducing the option to switch to per-window pinned tabs

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
**Test new users have per-window pinned tabs set as default Setting**
1. Execute `./macOS/clean-app.sh debug`
2. Run the app and finish the onboarding process
3. Pin a couple of tabs in the current window
5. Open a new window and verify there are no pinned tabs
6. Test pinning a different set of tabs in the new window
7. Go to Settings -> General and verify the pinned tab setting is set to "Separate in each window"

**Test pinned tabs are merged correctly when switching to shared pinned tabs**
1. With the state from the previous test with multiple windows containing different set of pinned tabs, go to Settings -> General
2. Switch the pinned tabs setting to "Shared across all windows"
3. Verify you received an alert (warning) about pinned tabs being merged
4. Confirm the change in the alert
5. Verify the current window contains all pinned tabs merged
6. Verify the other window contains the same pinned tabs
7. Make some changes to pinned tabs and make sure they are applied to all windows

**Test switching from shared pinned tabs to per-window pinned tabs**
1. With the state from the previous test, go to Settings -> General
2. Switch the pinned tabs setting to "Separete in each window"
3. Verify the current window contains the same set of pinned tabs.
4. Verify the other window has no pinned tabs

**Test restoration of per window pinned tabs when the session restoration is turned off**
1. In Settings -> General, set "Open a new window" for the session restoration setting and "Separate in each window" for pinned tabs setting
2. Open a bunch of windows with a couple of tabs and set some pinned tabs in each window.
3. Quit the app
4. Open the app and verify all pinned tabs have been restored and no regular tabs have been restored

**Test restoration of per window pinned tabs when the session restoration is turned on**
1. In Settings -> General, set "Reopen all windows from last session" for the session restoration setting and "Separate in each window" for pinned tabs setting
2. Open a bunch of windows with a couple of tabs and set some pinned tabs in each window.
3. Quit the app
4. Open the app and verify all windows with regular and pinned tabs have been restored.

**Test restoration of shared pinned tabs with the various session restoration settings**
1. In Settings -> General, set "Open a new window" for the session restoration setting and "Shared across all windows" for pinned tabs setting
2. Open a bunch of windows with a couple of tabs and create some shared pinned tabs.
3. Quit the app
4. Open the app and verify shared pinned tabs have been restored correctly
5. Repeat the test with the "Reopen all windows from last session" session restoration setting and verify windows are restored with both regular and pinned tabs correctly

**Test 'Reset Pinned Tabs' when per-window pinned tabs are enabled**
1. Set the "Separate in each window" pinned tabs setting
2. Open multiple windows with some pinned tabs in each window
3. Go to Debug -> Reset Data -> Reset Pinned Tabs
4. Make sure all pinned tabs have been cleared

**Test 'Reopen last closed tab' when per-window pinned tabs are enabled**
1. Set the "Separate in each window" pinned tabs setting
2. Open multiple windows with some pinned tabs in each window
3. Close a pinned tab
4. Go to History -> Reopen Last Closed Tab
5. Verify the pinned tab has been added back
6. Close a pinned tab again
7. Switch to the other window
8. Go to History -> Reopen Last Closed Tab
9. Verify the pinned tab has been added to the new window

**Test Fire button when per-window pinned tabs are enabled**
1. Set the "Separate in each window" pinned tabs setting
2. Open a window and pin some tabs
3. Burn a pinned tab
4. Make sure the tab is still present in the window and it has been reloaded
5. Burn the current window
6. Make sure the set of pinned tabs has been preserved after burning
7. Open a couple of more windows and pin some tabs
8. Burn all data
9. Make sure all pinned tabs sets have been preserved. It means, all tabs have been closed except pinned tabs. (In case a window didn't contain any pinned tab, it's gone)

**Test migration of shared pinned tabs for existing users**
1. Execute `./macOS/clean-app.sh debug`
2. Switch to the `main` branch
4. Run the app and pin a couple of tabs
5. Quit the application
6. Switch back to the `tom/per-window-pinned-tabs` branch
7. Run the app
8. Make sure the same pinned tabs are present and they are shared across browser windows
9. Optionally, verify the pinned tabs setting is set to "Shared across all windows"

**Test the Discovery dialog**
1. With the state from the end of the previous test, pin another tab
10. Verify the app presented a discovery dialog - a pop up dialog pointing to the new pinned tabs allowing user to switch to per-window pinned tabs
11. Switch to per-window pinned tabs using the dialog
12. Verify the pinned tabs are now separate in each window

**Test back/forward list is not preserved in session state data**
1. In a pinned tab, navigate to couple of URLs to create back/forward list of websites
2. Quit the app
3. Start the app again and verify the back/forward list is empty for the pinned tab

**Test pixels**
1. Test `userPinnedTab` is fired when user pins a tab
2. Test `userUnpinnedTab` is fired when user unpins a tab
3. Test  `userSwitchedToSharedPinnedTabs` is fired when user switches to shared pinned tabs
4. Test  `userSwitchedToPerWindowPinnedTabs` is fired when user switches to per-window pinned tabs
5. Make sure `userPinnedTab` is not fired when migration is performed from shared to per-window and back

### Impact and Risks
High

title: VPN and PIR issues fix
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1205842942115003/1209654847406840/f
CC: @diegoreymendez  @THISISDINOSAUR @samsymons @miasma13 

### Description

Fix for the token issue introduced in https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/120

What happened:

**VPN:**

Different parts of the app use different ways to store and retrieve the access token. 
The `DefaultAccountManager` is used in the main app but not in the SysExt where `NetworkProtectionKeychainTokenStore` is used directly. The two classes use different keys to store the access token.
In [a recent PR](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/120), I mistakenly swapped the classes that were initialised side by side and implemented the same protocol (`SubscriptionTokenHandling`), so no error was detected at build time.

Fixes:
- In `MacPacketTunnelProvider` I restored the `tokenHandler = tokenStore`

**PIR**
The issue with PIR was only with the e2e tests, the way the token is overwritten during the tests didn't result in the SubscriptionManager thinking that the user was logged in.

Memory improvements by @samsymons see details here: https://app.asana.com/0/1193060753475688/1209661386167901

### Testing Steps
1. Subscribe to privacy pro
2. Start VPN
3. Start DBP

### Description

This PR reduces PIR E2E test memory usage, as it's likely causing issues with the runner images. The issue is related to the `awaitFulfillment` blocks in the suite, which run their block repeatedly until they either get a success or time out.

title: macOS: Freemium PIR - Add Follow-up Pixel Measurement of Cohort Subscriptions
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1206488453854252/1209643339074944

### Description
This PR implements a follow-up retroactive measurement to enable us to compare subscriptions between the control and treatment cohorts. Our metric works as follows:
* Adds a new pixel which is fired under the following conditions:
** User is in the control or treatment cohort
** User has an active PP subscription (wouldn't include users who have since cancelled)
* The pixel includes the following parameters:
** Cohort
** Days enrolled (the number of days the user has been enrolled in the experiment)
* The pixel is unique (fired once per user)

### Testing Steps
1. Launch the browser. 
2. Via the debug `Freemium` menu, select `Enroll into Experiment`
3. Filter the Xcode console by “pixel"
4. Re-launch the browser
5. Ensure the `m_mac_dbp-free_subscription_status_u` pixel **is not fired** (check the console)
6. Sign into your Privacy Pro subscription
7. Re-launch the browser
8. Ensure the `m_mac_dbp-free_subscription_status_u` pixel **is fired** (check the console), and looks like:

```
👾[Unique-Skipped] m_mac_dbp-free_subscription_status_u ["appVersion": "1.130.0", "daysEnrolled": "0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "experimentCohort": "treatment”]
```

#### What could go wrong?
Incorrect data if pixel is fired incorrectly.

body:
<!--

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1202406491309510/task/1209377843227194
### Description
- update the suggestions algorithm to match Windows implementation (Show both History record and Open tab:
 - https://github.com/duckduckgo/windows-browser/blob/ed93effed38cbdd60849629e336345a36731186f/WindowsBrowser.Autocomplete/Services/SuggestionSortAlgorithm.cs
 - https://github.com/duckduckgo/windows-browser/blob/ed93effed38cbdd60849629e336345a36731186f/WindowsBrowser.Autocomplete/Services/ScoringService.cs
- Add JSON Suggestions test scenarios: [`privacy-reference-tests`](https://github.com/duckduckgo/privacy-reference-tests/pull/142/files)
- 1st PR of the series with refactoring: https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/154

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Activate Internal User from the Debug Menu
2. Activate `autocompleteTabs` override from Debug -> Feature flag overrides menu
3. Open couple of github.com pages, couple of app.asana.com pages and a https://asana.com/resources page, settings, bookmarks, 2 new tabs
4. Switch to the New Tab, start entering `asa`: history record should be autocompleted, one app.asana.com Switch To Tab record should be right after it, asana.com/resources should be below bing results; enter `git` – same (switch to tab suggestion should be either 2nd or at the end of the list
5. Switch to app.asana.com, start entering `app.asa` - validate another app.asana.com is not suggested to switch to, history entry should be suggested;
6. Validate entering `set` suggests to switch to the Settings tab at the bottom, `book` – to the Bookmarks tab. `new` shouldn‘t suggest an open New Tab to switch to.

7. Validate Open Tabs don‘t appear in the Top Hits section

title: Improve logic for newly selected tabs after closing one
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1204006570077678/1209684411145358/f
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description
Improves the logic of how we return to a tab after closing one.

When closing a tab, the following rules will be used to find the appropriate tab to activate. Rules will be evaluated top to bottom and evaluation stops once a tab has been found:
1. If this tab has a parent (i.e. has been opened via "Open In New Tab"):
a. Try to find the next tab with the same parent tab
b. Try to find the previous tab with the same parent tab
c. Try to find the parent tab
2. Try to find the next tab that has the closing tab as it's parent
3. Try to find the previous tab that has the closing tab as it's parent
4. Try to find the previously opened tab.
5. Try to find the next tab
6. Try to find the previous tab

### Testing Steps
1. Open a site on a tab
2. To create a child tab, right tap on a link and tap ‘Open Link In New tab'
3. To create a regular/normal tab, jsut tap CMD + T or the + button in the TabBar

### Impact and Risks
Medium to low.

#### What could go wrong?
Users could be used to the old way causing confusion.

### Quality Considerations
I’ve considered different edge cases that I covered with unit tests.

### Notes to Reviewer
Nothing specific.

title: Malicious Site Protection - Attempt to prevent crashes
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1206329551987282/1209638992004951/f

### Description

This PR attempts to mitigate crashes happening for Malicious Site Protection by:

1. Use `fatalError` if ApplicationSupportDirectory is unavailable when the DataManager is initialised. This is a slight improvement as the `fatalError` message should be available in the crash logs. [fc3b11f](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/commit/fc3b11ff388d280c2c656a58f70c4abd5744c3c9)

2. Ensure Background Tasks identifiers are registered only once. [9914e8a](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/commit/9914e8a23ce2c8dfbbd8e8206833223e357619ad)

3. Prevent starting new dataset updates if there are already requests in flight. [603ec57](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/commit/603ec576f3f6a7dc0589ba0b70df0826928e8c64)

4. Prevent starting/stopping update tasks multiple times if the user continuously switches the toggle flag in the settings by adding a debounce. [74a20d3](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/commit/74a20d3391064122f658e1569cd3d041d9d36027)

5. Serialise the update of datasets when `updateData` is called [514b260](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/258/commits/514b260b2ce82ff338101483b16664238651fd35) 

### Testing Steps
1. Ensure CI is green
2. Smoke test Malicious Site Protection feature:
2.1 Delete the App.
2.2 Ensure datasets are fetched when the app launches
2.3 Ensure [phishing](http://privacy-test-pages.site/security/badware/phishing.html), [malware](http://privacy-test-pages.site/security/badware/malware.html), and [scam](http://privacy-test-pages.site/security/badware/scam.html) (if the feature is enabled)websites are intercepted and blocked

### Impact and Risks
High:  Cold affect or break a core flow

### Quality Considerations
While the new approach reduces the risk of data races by keeping dataset modifications within the actor's isolation, it introduces a small performance tradeoff. Indeed, the actor remains locked during dataset changes, potentially reducing concurrent access in scenarios where large number of objects need to be inserted, updated, or deleted.

### Notes to Reviewer
I was unable to reproduce the crashes. These changes attempt to address potential root causes, such asaces in dataset operations and system-triggered terminations, such as when possible data or background tasks with the same identifiers are registered more than once.

The crashes appear in Sentry with a SIGKILL 0 signature, indicating that the OS terminated the process. Example crash report:

```
Application Specific Information:
SIGKILL 0
```
These reports lack the termination reason that would typically help identify the underlying cause, as described in [Apple's documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/sigkill). I’m unsure if this is an issue with Apple's reporting or with how we're integrating with Sentry.
 
@mallexxx I’ve implemented the changes we discussed to make the dataset changes as single operation.
@bwaresiak If you could please take a look at the PR that would be great.
@SabrinaTardio could you just quickly check I didn’t affect your scam work since I had some merge conflicts?

title: AuthV2 - Feature flag for iOS and macOS
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1205842942115003/1209170372758740/f
CC: @miasma13 @diegoreymendez 

### Description

- All Subscription Auth V1 and V2 initialisations are now behind a disabled development feature flag that can be enabled via the debug menu
- Migration from V1 to V2 and rollback from V2 to V1 supported and tested

### Testing Steps

For both iOS and macOS

1. Double check the feature flag is disabled (Debug > Feature Flag Overrides > privacyProAuthV2)
2. Subscribe to Privacy Pro
3. Enable VPN
4. Enable `privacyProAuthV2` feature flag (it enables AuthV2)
5. Kill the app
6. Restart the app, The VPN should be disconnected but can be restarted straight away.
7. Disable `privacyProAuthV2` feature flag (it disables AuthV2 and roll backs to V1)
8. Kill the app
9. Restart the app, The VPN should be disconnected but can be restarted straight away.

### Impact and Risks

High: we could break the VPN and the subscription UX

#### What could go wrong?
- The VPN could not restart automatically after a migration from V1 to V2 or vice versa, that's ok, but if started manually everything should work as usual

title: Support dynamic favicons in the macOS browser
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209728950138483/f

### Description:
This change adds support for dynamic favicons, i.e. it handles changes to the favicon
made by the website asynchronously after load.
Old favicons user script was replaced with a content-isolated subfeature from C-S-S.
Favicons handling for a Tab was moved to a dedicated Tab Extension.
Minor updates to FaviconsManager were made to simplify the API.

### Testing Steps
See [this task](https://app.asana.com/0/72649045549333/1209718156754292) for the list of test websites and websites known to not work fine.
1. Open https://rpsthecoder.github.io/favicon-canvas-loader/ to see how dynamic favicons work.
2. Open https://privacy-test-pages.site/features/favicon/favicon_js/index.html for a more controllable example.
3. Click "Set default now”. Open History from Main Menu and verify that the favicon matches the history entry for this website.
4. Click “Set override now”. Open History from Main Menu and verify that the history entry displays an overridden favicon.
    * Note that you can test the same with History View (cmd+y) but it being a website causes some caching to happen which may present the outdated favicon until the tab is closed and reopened.
5. Repeat the same test (steps 3-4) with Bookmarks Manager and verify that it displays the most recently used favicon.

### Impact and Risks
Low: The only real change (not counting the tab extension) is to how frequently favicons may be reported by a website.

### Quality Considerations
As far as performance is concerned, I’ve tested https://rpsthecoder.github.io/favicon-canvas-loader/ on a 2015 MacBook Air with Big Sur where it worked perfectly fine, with no CPU spikes or beach-balling. More frequent updates than that are throttled on the C-S-S end (the native app won’t receive updates more frequently).

(instead of cascading from that frame that resulted in shifting the window to the right and down).

### Testing Steps
1. Launch the app and, to simplify testing, put the window in the upper-left corner of the screen.
2. Burn all data. Verify that the new window is placed in the exact same frame in the upper-left corner of the screen.
3. Repeat the same with burning “current window”.
4. Repeat the same with burning “current tab” when you only have 1 tab.
5. Open multiple windows and burn all data. Verify that the new window is placed in the exact same frame as the window you’ve initiated burning from.

### Impact and Risks
Low

#### What could go wrong?
Nothing really – we’re assigning an optional dropping point to new window function. If non-nil, it represents previous window frame, if nil it does nothing (like currently).

title: iOS: Privacy Pro Onboarding Promotion - Ensure Correct Keyboard Behavior
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209738106994913

### Description
This PR makes changes to ensure we display/dismiss the keyboard as expected when displaying/dismissing the Privacy Pro Onboarding Promotion. See test cases below.

### Test Prerequisites
1. Force a treatment cohort by adding `return .treatment` as the first line of the `getCohortIfEnabled` method in `OnboardingPrivacyProPromoExperiment`

### Testing Steps
#### Test Case 1 ####
1. Fresh install the app on a physical device
2. Launch and proceed to the ‘High Five’ last onboarding step
3. Tap ‘High Five’ to display the PP promotion
4. Ensure the Keyboard is dismissed
5. Tap ‘Learn More'
6. Ensure the keyboard remains dismissed the the PP paywall is opened

#### Test Case 2 ####
1. Fresh install the app on a physical device
2. Launch and proceed to the ‘High Five’ last onboarding step
3. Tap ‘High Five’ to display the PP promotion
4. Ensure the Keyboard is dismissed
5. Tap ’Skip'
6. Ensure the omnibar becomes focused and the keyboard is displayed

#### Test Case 3 ####
1. Fresh install the app on a physical device
2. Launch and proceed to the ‘High Five’ last onboarding step
3. Dismiss the keyboard by tapping the back arrow in the omnibar
4. Ensure the Keyboard is dismissed
5. Open a new tab
6. Ensure the PP promotion is displayed and the keyboard remains dismissed

### Impact and Risks
Medium: If this did not work as expected, existing omnibar and keyboard behavior could be impacted.

#### What could go wrong?
The omnibar and keyboard might not behave as expected (i.e not be focused on a new tab opening)

title: [iOS][Onboarding] Release Add To Dock intro to all users and remove atb from pixels
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1206329551987282/1209746049470520/f

### Description

This PR addresses:
1. Removes experiment for Add to Dock and release winner (Add to Dock prompted early in the onboarding to all users) 
2. Removes atb from onboarding pixels.
3. Clean up the logic of the OnboardingIntroViewModel.

### Testing Steps - Onboarding Flow

**Scenario 1 - Present Add to Dock from linear onboarding - iPhone** ✅ 
1. Add return `true` in `HomeRowReminder` -> `func showNow() -> Bool` at line 50
2. Ensure that Add to Dock Dax dialog is presented after "Set Default Browser" dialog.
3. Ensure that the Add To Dock Banner at the top of the web view is not presented after tapping on the first suggested search.
4. Continue with the flow and ensure that the Add to Dock promo is not presented in the final contextual dialog.
5. Repeat the test and ensure the “Show me how” button in the Add to Dock promo dialog shows the video tutorial.
6. Background and foreground the app while the video is playing and ensure the video resumes playing.
7. Ensure the onboarding flow continues when tapping the “Got It” button.

**Scenario 2 - Does Mot Present Add to Dock from linear onboarding - iPad** ✅ 
1. Add return `true` in `HomeRowReminder` -> `func showNow() -> Bool` at line 50
2. Ensure Add to Dock screen is not presented for iPad users in the onboarding flow.
3. Ensure that the Add to Dock banner appears after the first search (since we return true)

### Testing Steps - Privacy Pro Experiment

**Test Prerequisites**

Force a treatment cohort by adding return .treatment as the first line of the `getCohortIfEnabled` method in `OnboardingPrivacyProPromoExperiment`

**Testing Steps**

**Test Case 1** ✅ 

1. Fresh install the app on a physical device
2. Launch and proceed to the ‘High Five’ last onboarding step
3. Tap ‘High Five’ to display the PP promotion
4. Ensure the Keyboard is dismissed
5. Tap ‘Learn More'
6. Ensure the keyboard remains dismissed the the PP paywall is opened

**Test Case 2** ✅ 

1. Fresh install the app on a physical device
2. Launch and proceed to the ‘High Five’ last onboarding step
3. Tap ‘High Five’ to display the PP promotion
4. Ensure the Keyboard is dismissed
5. Tap ’Skip'
6. Ensure the omnibar becomes focused and the keyboard is displayed

**Test Case 3** ✅ 

1. Fresh install the app on a physical device
2. Launch and proceed to the ‘High Five’ last onboarding step
3. Dismiss the keyboard by tapping the back arrow in the omnibar
4. Ensure the Keyboard is dismissed
5. Open a new tab
6. Ensure the PP promotion is displayed and the keyboard remains dismissed

- [ ] Enable `exchangeKeysToSyncWithAnotherDevice` FF on all devices.

title: Improved subscription activation flow
body:
**Task/Issue URL:** https://app.asana.com/0/1200019156869587/1208277374981161/f
CC: @federicocappelli 

### Description
Redesigned Privacy Pro activation experience on iOS and macOS, both when: activating a subscription bought on another device, and having subscription activated on another device.

**Scope of changes:**
- When unsubscribed: "I Have a Subscription" flow to activate subscription on this device
- When subscribed: "Add to Device" flow to add email and activate subscription on another device 

**Figma:**
- [Design - Streamline UX of Subscription Activation](https://www.figma.com/design/u0kcBkqincD1hBMfHk03z2/Streamline-UX-of-Subscription-Activation?node-id=1149-47466&t=52BeSwALEhdKtwI6-1)
- [Flowmap - Streamline UX of Subscription Activation](https://www.figma.com/design/u0kcBkqincD1hBMfHk03z2/Streamline-UX-of-Subscription-Activation?node-id=1884-59730)

### Testing Steps
**To be tested on iOS and macOS**
1. **Activate on this device** 
**Before:** Have an active Privacy Pro subscription with added email address. Sign out from the subscription on the device.
**Test:** When signed out restore subscription via new activation flow under "I Have a Subscription" using email address.

2. **Activate on this device (launched from purchase page)** 
**Before:** Have an active Privacy Pro subscription with added email address. Sign out from the subscription on the device.
**Test:** When signed out restore subscription via purchase page footer link: "I Have a Subscription" using email address. Verify if welcome page buttons work as expected and the back button navigates back to main settings screen.

2. **Add email and add to another device** 
**Before:** Have an active Privacy Pro subscription without an email address on the device.
**Test:** Open subscription settings use new activation flow under "Add to device" to add email address to subscription and follow guide to activate in on another device.

3. **Add to another device when email already connected** 
**Before:** Have an active Privacy Pro subscription with an email address connected on the device.
**Test:** Open subscription settings use new activation flow under "Add to device" to activate subscription on another device. The steps to add email address should be skipped.

4. **Editing/deleting email** 
**Before:** Have an active Privacy Pro subscription with an email address connected on the device.
**Test:** Open subscription settings. Edit/delete email functionality flow should be available unchanged as a separate option next to "Add to Device" button.

5. **Verify adding email in after-purchase flow**
**Before:** Sign out from the subscription from the device. In case of App Store purchase ensure that subscription from the current Apple Account did not have an email attached.
**Test:** Purchase subscription. When complete from the "Welcome" page select first option allowing you to link email address to your subscription.

**To be tested on iOS only:**
- Verify if add email and new activation flows have correctly implemented navigation, for validation please use scenarios described in: https://app.asana.com/0/1200019156869587/1209784536034639/f

**Additional checks**
1. **Email / Apple Account modal is shown for macOS App Store build**
**Before:** Use macOS app enabled for App Store purchase and sign out from any subscription.
**Test:** Open settings. Selecting "I Have a Subscription" should show native modal with selection for activation using Email or Apple Account.

2. **Email / Apple Account modal is not shown for macOS Stripe build** 
**Before:** Use macOS app enabled for Stripe purchase and sign out from any subscription.
**Test:** Open settings. Selecting "I Have a Subscription" should not show the modal but launch the new activation flow directly.


### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
Subscription activation flow for both restoring and activating on another device may be broken.

body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209254337758531

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209325145462547
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/0/481882893211075/1209208071633607
CC: @vkraucunas @miasma13 

### Description

New Native <> Web messages for AuthV2 implemented in iOS and macOS

### Testing Steps

## 0: Setup Browser for Testing
- Be signed in as an internal user: https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207106679326661
- Enable AuthV2 by overriding the `privacyProAuthV2` flag from Debug > FeatureFlag Override
- Restart the app (the override is persistent)
- Point browser at staging assets: Debug > Subscription > Environment > Staging
- Debug > Subscription > Custom Base Subscription URL, enter `https://vkraucunas.duckduckgo.com/subscriptions`
  - By doing this, you may not need to do much pasting of the URLs after being logged in because launching the Manage view via Subscription Settings will send you to the correct place, but I always check anyway. 

## 1: Create Account 1 & Add email (App Store)
- Page: https://vkraucunas.duck.co/subscriptions
- Pick a subscription and complete a transaction on App Store
- When you land at `/subscriptions/welcome`, select the “Add Privacy Pro to your devices via an email” 
- Add an email `/subscriptions/add-email`
- Receive the OTP and enter it
- See success screen, click Done

## 2: Sign out
- Debug > Subscription > Remove Subscription from this Device

## 3: Create Account 2 (Stripe)
- Page: https://vkraucunas.duck.co/subscriptions
- Pick a subscription and complete a transaction on Stripe
  - Use a different email than round 1. 
- When you land at `/subscriptions/welcome`, don’t add an email

## 4: Sign out
- Debug > Subscription > Remove Subscription from this Device

## 5: Login/activate an account with assigned email on account
- Page: https://vkraucunas.duck.co/subscriptions/activate
- Enter the email you entered for Create Account 1
- Receive the OTP and enter it
- See success screen, click Done

## 6: Sign out
- Debug > Subscription > Remove Subscription from this Device

## 7: Login via `/activation-flow`
- Page: https://vkraucunas.duck.co/subscriptions/activation-flow/this-device/activate-by-email
- Enter the email used for Create Account 2
- Receive the OTP and enter it. or fire another with the “Resend Passphrase” btn
- See success screen, click Done

## 8: Add email via `/activation-flow`
- Page: https://vkraucunas.duck.co/subscriptions/activation-flow/another-device/add-email
- Start with account signed in
- Enter an email address
- Receive the OTP and enter it. or fire another with the “Resend Passphrase” btn
- See success screen, click Done

## 9: Edit email via `/manage` while logged in
- Open Subscriptions Settings via the browser menu, select Edit under Activate on Other Devices
- Page: https://vkraucunas.duck.co/subscriptions/manage
- Start with an account logged in and with email added to it
- Select the pencil btn for edit
- Enter a new and exciting email address
- Receive the OTP and enter it. or fire another with the “Resend Passphrase” btn
- See success screen, see the new email in Subscription Settings / on the “see subscription” from the debug menu

## 10: Remove email via `/manage` while logged in
- Page: https://vkraucunas.duck.co/subscriptions/manage
- Start with an account logged in and email on file with it
- Select the trash can, accept at the additional prompt
- See success screen, see the empty email in Subscription Settings / on the “see subscription” from the debug menu

## 11: Add email via `/add-email` while logged in
- Open Subscriptions Settings via the browser menu, select Add Email under Activate on Other Devices
- Page: https://vkraucunas.duck.co/subscriptions/add-email
- Enter an email 
- Receive the OTP and enter it. or fire another with the “Resend Passphrase” btn
- See success screen, see the new email in Subscription Settings / on the “see subscription” from the debug menu

## 12: Visit IDTR 
- Launch IDTR however is appropriate for the environment 
- Page: https://vkraucunas.duck.co/identity-theft-restoration

### Description
This change fixes two things:
- With the previous change, I introduced a bug in which if the closed tab was not active, we applied the logic as if it was active, which was wrong and unintentional.
- The rule of returning to the previous active tab was missing some logic. On Windows, the previously active tab is only remembered until the user moves to an existing tab or creates new tabs.

### Testing Steps

**Testing steps of the first bug**
1. Open some site like Wikipedia, and open some links from there using CMD + Tap
2. Open a new tab and keep that tab selected
3. Right tap one of the child tabs and close it
4. The active tab should be the new tab and no other sibiling or parent of the closed tab should be selected

**Test we return to the previous active tab**
1. Open five tabs (no related)
2. Select the first tab
3. Use CMD + T or tapping the + in the tab bar to open a new tab
4. Close that tab
5. The first tab should be selected

**Test we do not return to the previous active tab if another tab was selected**
1. Open five tabs (no related)
2. Select the first tab
3. Use CMD + T or tapping the + in the tab bar to open a new tab
4. Select tab number 5 (the one before the recently opened)
5. Go back to the last tab and close it
6. Tab number 5 should be selected instead of the first tab

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
The scenario disrupts other flows when closing tabs.

### Quality Considerations
I’ve added unit tests and UI tests to cover this new scenarios.

### Notes to Reviewer
Do as much test as you can for your user flows.

title: [iOS]Add new pixels to measure app launches
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1209593812414962 ### Description This PR adds new pixels to measure: 1. When the app is launched by tapping an external link (cold start and resume from backround) 2 When the app is launched by sharing a link/search via the share extension. (cold start and resume from background) **NOTE** I will open the Privacy Triage once the review has been approved to avoid creating extra works for Privacy team if we decide to change pixels name or add more of them. Hence, the `DO NOT MERGE` label. **Privacy Triage** [Privacy Triage Approved](https://app.asana.com/0/69071770703008/1209811367393595/f) ### Testing Steps **Scenario 1 - Measure App launched by external link (cold start)** ✅ 1. Ensure to select `iOS Browser` scheme and change app launch to “Wait for executable to be launched” in `Edit Scheme` -> `Run` -> `Info`. 2. Ensure DDG is set as default browser in system settings. 3. Build and run the app. (Bear in mind the App won’t launch as usual but it will wait for an event to happen). 4. Save a link in Notes app, e.g https://www.apple.com. 5. Tap on the link just added in Notes. 6. The App will launch. 7. Ensure that `m.app-launch.tapped-external-link` pixel fires. 8. Repeat the test using an ‘http’ URL. **Scenario 2 - Measure App launched by external link (resume from background)** ✅ 1. Ensure DDG is set as default browser in system settings. 2. Launch the App. 3. Background the App. 4. Save a link in Notes app, e.g https://www.apple.com. 5. Tap on the link just added in Notes. 6. Ensure that the app comes to foreground and `m.app-launch.tapped-external-link` pixel fires. 7. Repeat the test using an ‘http’ URL. **Scenario 3 - Measure App launched by share extension (cold start)** ✅ 1. Ensure to select `iOS Browser` scheme and change app launch to “Wait for executable to be launched” in `Edit Scheme` -> `Run` -> `Info`. 2. Build and run the app. (Bear in mind the App won’t launch as usual but it will wait for an event to happen). 3. Open a link in Safari, e.g https://www.apple.com. 4. Press the share button -> More -> Select DuckDuckGo app. 5. The App will launch. 7. Ensure that `m.app-launch.shared-link` pixel fires. **Scenario 4 - Measure App launched by share extension (resume from background)** ✅ 1. Launch the app. 2. Put the app in background. 2. Open a link in Safari, e.g https://www.apple.com. 3. Press the share button -> More -> Select DuckDuckGo app. 4. Ensure that the app comes to foreground and `m.app-launch.shared-link` pixel fires. ### Impact and Risks Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features. #### What could go wrong? Possibility of inaccurate measurements if the implementation is incorrect. ### Quality Considerations There are other deep link schemes that we could measure. We can add them in the future if we’re interested in those. ### Notes to Reviewer I will open the Privacy Triage once the review has been approved to avoid creating extra works for Privacy team if we decide to change pixels name or add more of them. — ###### Internal references: [Definition of Done](https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207634633537039/f) | [Engineering Expectations](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/199064865822552) | [Tech Design Template](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/184709971311943)

title: Fixes an issue where exclude local networks isn't working well.
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1207603085593419/task/1210534790670685?focus=true

### Description

Fixes two issues:
- No longer adding allowed IPs to included ranges because that was including "0.0.0.0".
- The [link-local range is being excluded](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/bf3f55294e8b7c78c162efe242a22288ef05b381/BrowserServicesKit/Sources/NetworkProtection/Routing/VPNRoutingRange.swift#L25), but [also included in ](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/bf3f55294e8b7c78c162efe242a22288ef05b381/BrowserServicesKit/Sources/NetworkProtection/Routing/VPNRoutingRange.swift#L61)[publicNetworkRange](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/bf3f55294e8b7c78c162efe242a22288ef05b381/BrowserServicesKit/Sources/NetworkProtection/Routing/VPNRoutingRange.swift#L61)[ by range ](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/bf3f55294e8b7c78c162efe242a22288ef05b381/BrowserServicesKit/Sources/NetworkProtection/Routing/VPNRoutingRange.swift#L61)[168.0.0.0/6](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/bf3f55294e8b7c78c162efe242a22288ef05b381/BrowserServicesKit/Sources/NetworkProtection/Routing/VPNRoutingRange.swift#L61) - likely creating a conflict in our configuration.  This is an error as this range should be always excluded.

### Testing Steps

- Test iOS and macOS.
- Test TunnelCrack
- Test TunnelVision
- While pinging something on the local network toggle "exclude local networks".  Make sure the ping fails and succeeds as appropriate.

### Impact and Risks

Medium.

Routing changes can be tricky if done wrong.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1201899738287924/1209769490544821/f

### Description
This change reworks FaviconManaging, FaviconImageCaching and FaviconReferenceCaching APIs
to move MainActor requirement from protocols and into individual functions/properties, to allow
for initializing in non-isolated contexts.
It also updates some APIs to async and fixes MainActor requirements across the codebase, limiting
the number of warnings.
FaviconManager.shared was removed and replaced with an instance owned by App Delegate
and instantiated there. Nonisolated and MainActor(unsafe) directives were removed where possible.

### Testing Steps
Smoke test favicons:
* Open multiple tabs at once (e.g. from the bookmarks bar or bookmarks manager) and verify that all tabs and their favicons load fine and that no crashing happens.
* Verify that favicons are properly cached and retrieved from cache.
* Verify that favicons are correctly restored during state restoration.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Favicons refactoring may break user flows and lead to occasional crashes.

### Quality Considerations
Favicons operations were all happening on the main thread already before this change so there should be no
performance impact here.

### Notes to Reviewer
I’ve been testing this change for almost a week now and am feeling pretty confident about it, but I’d appreciate a critical look. Worst case we won’t merge it, but hopefully the changes are reasonable.
