title: [iOS] Fix webview deallocation check
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1206329551987282/1209482845377256/f

### Description

`WebDuckPlayerNavigationHandler`.`setupYoutubeNavigationRequestObserver` combine closure strongly retains the instance of WKWebView. 

In some scenarios (not easily reproducible) the `DeallocationCheckAction` `assert` function fires as the WebView is not deallocated. 

I found that the issue started appearing in commit `112c7fa184f04178bfc7f75e321dbff942d7acff DuckPlayer: 31. PoC: Open Player Links in Youtube (#3919)`

Capturing weakly the webview seems to fix the issue.

### Testing Steps

1. Remove the webview from the capture list in `setupYoutubeNavigationRequestObserver`
1. Do a SERP (e.g search for baby ducklings).
2. For all the results shown 
3. Long press.
4. Tap on Open Tab in Background
5. Keep doing it till the `DeallocationCheckAction` assertion fires.
6. Re-add the webview in the capture list in `setupYoutubeNavigationRequestObserver`.
7. Repeat from Step 1.
8. Ensure that the `DeallocationCheckAction` assertion does not fire.

### Impact and Risks
Low

---

**Copilot summary:**

This pull request introduces significant changes to the `DataBrokerProtectionCore` module, focusing on improving job management, refactoring dependencies, and replacing existing job runner implementations with a new structure. The most notable changes include renaming properties in `BrokerProfileQueryData`, removing legacy job runner classes, and introducing a new `BrokerProfileJob` class and its dependencies.

### Refactoring and Property Updates:
* Renamed `operationsData` to `jobsData` in `BrokerProfileQueryData` to better reflect its purpose. Updated related logic to use the new property name. (`BrokerProfileQueryData.swift`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6b5efce4da4b80c6607a61d351d033b065a6c2983531df37e3f266a4e6e68176L28-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6b5efce4da4b80c6607a61d351d033b065a6c2983531df37e3f266a4e6e68176L37-R37)

### Removal of Legacy Implementations:
* Removed the `DataBrokerOperationsCreator` class, which previously handled the creation of operations for data brokers. (`DataBrokerOperationsCreator.swift`, [SharedPackages/DataBrokerProtectionCore/Sources/DataBrokerProtectionCore/OperationQueueManaging/DataBrokerOperationsCreator.swiftL1-L62](diffhunk://#diff-9453abcfc6a73860260f26494d0183831119cc9d3fae384eca88207779cc4921L1-L62))
* Removed the `DataBrokerJobRunner` and `DataBrokerJobRunnerProvider` classes, which were responsible for running and providing job runners. (`DataBrokerJobRunner.swift`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-46018afbbf3f0a54002d1e043335cd29d2b51ac0d1674697273629e7e41c8e3cL1-L97); `DataBrokerJobRunnerProvider.swift`, [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-af91a68bfdfcfaefb22bea7b262d3111d9f572967aabba8ea16b338607f733edL1-L48)

### Introduction of New Job Management:
* Added the `BrokerProfileJob` class, which provides a more modular and extensible approach to managing broker jobs. This class supports asynchronous execution, prioritization, and filtering of jobs based on type and priority date. (`BrokerProfileJob.swift`, [SharedPackages/DataBrokerProtectionCore/Sources/DataBrokerProtectionCore/Operations/BrokerProfileJob.swiftR1-R250](diffhunk://#diff-31701bdc425efb56f500a78d7d5e15b399f590222f9dc4898960b1416cb005a8R1-R250))

### Dependency Injection Enhancements:
* Introduced the `BrokerProfileJobDependencies` structure, which centralizes the dependencies required for job execution, such as database access, privacy configurations, and services. This replaces the previous approach of scattered dependency management. (`BrokerProfileJobDependencies.swift`, [SharedPackages/DataBrokerProtectionCore/Sources/DataBrokerProtectionCore/Operations/BrokerProfileJobDependencies.swiftR1-R112](diffhunk://#diff-838b8f71b7a8e9b01c43f2664093bcd6ffda52388317088976f9b4d17530bdbeR1-R112)) 

These changes improve the maintainability and scalability of the job management system by consolidating logic, enhancing dependency injection, and removing outdated implementations.

title: icons.duckduckgo.com light and dark themes
body:
Thank you very much for your service which provides websites favicons.
It was extremely useful for me in building my [Tab Finder Safari Extension](https://github.com/kopyl/safari-tab-switcher) (extension for switching between tabs), because there is no way to fetch a favicon with a Safari API sadly :(

There are a few similar APIs, but yours turned out to be the fastest and most reliable.

But similar to all of the others, it has one flaw – it can't fetch icons in different scheme – light or dark.

Do you think it's possible to implement?
Do you have your service open sourced? If so, maybe I can have a look and help with implementing it.

5. Open a new window and see the extension icon present in the navigation bar

title: Support for staging App Store storefront region override on iOS
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/414709148257752/task/1209856405160605?focus=true
cc: @federicocappelli 

### Description
Similar to how it is done on macOS implement debug menu option for setting a fixed storefront region override that can be used during testing. Set override region is used instead of getting value via StoreKit API to determine available subscription products for purchase.
override value can be set to one of three values: "None", "USA", "Rest of World"
override is only used when internal user mode is enabled and using staging environment

Implementation for using override is already in place (used by macOS), we miss debug menu option to set the value and configuration to read and pass the current override value to the StorePurchaseManager. 

⚠️ Change of override may require app restart to take effect. 

### Testing Steps (iOS)
Ensure you are using Alpha build for testing and test on real device

**When:**
- Internal user mode is enabled
- subscription environment is set to staging
- region override is set to "None" 

**Then:** 
- Purchase page shows products (description on the page, purchase options in the footer and matching ToS) for the current Apple IDs region (or one shown in the debug menu)

---

**When:**
- Internal user mode is enabled
- subscription environment is set to staging
- region override is set to "USA" 

**Then:** 
- Purchase page shows products (description on the page, purchase options in the footer and matching ToS) for the US region
- After purchase user is granted 3 US Privacy Pro entitlements (VPN, PIR, ITR) and its features are listed in Settings
 
---

**When:**
- Internal user mode is enabled
- subscription environment is set to staging
- region override is set to "Rest of World"

**Then:** 
- Purchase page shows products (description on the page, purchase options in the footer and matching ToS) for the US region
- After purchase user is granted 2 Rest of World Privacy Pro entitlements (VPN, ITR) and its features are listed in Settings

---

**When:**
- Internal user mode is disabled
- subscription environment is set to staging
- region override is set to "USA" or "Rest of World" 

**Then:** 
- Override is not applied and purchase page shows products (description on the page, purchase options in the footer and matching ToS) for the current Apple IDs region (or one shown in the debug menu)

---

**When:**
- Internal user mode is enabled
- subscription environment is set to production
- region override is set to "USA" or "Rest of World" 

**Then:** 
- Override is not applied and purchase page shows products (description on the page, purchase options in the footer and matching ToS) for the current Apple IDs region (or one shown in the debug menu)


### Impact and Risks
None: Internal tooling, documentation

#### What could go wrong?
Little to no risks, region override is only available in the debug menu and its application is guarded by internal user mode and staging environment.
Also implementation to apply the logic is already present as being already used on macOS.

---

title: [iOS] Onboarding - Add Skip Option for Returning Users
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1206329551987282/1209816694983045/f
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

This PR enables returning users to skip the onboarding flow.

### Testing Steps

**Scenario 1 - Returning Users - Start Onboarding Flow**
1. Ensure `isNewUser` returns `false` in `OnboardingManager.swift`
2. Launch the App and wait for the onboarding intro dialog to appear.
3. Ensure the “I’ve been here before" button is visible”.
4. Tap the “Let’s do it button”
5. Ensure the user can complete the onboarding flow and that the Dax Dialogs are prompted when browsing. 

**Scenario 2 - Returning Users - Skip Onboarding Flow and then Resume it**
1. Ensure `isNewUser` returns `false` in `OnboardingManager.swift`
2. Launch the App and wait for the onboarding intro dialog to appear.
3. Ensure the “I’ve been here before" button is visible”.
4. Tap the “I’ve been here before” button.
5. Wait for the confirmation dialog to appear.
6. Tap the “Show Tutorial” button.
7. Ensure the onboarding resume from the browser comparison chart and that the Dax Dialogs are prompted when browsing. 

**Scenario 3 - Returning Users - Skip Onboarding Flow and Confirm Skip flow**
1. Ensure `isNewUser` returns `false` in `OnboardingManager.swift`
2. Launch the App and wait for the onboarding intro dialog to appear.
3. Ensure the “I’ve been here before" button is visible”.
4. Tap the “I’ve been here before” button.
5. Wait for the confirmation dialog to appear.
6. Tap the “Start Browsing” button.
7. Ensure the onboarding is dismissed and the Dax Dialogs are NOT prompted when browsing.

**Scenario 2 - New Users**
1. Ensure `isNewUser` returns `true` in `OnboardingManager.swift`.
2. Launch the App and wait for the onboarding intro dialog to appear.
3. Ensure the “I’ve been here before" button is NOT visible”.
4. Smoke test the onboarding flow and ensure the Dax Dialogs are prompted when browsing.

**Scenario 3 - Pixels**
1. Ensure `isNewUser` returns `true` in `OnboardingManager.swift`.
2. Launch the App and wait for the onboarding intro dialog to appear.
3. Tap the “I’ve been here before” button.
4. Ensure that the `m_preonboarding_skip-onboarding-pressed` pixel is fired.
5. Tap the “Start browsing” button.
6. Ensure that the 'm_preonboarding_confirm-skip-onboarding-pressed’ pixel is fired.
7. Repeat the test, tap the “Show Tutorial” button and ensure that ‘m_preonboarding_resume-onboarding-pressed’ pixel is fired.

Ensure that 'm_preonboarding_resume-onboarding-pressed’ is not fired when tapping the “Let’s do it button"

### Impact and Risks
What's the impact on users if something goes wrong?
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
- Wrong events reported.
- Returning users not able to skip the onboarding flow.

### Quality Considerations
- What monitoring have you added?
Pixels to measure the percentage of returning users skipping the onboarding flow.

### Notes to Reviewer
Please smoke test the whole onboarding flow.

title: Support opening links from New Tab Page using middle mouse button
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1201048563534612/1209842499332909/f

### Description
This change unifies links opening logic between Recent Activity and Favorites widget and adds support
for middle mouse button.

### Testing Steps
1. Go to _Main Menu -> Debug -> New Tab Page -> Mode -> Recent Activity_ to enable Recent Activity.
2. Have some favorites too.
3. Also have a mouse with at least 3 buttons.
4. Click a favorite or link in a Recent Activity and verify the following:
5. When clicked with a middle mouse button opens a new background tab.
6. When clicked with a middle mouse button + Shift opens a new foreground tab.
5. When clicked with a left mouse button opens it in a current tab.
7. When clicked a left mouse button + Shift opens it in a current tab.
8. When clicked with a left mouse button + cmd opens it a new background tab.
9. When clicked with a left mouse button + cmd + option opens it a new window.


### Impact and Risks
Low

### Quality Considerations
I updated tests, also de-duplicated some code so it’s easier to maintain going forward.

### Notes to Reviewer
The actual change here is that middle mouse button would previously open a link in a current tab, and the change updates it to open in a new background tab (or foreground, when Shift is pressed). The rest of the testing steps are there for completeness ;)

title: improvements in subscription with AuthV2 resiliency
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1209974732411306
CC: @miasma13 

### Description

This fixes a bug I noticed in iOS that causes a couple of issues when the device is connected to a wifi with 100% packet loss, for example, a wifi with a captive portal before authentication.

How to reproduce the bugs:
- Start the app
- Enable AuthV2 feature flag
- Kill the app
- Start the app and subscribe/restore the subscription
- Enable 100% packet loss in the iOS network link conditioner
- Kill the app
- Start the app
- Bug #1: The app needs a long time to start (60s, the API request timeout), this was due to a blocking semaphore in the token provider
- Bug #2: remove the subscription from settings: nothing happens for 60s, the logout API call was blocking the operation.

Fixes:
- iOS token provider is now async; the synchronous code has been moved.
- The logout now runs the logout API call in a Task

### Known bugs

Both with AuthV1 and V2, when the app is opened for the first time without an internet connection, the subscription setting is not displayed.

### Testing Steps

1. Test the iOS app's standard operations while enabling 100% packet loss in the iOS network link conditioner
2. Test the macOS app's standard operations while enabling 100% packet loss in the iOS network link conditioner

title: Add TabCrashRecoveryExtension and a feature flag for tab crash recovery
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1209977265286174?focus=true ### Description This change moves tab crash handling to a dedicated extension that responds to webContentProcessDidTerminate. It also introduces a feature flag for the new handling of tab crashes. The feature flag is disabled by default. ### Testing Steps **Current behavior – non-internal user** 1. Remove internal user state 2. Open some website with a known URL (example.com is fine) 3. Open Activity Monitor.app and search for example.com. You should see 1 result. 4. Quit the process from Activity Monitor (X button) 5. Verify that the tab presents the error. 6. Reload the page and repeat steps 3-5. **Current behavior – internal user** 1. Set internal user state 2. Open some website with a known URL (example.com is fine) 3. Open Activity Monitor.app and search for example.com. 4. Quit the process from Activity Monitor (X button) 5. Verify that the tab reloads example.com. 6. Reload the page and repeat steps 3-5. **New behavior** 1. Set internal user state 2. Enable tabCrashRecovery feature flag 3. Open some website with a known URL (example.com is fine) 4. Open Activity Monitor.app and search for example.com. 5. Quit the process from Activity Monitor (X button) 6. Verify that the tab reloads example.com. 7. Wait for more than 5 seconds and reload the page. Repeat steps 3-6 (the tab reloads). 8. Quit the process again and quickly quit it one more time. If you were faster than 5s, you would see the error page. Edit `TabCrashRecoveryExtension.Const.crashLoopInterval` to a value larger than 5 to help with testing. ### Impact and Risks Low #### What could go wrong? Not much, the tab extensions framework is stable and battle-tested and I consulted with Alex when implementing this change :) ### Quality Considerations I’m not adding unit tests because I expect the solution to evolve. Existing solution didn’t have unit tests either, but I’ll add unit tests in a further PR. ### Notes to Reviewer N/A --- ###### Internal references: [Definition of Done](https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207634633537039/f) | [Engineering Expectations](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/199064865822552) | [Tech Design Template](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/184709971311943)

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206329551987282/task/1208837629360126?focus=true

### Description

Re-enable DaxDialogs factory tests that were flaky. 

**Background:**

Some of these tests rely on SwiftUI’s `onAppear` being triggered in order to assert certain conditions.
For onAppear to be called, the view must be part of a view hierarchy attached to a window. Simply creating a `UIHostingController` is not enough — and even presenting it from another `UIViewController` does not trigger `onAppear`. The view needs to be rendered inside a visible (non-hidden) window for the SwiftUI lifecycle to begin.

Previously, the tests were using `makeKeyAndVisible()` on a dummy `UIWindow` to satisfy this requirement. However, this unintentionally replaced the main window of the host app, causing flaky behaviour and side effects across tests.

**Fix:**

This fix avoids calling `makeKeyAndVisible()` and instead attaches the view to a dummy `UIWindow` with `isHidden = false`. This is sufficient to trigger onAppear, without interfering with the app's main window or UI state.

### Testing Steps
Ensure CI is green

### Impact and Risks
Introduce flakiness in tests.

### Notes to Reviewer
The ticket also mentions "Tests use waitForExpectations while underlying calls potentially spawn Tasks - we should not mix structured concurrency with that API as it could produce unexpected deadlocks.” There are no tasks spawn from the SUT and its mocks. So the current fix should be enough.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1208698793834668
Tech Design URL:
CC: @afterxleep 

### Description

https://github.com/duckduckgo/iOS/pull/3519 introduced a debounce which was supposed to prevent hangs in some cases ([see Asana](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/414709148257752/task/1208671955053442?focus=true)), however it introduced a bug when some of the events could be fired out of order, causing the bars to remain in mid-transition state.
I removed the debounce and forced a layout pass after applying the transition to prevent late layout loop right before going to the next update.

Additionally I improved the scrolling experience to not show up blank bars container when find in page control is visible (additional constraint).

### Testing Steps

Do each for bottom and top bar setting:

1. On a random page, check whether showing and hiding bars is not stopping mid-point when doing a quick and short "flick" scroll. Do a general smoke check on hiding bars.
2. Open Find In Page and check if scroll insets are properly adjusted.
3. On a page with form inputs check if all input fields are accessible.
4. Verify if scrolling / zooming / rotating (rapidly in opposite directions) on https://randomtests.netlify.app/sample3.pdf does not cause a hang.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
App can hang in rare cases, webView insets can be calculated in a wrong way.

title: Networking V2 - New retry policy delay types
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1209775674444425?focus=true

### Description

Networking V2 now supports 3 different types of retry policy delays:
- Fixed: Always the same at each consecutive retry attempt
- Exponential: Exponential delay (2,4, 8, 16...) at each consecutive retry attempt
- Jitter:  Random value between set boundaries at each consecutive retry attempt

`Networking/v2/README.md` has been updated and expanded

### Testing Steps

Testing this is a bit tricky but:
1. Install Network Link Conditioner
2. Start the macOS app
3. Override AuthV2 feature flag
4. Restore your DDG subscription
5. Close settings
6. Enable Network Link Conditioner (100% loss)
 ![Screenshot 2025-04-16 at 15 12 14](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e831e22f-6cdb-4414-9ae4-2351ff0b95dc)
7. Open app settings
8. Check the logs, you'll see the Subscription API request failing every 30 seconds and retry with a delay that grows exponentially

The request uses:
```
APIRequestV2.RetryPolicy(maxRetries: 3, delay: .exponentialBackoff(baseDelay: .seconds(2)))
```

![Screenshot 2025-04-16 at 15 17 16](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f32f685-b10f-45ee-a2ae-84d6c3e1f438)

![Screenshot 2025-04-16 at 15 17 23](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe0ad0f6-26a0-45f5-a63f-2a95e24ceb0e)

![Screenshot 2025-04-16 at 15 17 30](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95ea18c2-f017-4d1d-ac54-03576bf37374)


New unit tests for the various retry policy delays have been added

title: macOS: Add an option to force tab crash
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

⚠️ If you're an external contributor, please file an issue before working on a PR. Discussing your changes beforehand will help ensure they align with our roadmap and that your time is well spent.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1209981645435762?focus=true
CC: @jotaemepereira 

### Description
This change adds a feature flag called tabCrashDebugTools that’s disabled by default.
When enabled, it adds an option to tab bar item context menu to force crash the tab.

### Testing Steps
1. Run the app, and disable internal user state as needed: _Main Menu -> Debug -> Remove Internal User State_.
2. Right click a tab item view and verify that the context menu **does not** include “Crash Tab” option at the bottom.
3. Enable Internal User state: _Main Menu -> Debug -> Set Internal User State_.
4. Right click a tab item view and verify that the context menu **does not** include “Crash Tab” option at the bottom.
5. Enable `tabCrashDebugTools` feature flag from _Main Menu -> Debug -> Feature Flag Overrides_.
6. Right click a tab item view and verify that the context menu **includes** “Crash Tab” option at the bottom.
7. Activate “Crash Tab” option and verify that the tab was immediately reloaded.
8. Pin a tab and right click it. Verify that the context menu **includes** “Crash Tab” option at the bottom.
7. Activate “Crash Tab” option on a pinned tab and verify that the tab was immediately reloaded.

### Impact and Risks
Low

#### What could go wrong?
The biggest risk is about making this option available to users, which I mitigated by requiring a feature flag that’s disabled by default (and only overridable by internal users anyway), and by verifying the logic with unit tests.

### Quality Considerations
See above.

title: [macOS] Min window size: Adjust minimum address bar width
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

⚠️ If you're an external contributor, please file an issue before working on a PR. Discussing your changes beforehand will help ensure they align with our roadmap and that your time is well spent.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1209568315204838
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1209811936242195

### Description

This updates the address bar layout in macOS to allow it to be resized, to support a minimum window size of 544 pt.

Various parts of the layout were limiting the window size and have been adjusted:

1. The home page now shows the Dax logo inside the address bar, instead of to the left of it.
2. The address bar has a minimum and maximum width for very large/small window sizes.
3. The address bar can take up all of the available space (no extra spacing on either side) at smaller window sizes.

Notes:

* The “Switch to Tab” box is hidden in the address bar at smaller window sizes, to prioritize showing the address bar text.
* There is a fix to the trailing space for the address bar text field. This accounts for the space taken by the AiChat, bookmark, and clear buttons. (Without this fix, there could be extra space on the right side of the address bar when no buttons were showing.)
* Support for resizing the window to the smallest size when the zoom or permissions buttons are visible in the address bar will be added separately.

Before|After
-|-
![Screenshot 2025-04-18 at 13 41 50](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17afb039-c71a-4b28-8dab-eb166a48f136)|![Screenshot 2025-04-18 at 13 18 31](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f2861e8-c772-48a7-8aeb-991ac9d3066c)
![Screenshot 2025-04-18 at 13 42 02](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a88247df-52f2-45f8-a643-1d4c846f469c)|![Screenshot 2025-04-18 at 13 18 51](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87eeaa38-98ff-45de-b24f-7ab55e260e8e)
![Screenshot 2025-04-18 at 13 42 12](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eaf560e1-3e85-4657-a009-820a3e718323)|![Screenshot 2025-04-18 at 13 20 03](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c4ab2074-e45b-4d7e-a42d-65abffb77e7c)



### Testing Steps
1. Enable all navigation bar items (including the home button on the left) and confirm you can resize the window to 544 pt, with the address bar resized as expected.
2. Hide all navigation bar items and confirm you can resize the window to 544 pt, with the address bar resized as expected.
3. Resize the window as large as possible as confirm the address bar is resized as expected (centered with a maximum width).
4. Confirm the address bar works as expected in these scenarios:
    * On the home page.
    * While searching/entering an address.
    * While entering an address that is open in another tab.
    * While displaying a website address.
    * With the AiChat button visible/hidden in the address bar.
5. Hide all navigation bar items and confirm you can resize the window to 544 pt.
6. Test across all supported macOS versions to confirm layout behaves as expected as window is resized.

### Impact and Risks

Medium: The likely impact would be visual, but if the address bar is resized poorly it could hinder the ability to read and enter text there.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1209949983074592?focus=true
- https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/740131

### Description
- Hack to break retain cycle between `AppKitMenuDelegate` ⇆ `ContextMenuResponder` when SwiftUI `.contextMenu` is used
- The issue seems to be caused by the fact that `AppKitMenuDelegate.menuResponder` should have been a weak variable but was declared as strong, leading to a retain cycle between `lazy var ContextMenuResponder.delegate: AppKitMenuDelegate` and `AppKitMenuDelegate.menuResponder`.
- The future fix by Apple would likely make the `AppKitMenuDelegate.menuResponder` variable weak, and nullifying it would cause an over-release. Nullifying the `lazy var delegate` does the trick and should be relatively safe to use.
- Reenable assertion failures probably accidentally disabled in some previous PRs and fix related test failures

### Tested on:
- ✅ Big Sur (Intel)
- ✅ Monterey (Intel)
- ✅ Ventura (Intel/M4)
- ✅ Sonoma (M4)
- ✅ Sequoia 15.0.1/15.4.1 (M4)

<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->

4. Right click the tab and choose Close
5. Validate video is stopped
6. Repeat opening different configurations of pinned tabs testing their context menu opening/closing and other places using SwiftUI context menu

title: Default values for feature flags
body:
**Re-open of https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/112**

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1200194497630846/1209432750561445
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/0/1202926619870900/1209523442095784

### Description

The current implementation of FeatureFlagger in BSK requires all feature flags to be explicitly defined in both the codebase and the privacy configuration service, which is used to remotely control feature flags at runtime. Over time, this leads to an accumulation of legacy flags within the privacy configuration, increasing maintenance overhead and complexity.

Introducing a new feature flag type: Failsafe. A Failsafe flag would be enabled by default in the codebase and would not have an explicit equivalent in the privacy configuration service on launch. However, it could be remotely disabled via the privacy configuration if necessary.

I've added some example flags for demonstrative purposes but would be happy to remove them if the reviewer thinks that's best.

### Testing Steps 
**macOS**
1. Go to Debug -> Feature Flag Overrides
2. Look for the two feature flags named `failsafeExample*`
3. Make sure their default values are on

**iOS**
1. Go to Settings -> All debug options -> Feature Flags
2. Look for the two feature flags named `failsafeExample*`
3. Make sure their default values are on

### Impact and Risks

Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
In later PRs if someone accidentally defaults a feature to on
**Mitigation**: All FeatureFlag / Experiment FeatureFlag definitions default to `false` so the developer has to consciously set this.

See https://app.asana.com/0/481882893211075/1209556022249884/f

title: Display an info icon to notify users about a crashed tab
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

⚠️ If you're an external contributor, please file an issue before working on a PR. Discussing your changes beforehand will help ensure they align with our roadmap and that your time is well spent.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1209977265286175?focus=true

### Description
This change displays an info icon next to the tab favicon for 20 seconds after a single crash.
The icon can be activated and it would show a popover explaining that the tab has crashed.
The icon is displayed on both active and inactive tabs when they crash.
If the popover is open, the 20s timer is invalidated. If the user clicks anywhere when the popover
is open, the popover gets closed and icon disappears.
The crash icons replaces audio icon on the tab bar view item.

### Testing Steps
**Feature flag disabled and non-internal user:**
1. Run the app and remove internal user state.
2. Open a website.
3. Crash a website using Activity Monitor.
4. Verify that the error page is shown and the tab bar view item doesn’t display an extra icon.

**Feature flag disabled and internal user:**
1. Run the app and set internal user state. Enable `tabCrashDebugTools` feature flag.
2. Open a website.
3. Crash a website using Activity Monitor.
4. Verify that the website is reloaded and the tab bar view item doesn’t display an extra icon.

**Feature flag enabled:**
1. Run the app and enable `tabCrashRecovery` and `tabCrashDebugTools` feature flags.
6. Open a tab and navigate to a website.
7. Crash a tab using context menu.
8. Verify that the tab is reloaded and an icon is displayed.
9. Click the icon and verify that a popover is displayed. Keep the popover on screen for >20s and verify that the icon doesn’t disappear.
10. Click anywhere on the app and verify that the popover and the icon are gone.
11. Crash the tab again and verify that the icon is displayed. Do nothing and verify that after 20s the icon disappears.
12. Crash the tab again and crash it one more time (in under 5 seconds). Verify that the tab displays an error page and the info icon is gone. Verify that reloading loads the website.
13. Repeat a single crash for a youtube video website to verify that the icon replaces the audio icon.
14. Finally, repeat the tests with a pinned tab.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

#### What could go wrong?
Not much as it’s just UI added on top of a previously reviewed mechanism.

### Quality Considerations
Full unit tests suite is added 👍

title: [macOS] Min window size: Adjust suggestions, Bookmarks, and Settings minimum window size
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1209993929328796?focus=true
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/481882893211075/task/1210044556037376?focus=true

### Description

This adjusts three parts of the app to handle the smaller minimum window size:

* Suggestions window (when entering text in the address bar)
* Bookmarks manager
* Settings

#### Suggestions window

The “Switch to tab” box is now only shown in the suggestions window if there is space for it (if the suggestions window is greater than a minimum width).

Related to this, the “Switch to tab” behavior in the address bar was updated to match (basing it on the size of the address bar rather than the overall window size).

#### Bookmarks manager

The Bookmarks manager can now be resized to the minimum window size:

* The sidebar can be compressed to a minimum 128 pt.
* When needed, the sidebar contents are truncated to fit and the bookmark count is hidden.
* The detail view (on the right) is updated to match the design spec:
   * The padding around the content is decreased.
   * The minimum width for the search bar was increased.
   * The buttons (new bookmark, new folder, delete, sort) are now compressed one at a time as the window is resized, so some labels don’t need to be truncated (instead of all labels being somewhat truncated).

#### Settings

The Settings (all sections) can now be resized to the minimum window size:

* The sidebar can be compressed to a minimum 128 pt.
* When needed, the sidebar contents are truncated to fit.
* The General section is updated to adjust to the smallest window size (allowing the contents to be resized to fit).

Note: I tested all of the buttons and links in each Settings section. The only view I found that didn’t stay within the minimum window size is Passwords & Autofill > Password Manager > Export Passwords. This displays a wider view (because the text does not wrap) but when it is closed, the window remains at the minimum size.

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Resize the window to the smallest window size.
2. Enter the address of a website open in another tab, and confirm the “Switch to tab” box does not appear in the suggestions window or in the address bar.
3. Open the Bookmarks manager (e.g. go to Bookmarks > Manage Bookmarks).
4. Confirm the window size didn't change, and the sidebar and detail view appear as expected. (Check that nested bookmark folders don’t prevent the window from being the smallest size, even if they aren’t all visible.)
6. Resize the window and confirm the sidebar and then the detail view expands as expected.
7. Resize the window again to the smallest window size.
8. Open Settings (using the menu at the top of the Bookmarks sidebar or e.g. go to DuckDuckGo > Settings in the menu).
9. Confirm the window size didn’t change, and the sidebar and detail view appear as expected.
10. Resize the window and confirm the sidebar and then the settings section expands as expected.
11. Open each settings section and confirm it is displayed as expected, and the settings it contains are visible and can be interacted with without changing the window size.

Confirm it works as expected in the following scenarios:

- Testing across all supported macOS versions.
- Testing with different interface languages (English and at least one verbose, non-English language).
   - Instead of changing the system language, you can edit the product scheme and go to Options > App Language > select Double-length Pseudolanguage. Then, build and run the app as usual to check the UI with very long strings.

### Impact and Risks

Low: Minor visual changes

#### What could go wrong?

Layout in the updated sections could be unexpected, with text unexpectedly truncated/unreadable when the window is resized.

title: Return early from navigationDidFail when it contains webkit termination error
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210080097969176?focus=true
CC: @mallexxx 

### Description
Turns out that on slower machines the webkit process termination may call navigationDidFail
callback before it calls webContentProcessDidTerminate. The former is then called with
the WebKit Termination error, and causes the termination error to be handled and webview state
altered to handle navigation error, which in fact isn’t a navigation error. That broke handling
webkit termination by the crash recovery extension.
This change updates navigationDidFail handler to return early in case of webkit termination error,
so that the termination handler can do its job.

### Testing Steps
I’ve tested it on:
* Big Sur, 
* Ventura
* Sequoia.

It was also an issue for Tak, who tested the build on his Ventura machine and found the issue to be fixed.
I consulted the change with Alex as well.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

title: AuthV2 Token branching between main app and SysExt fix
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/inbox/1205736674596206/item/1210082295267504/story/1210084645776832?focus=true
CC: @miasma13 

### Description

In [this task](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/inbox/1205736674596206/item/1210082295267504/story/1210084645776832?focus=true) Thomas noticed that, with AuthV2, we are getting a lot of 401 errors from the macOS VPN SysExt.

**What the app was doing:**
the main app uses token T1
the main app sends T1 to the SysExt
the main app force refresh T1 and obtains T2
the main app uses T2 from now on
the SysExt receives T1 and uses T1 from now on
Issue: The first time SysExt tries to refresh the token, it fails because T1 has already been refreshed more than 1h before.

**The fix:**
the main app uses token T1
the main app sends T1 to the SysExt
the main app force refresh T1 and obtains T2
the main app uses T2 from now on
the SysExt receives T1
the SysExt receives force refresh T1 and obtains T3
the SysExt uses T3 from now on

### Testing Steps

The best way to test this is by Thomas checking the backend, as nothing is noticeable from the client side.
The tests will be performed before merging.

---

### Description
Adjusting initial window size to 95% of visible screen area

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
**Test initial window size**
1. Execute `./macOS/clean-app.sh debug`
2. Run the app and observe the initial window size. It must be 90 percent of the visible screen area (visible screen area = screen area without the status bar and the Dock)

**Test window size of reopened window**
1. Resize the window
2. Close the window
3. Open a new window and make sure it has the same size and location as the closed window

**Test window size of restored window**
1. Quit the app
2. Open the app again and make sure the window has the same size and location

**Test ultra-wide monitor**
1. Execute `./macOS/clean-app.sh debug`
2. Run the app on ultra-wide monitor and observe the initial window size. The ratio should never be larger than 16:9, which means the window will be narrower than the ultra-wide screen.

**Test large monitor (Studio Display)**
1. Execute `./macOS/clean-app.sh debug`
2. Run the app on ultra-wide monitor and observe the initial window size. The size shouldn't be larger than 1920x1080 points

Note: If you don't have ultra-wide and large monitor, adjust constants in `InitialWindowFrameProvider` to test the functionality on your current display.

title: Disable tab auto-reload when tab crash debugging flag is set and crash recovery flag is not set
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210107348381777?focus=true

### Description
When Tab crash recovery flag is disabled, the app falls back to the legacy mechanism of auto-reloading
after all crashes for internal users. This prevents testing (observing) tab crashes. This change updates
the logic so that when tabCrashDebugging flag is enabled and tabCrashRecovery is disabled, auto-reload
is disabled for internal users.

### Testing Steps
1. Override `tabCrashRecovery` flag to be disabled.

        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 5) {

title: Fixes "ContentScopeScripts" building issue
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201037661562251/task/1210115274395884?focus=true

### Description

Resolves a common build issue we've been seeing recently.

> error: remove failed remove(/Users/ddg/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/DuckDuckGo-cwxizrjfhszusnhlertkynlioqyr/Build/Products/Debug/DuckDuckGo Personal Information Removal.app/Contents/Resources/ContentScopeScripts_ContentScopeScripts.bundle/Contents/Resources/pages/new-tab/company-icons): Directory not empty (66) (in target 'DuckDuckGoDBPBackgroundAgent' from project 'DuckDuckGo-macOS')

This is caused by a script in the build steps that's called "Copy Swift Package resources".

It was implemented to resolve [this issue](https://forums.swift.org/t/swift-packages-resource-bundle-not-present-in-xcarchive-when-framework-using-said-package-is-archived/50084/2), but only needs to be run for archive / install builds.

### Testing Steps

Just build a couple of times and make sure you get no errors about `ContentScopeScripts`.  Make sure the CI goes green.

### Impact and Risks

Low: I can think this would affect anything as it was implemented for archive builds (ie: install builds).

title: Fixes an issue that was causing the VPN to start on its own during the auth v2 migration
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1207603085593419/task/1210114952670833?focus=true

### Description

Fixes an issue that was causing the VPN to start on its own during the auth v2 migration

### Testing Steps

1. To make testing easier you can force reproduce the issue by forcing [this condition](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/0b3707d267adf0a7735002ef85fcb6e8f2e9b8fc/macOS/DuckDuckGoVPN/VPNAppEventsHandler.swift#L52) to succeed.  The same condition-change can be used to validate the original issue in `main` or disabling the guard added in this PR.
2. Please test using the "macOS VPN Agent" scheme.  You'll need to disable VPN agents following these steps in Terminal.app:
    - `launchctl list | grep duck"
    - Pick the ID for the agent you want to disable
    - `launchtl remove <agent_id>`

title: [macOS] Add overflow menu for pinned nav bar buttons
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1209813459676820?focus=true

### Description

This adds an overflow menu to the browser navigation bar. When the browser window is resized to a small width, and there are buttons pinned to the nav bar (e.g. the home button, or shortcuts like downloads, passwords), the overflow menu is displayed if the buttons overflow the available width.

#### Expected behavior

* When a window/tab is opened, a new button is added to the navigation bar, or the window is resized, the overflow menu will appear if needed.
* When the overflow menu is needed, buttons will be moved one at a time from the navigation bar to the overflow menu.
* When more space is available in the navigation bar, buttons will be moved one at a time from the overflow menu back to the navigation bar.
* When a menu item in the overflow menu is clicked on, and has a related popover, it will become visible in the navigation bar and the popover will be displayed.

#### Primary Changes

* Adds an overflow menu button that is hidden by default.
* Tracks the pinned views, and which views are visible in the navigation bar or moved into the overflow menu. These properties also determine the order that views will be moved in/out of the overflow menu.
* Tracks the required width for the pinned views, and the available space for showing the in the navigation bar (`overflowThreshold` - this is the threshold for moving items into the overflow menu).
* When the view appears, the view is resized, the shortcut buttons in the navigation bar change, or the zoom/permissions buttons in the address bar change, the navigation bar is updated (moving items in or out of the overflow menu) based on the window’s width and available space.

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Right-click in the navigation bar to enable the optional pinned views:
   * Home button
   * Passwords shortcut
   * Bookmarks shortcut
   * Downloads shortcut
   * VPN shortcut
2. Open a website and zoom in or trigger permissions (e.g. camera/microphone, pop-up window).
3. Confirm you can resize the window to a large size and all buttons are visible in the navigation bar.
4. Confirm you can resize the window to the smallest width (544 pt) and buttons are progressively moved into the overflow menu.
5. Open the overflow menu and select an item. Confirm it performs the expected action (e.g. “Home” takes you to homepage; other buttons are moved back to the navigation bar and their respective popovers are opened).

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes

#### What could go wrong?
Buttons could be hidden/shown unexpectedly at small window widths, or resize the window unexpectedly

title: [macOS] Allow smaller minimum window size
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1210159114504360?focus=true

### Description

This is the final PR to merge these changes:

* https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/536
* https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/577
* https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/648

Additional changes in this PR:

* Resolves merge conflicts:
   * Reverts earlier change that moved the Dax logo inside the address bar (this is feature flagged in `main` as part of the ongoing visual refresh).
   * Now supports resizing the window to the smallest width with the Dax logo inside or outside the address bar.
* The address bar stays the same width when activating the text field.

Not resolved:

From https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/648#pullrequestreview-2814280977:

> Address bar string is truncated too early, even with the hidden bookmarks button, there’s still room for more text.

This happens because the passive text field is moved to the left, to accommodate the AI chat button:

https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/28ea3a57332a19661f8edca08aa47113e84b1b6c/macOS/DuckDuckGo/NavigationBar/View/AddressBarViewController.swift#L670

As far as I can see, it only happens when the AI chat button is visible _and_ the zoom/permissions buttons are shown. Because of how the layout is currently done, I can’t find a reasonable way to adjust it right now.

### Testing Steps

Test with the `visualRefresh` feature flag enabled and disabled:

1. Confirm the window can be resized down to 544 pt; opening new tabs and windows retains that width.
2. All settings pages can be resized, viewed, and interacted with at the narrow width.
3. The bookmarks management page can be resized, viewed, and interacted with at the narrow width.
4. The Home button and shortcuts (Passwords, Bookmarks, Downloads, VPN) can be enabled from the View menu. When needed, these buttons will move to an overflow menu to fit the narrow width.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes

#### What could go wrong?
The window resize not working as expected. In particular, the resize not working correctly when the Dax logo appears outside the address bar (on the home page).

title: Prevent multiple sync connection requests simultaneously
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1202926619870900/task/1210171634625852?focus=true

### Description

We discovered that a recent [Rise in macOS login errors after exchange flow rollout](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210047340594631) could well be due to pasting an exchange code multiple times on macOS. Windows doesn't have this issue because they present a "Preparing to Sync" in this case, blocking any further interaction.

We can present the same dialog on macOS too, however this would require a cancel button which is a change that would require a Ship Review (see [Update macOS Preparing to Sync dialog to be cancellable](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210170146955358)).

Instead, let's just block further requests if one is in flight so we don't spam the backend and cause errors.

### Testing Steps
1. Make sure you have sync enabled on one device (let's say iOS for the purposes of this test, can be any though)
2. Build the macOS app from this branch and go to the sync screen (Settings -> Sync and Backup)
3. Make sure sync is *not* enabled
4. Click "Sync with another device" on both platforms
5. From the iOS device, tap Share Text Code and Copy
6. Make sure this code is on the pasteboard of your macOS device
7. Click the "Paste" button **multiple times rapidly.**
8. Confirm there is no error alert shown

title: Do not pretty print JSON injected into C-S-S script.
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1163321984198618/task/1209286025185882?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC: @jonathanKingston 

### Description
Currently, the privacy config is encoded as JSON to be injected into the C-S-S script. This allows C-S-S to use values from the config after injection.

The current implementation 'pretty prints' the config data (i.e. adding tabs and new lines so it is human readable). This is not needed, as the data is just directly consumed by the JS parser after injection. Switching to this compact encoding reduced the config size by 49% (350k -> 180k), and the resulting C-S-S script size by 27% (638k -> 468k).

### Testing Steps
1. Validate that C-S-S is still working, e.g. by checking that the tests on https://privacy-test-pages.site/features/element-hiding/ still pass.

title: Adds per-target support for xcstrings
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203108348835387/task/1210195313151129?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

Improves our localization resources so that we'll be able to have translations that are specific to a build target.  This resolves existing issues where building our App Store targets creates `.xcstring` file differences.

### Changes

- DuckDuckGo main browser targets (macOS) now use separate Info.plist and InfoPlist.xcstring files
- VPN System Extension targets now use separate Info.plist and InfoPlist.xcstring files.  We also relocated the .xcstring files to be near the info.plist files.
- Added AppStore.xcstrings and DeveloperID.xcstrings for target-specific strings.  Localizable.xcstrings is still used for strings that are used in both targets.

### Testing Steps

1. Build `macOS Browser`
2. Build `macOS Browser App Store`
3. Build `macOS Browser` again
4. Ensure there are no xcstring differences.

Feel free to repeat steps 1-3 as much as you want.  The  same steps can be used to see the issue in `main` that this PR is resolving.

### Impact and Risks

Medium.

#### What could go wrong?

If there's any mistake in my changes it could affect existing copy.

### Quality Considerations

- I'll merge this right after a code freeze to make sure we have 2 full weeks to spot any issue.
- I've exported the strings and reimported them and validated that the new xcstring files are properly updated.

### Notes to Reviewer

title: Updates should ask the user before restarting the app
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206580121312550/task/1210262964843197?focus=true

### Description

App updates will no longer automatically restart the App.

### Testing Steps

When switching the feature flag ON and OFF please restart the app to make sure you're working on a clean state.

Validate behavior is unchanged with feature-flag off:

1. Automatic updates should stop only at the restart checkpoint.
2. Manual updates should stop only at the download checkpoint.
3. Switching from automatic to manual while a download is ongoing should reset the update and stop at the download checkpoint.
4. Switching from manual to automatic while a download is ongoing should reset the update and start downloading again.
5. When automatic updates are enabled and the update is expired (use Debug Menu > Updates > Restart last update check), clicking "Restart to Update" should download the update again.

Validate new behavior with feature-flag on:

1. Automatic updates should stop only at the restart checkpoint.
2. Manual updates should stop at the download checkpoint and again at the restart checkpoint.
3. Switching from Automatic to Manual while a download is ongoing should reset the update and stop at the download checkpoint
4. Switching from Manual to Automatic while a download is ongoing should reset the update and start downloading again
5. When automatic updates are enabled and the update is expired (use Debug Menu > Updates > Restart last update check), clicking "Restart to Update" should install the update immediately.
6. When automatic updates are enabled and the update is expired (use Debug Menu > Updates > Restart last update check), closing settings should and reopening it should result in a new update being downloaded.  The same goes for the update notification (blue dot).


### Impact and Risks

Meidum: could affect the update feature, but I've done some thorough testing and expect the same will happen during this review.

#### What could go wrong?

We could break the update feature.

### Quality Considerations

The most important bit is to make sure to validate the current experience remains unchanged.

### Notes to Reviewer

title: iOS+macOS: Properly set app's user agent for all API requests
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203936086921904/task/1210056283063113?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description
We have identified that some parts of the app in their network calls were not properly setting app's user agent, hence it defaulted to the system one. The affected places included: Subscription v1 APIs, and APIs using Networking v2 (Subscription v2 APIs and Malicious Site Detection).

### Testing Steps
Verify user agent of the requests fired by the following APIs:
- Subscription v1
- Subscription v2 (including OAuth) 
- Malicious Site Detection

The expected user agent to be used is:
- iOS: `DefaultUserAgentManager.duckDuckGoUserAgent`
- macOS: `UserAgent.duckDuckGoUserAgent()`

### Impact and Risks
Low

#### What could go wrong?
Rather unlikely to affect unless we include a bug. Scope of change is to pass platform user agent and add it in a new header parameter.

title: iOS: Upgrade Privacy Pro Free Trials From Experiment to Full Feature
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206488453854252/task/1209771111633984

### Description
This PR converts the iOS Privacy Pro Free Trial feature from an experiment to a fully shipped feature. Changes include:

1. Adding a new non-experiment feature flag and wrapping type
2. Adding new Subscription products ids for production and staging
3. Removing experiment code (types, pixels etc.)
4. Adding tests & documentation

### Notes
* A separate PR with translations for the copy will follow later but does not block merging this PR

### Testing Steps
##### Check Settings Copy When User is Eligible for Trial & Purchase ROW Trial Sub Subscription
1. From AppStoreConnect, select a EU-based PP-eligible sandbox user (e.g one from Poland/Ireland who has no active Sub)
2. Sign in using this sandbox user in the iOS settings under `Developer`
3. Launch the alpha app and ensure it has no active subscription
4. Navigate to the settings screen, and ensure that you see the promo text “Try Privacy Pro Free” instead of the regular “Get Privacy Pro” text (See [here](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1209882621281268/comment/1210315800376202?focus=true))
6. Navigate to the PP paywall
7. Ensure that it displays the free trial UI (i.e. buttons with free trial copy)
8. Complete the purchase and ensure that Apple highlights that it’s a 1-week trial
9. Post-purchase ensure entitlements are as expected for the EU, and that PP works as expected

##### Check Copy When User Has No Subscription and is Ineligible for Trial
1. Cancel the subscription you purchased above
2. Remove sub from the device and wait for current subscription to expire (~5 mins with Sandbox users)
3. Navigate to the Settings screen and ensure it displays “Get Privacy Pro”
4. Navigate to the PP paywall
5. Ensure that it displays the non-trial UI (i.e. buttons with NO free trial copy)

### Impact and Risks
High: Privacy Pro, Subscriptions etc. could not function as expected

#### What could go wrong?
* Subscription purchase failing

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/414709148257752/task/1210229858278888
Tech Design URL:
CC: @amddg44 

### Description

Because "real" OmniBar was removed from the cell it probably meant it got reassigned to another one. This adds another reuse identifier distinguishing between the real and template OmniBars so that cells don't get cross-reused for these two cases.

### Testing Steps

More testing scenarios can be found in the [task](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/414709148257752/task/1210229858278888).

1. Create more than 3 tabs. Make sure there's no NTP tab at the end.
1. Swipe to the first tab.
1. Swipe to the last tab.
1. Drag more to create a new tab, but don't finish the gesture.
1. Make sure OmniBar is visible all the time.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
Not sure, as this part of the app proved to be troublesome recently.

title: Hidden webView pixel to fire only when error is invisible
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/414235014887631/task/1210251291351493?focus=true

### Description

There's a rare bug where the webView appears to be invisible occasionally on navigating to a tab. Some pixels were added to fire from the iOS TabViewController when the webView is hidden, not in the hierarchy etc. After releasing these, I found that there were a few fired when webView.isHidden. However, this may be the case when an error is showing.

Goal
Rule out cases where the tab's error view is showing (with text). Only fire it if:
- The error is invisible
- The error is visible but contains no text

### Testing Steps
- Make sure you're running while plugged into the debugger
- Visit https://privacy-test-pages.site/network-error/drop
- Check that the `m_debug_webview_in_visible_tab_hidden` is NOT fired

### Impact and Risks
<!-- 
What's the impact on users if something goes wrong?

High: Could affect user privacy, lose user data, break core functionality
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features
None: Internal tooling, documentation
-->

#### What could go wrong?
Worst case: pixel never fires and I'm back to square one.

### Quality Considerations
Just pixels that were already fired but honed in.

title: Disable Onboarding for iPad users running on OS 17.7.7
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/414709148257752/task/1210267814606214

### Description
A recent Apple update (version 17.7.7) affected the persistence layer, particularly the User Defaults, resulting in several issues, including the onboarding process appearing at every app launch.
For more info check [Asana](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/414709148257752/task/1210267814606214) 

This PR prevents showing the Onboarding for those users to avoid users’ frustration and complaints.

### Testing Steps
1. Check CI is green.
2. In `LaunchOptionsHandler.swift` change `systemVersion == “17.7.7”` to a version you can run on simulator/device.
3. Delete the DDG from simulator/device.
4. Run the app.
5. Ensure the linear onboarding is not presented.
6. Navigate to a web page with trackers e.g. instagram.com
7. Ensure that no Dax Dialogs are shown.   

### Impact and Risks
The feature is already broken for these users.

#### What could go wrong?
Can’t get worse than this.

### Description
Adds the pixels and parameters for the required alpha build. 
Note that these parameters must never reach production, and are compile flagged and commented appropriately 
Do not merge until privacy triage is approved

Also sneaks unrelated changes in:
- Fixes an issue where we didn't schedule a new background task if the previous one completed without the expiration handler firing
- Changes the events table in the db viewer to show the newest first
- Renames a file to remove the DataBrokerProtection prefix as previously discussed. The iOSManager is now the only one with it. I deliberately kept it, since following the same logic it would just be called "manager" which is definitely confusing. And it is the one object that manages all on DBP on iOS, so I think it's fair for it to still have DBP in the name

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Smoke test macOS with both debug and release builds

- Release build shouldn't do PIR jobs or fire pixels 
- The debug build should fire background task related pixels, and scan and opt out start and end pixels should have device IDs and device names. You check the device ID matches the ID in PIR settings
- You can force a background task to run by backgrounding the app, pausing the debugger, and running the following:
```
e -l objc -- (void)[[BGTaskScheduler sharedScheduler] _simulateLaunchForTaskWithIdentifier:@"com.duckduckgo.app.dbp.backgroundProcessing"]
```

title: Reapply shadows on NTP for visual updates
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

⚠️ If you're an external contributor, please file an issue before working on a PR. Discussing your changes beforehand will help ensure they align with our roadmap and that your time is well spent.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206226850447395/task/1210259281611903
Tech Design URL:
CC: @Bunn 

### Description

This re-applies the shadows on NewTabPage after a revert (https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/741) has been done to fix a hang.

Additionally I renamed the NTP root views so their purpose is more clear.

### Testing Steps

#### Making sure the NTP won't hang
1. Add 15-20 favorites
2. Set address bar position to bottom
3. Open NTP
4. Open keyboard by tapping on URL bar
5. Make sure app is still working without a hang

#### Testing updates to favorites collection
1. Enable experimental appearance. Restart app.
2. With a single favorite on NTP, make sure the page is scrollable.
3. Add a few **bookmarks**, while on NTP, enter bookmarks menu and mark 3 new bookmarks as favorites (so that they extend to another row).
4. Go back to NTP, make sure the grid shows up properly (is not misaligned)
5. Remove favorites so there's one less row required. Make sure the grid is not misaligned.

#### Testing shadows

title: Add Protections Report widget to unify Privacy Stats and Recent Activity
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1209353029633684?focus=true

### Description
This change unifies protection stats widgets on New Tab Page, allowing all users to access both Privacy Stats
and Recent Activity. Previously Recent Activity was only available to existing users and new users were seeing Privacy Stats.
The new widget that combines the two is called Protections Report. It provides its own API for visibility settings
and currently active “feed” (Privacy Stats or Recent Activity), plus defines API to request total number of blocked
trackers.
Visibility APIs for Privacy Stats and Recent Activity were removed and totalCount was removed from PrivacyStatsData.
Additionally this change updates AppearancePreferencesPersistor to use ThrowingKeyValueStoring instead of UserDefaults. All new code added to the persistor should use the new store, while the pre-existing properties still
rely on UserDefaults for storage. To make this happen, AppearancePreferences, StartupPreferences and
DataClearingPreferences singletons were removed and replaced with properties held by AppDelegate.

### Testing Steps
1. Run `./clean-app.sh debug` and launch the app. Verify that you’re being presented with Protections Report in expanded state (but no data of course) and the selected feed is “Stats”.
2. Quit the app, run `./clean-app.sh debug` and then also run `defaults write com.duckduckgo.macos.browser.debug new-tab-page.is-new-user -bool false`, and then launch the app. Verify that you’re being presented with Protections Report in expanded state (but no data) and the selected feed is “Details”.
3. Go to Settings -> Appearance and verify that under New Tab Page you see Favorites and Protections Report. Verify that toggling Protections Report from there adjusts the visibility of the protections widget.
4. Do a general smoke-testing of the Privacy Stats and Recent Activity. There are no changes to the widgets themselves and to their logic (besides visibility settings), only to how they’re presented on the NTP.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

#### What could go wrong?
The biggest risk is failing to migrate existing users properly to the new widget, in terms of migrating:
* visibility flag,
* collapsed/expanded state,
* selected feed.
The migration logic is handled by `NewTabPageProtectionsReportSettingsMigrator` and unit-tested thoroughly. There’s also [an Asana task](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210270584197856?focus=true) outlining the logic here (that’s extracted from the unit tests, actually).

title: Use ThrowingKeyValueStoring in AppearancePreferences and remove singleton
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210321544153920?focus=true
CC: @bwaresiak 

### Description
This change updates AppearancePreferencesPersistor to use ThrowingKeyValueStoring instead of UserDefaults.
All new code added to the persistor should use the new store, while the pre-existing properties still
rely on UserDefaults for storage.
To make this happen, AppearancePreferences, StartupPreferences and DataClearingPreferences singletons
were removed and replaced with properties held by AppDelegate.

### Testing Steps
1. Verify that CI is green.
2. Verify that [UI tests workflow](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/15183578651) is green.
3. Smoke test the app to verify that it doesn’t crash at startup and persists appearance settings.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
Removing singletons could cause app crashes, but that would happen on app startup, and my testing went well so it shouldn’t be a problem.

### Notes to the Reviewer
The changes here are mostly about renaming `.shared` to `NSApp.delegateTyped.*Preferences` with small refactoring here and there to inject preferences objects from the app delegate. I deliberately limited the scope of the refactoring for now, because it can be improved gradually once we have this first bit in place.

title: [macOS] Implement scheduling logic for default browser and add to dock prompts
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210257532277816
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/481882893211075/task/1210257532277827
CC:

### Description
This PR implements the scheduling logic for presenting the 'Set as Default’ (SAD) browser and Add to dDock (ATT = Add to Taskbar) prompts.
Scheduling rules are defined in this [task](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206329551987282/task/1210226206083041?focus=true) 

### Testing Steps

**Prerequisites:**
- Run ./macOS/clean-app.sh debug|review (depending if testing a debug or ad-hoc build)
- Return `true` in `isDefaultBrowserAndDockPromptFeatureEnabled:Bool` defined in `DefaultBrowserAndDockPromptFeatureFlagger.swift`
- Set default values for prompt timing to low value (e.g. 3) in `DefaultBrowserAndDockPromptFeatureSettings defaultValue: Int` defined in `DefaultBrowserAndDockPromptFeatureFlagger.swift`

**Scenario 1 - Show Prompts Depending on Time Schedule**
1. Install the app, ensuring that the prerequisites are followed.
2. Open System Settings and click ‘Date & Time’ under ‘General'. 
3. Disable ‘Set time and date automatically’ to be able to override the current time.
4. Set a date in the future for which the SAD/ATT popover should not show.
5. Open a new window. 
6. Ensure that no SAD/ATT popover is prompted.

- enable AuthV1

- enable authv2

- kill app

body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1210271282469228

### Description

- Adds throwing behavior when SecRandomCopyBytes fails, surfaces errors via a new OAuthCodesGeneratorError.

title: macOS Visual Refresh: Design Feedback
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210255472500732?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

# Description
This addresses different design issues, improvements and changes in requirements for the new visual refresh. 

I will do my best to make a list of the different changes made, list of known issues and what we will do as follow-up work.

## Changes in the tab bar

### Fire graphic is missing gradients - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210340821019436?focus=true)

Fixed by changing the SVG to a PDF, given the SVG was not exporting the gradients correctly

![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 2 32 35 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fd3661f-e19a-4c77-95a8-27638ec6f87e)

### The + button in the tab bar being cut-off - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210267156924626)

See the attached gif of the old behavior (the + button was being cut-off). This is now fixed by calculating the width of the tab collection view correctly now that we added the extra space for the s-shaped tabs.

![CleanShot 2025-05-20 at 20 36 05](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/766ca609-765f-4961-8a4f-088608a795bc)

### Tweaks to the S-Shaped - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210340821019431?focus=true)

We did the following changes to make the S-shaped lool better: 
- changed the size for 12px to 10px on standard tabs (it was wrong before)
- tabs now touch the top of the window (it had some space before)

### Hide adjacent separators on hover - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210340821019437?focus=true)

When you hover over a standard tab, now we hide the separators. This was done by checking the element to the left of the hovered cell and if it existed, update the separator there.

![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 14 40 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19e38d80-16bb-46c7-b772-fa2c26a918db)

### Tabs in overflow have the bottom corner clipped - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210340821019435?focus=true)

We reduced the space of the s-shaped in the overflow.

| Before | After |
| ------ | ----- |
![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 20 00 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af6eae41-c792-4782-8c78-e60c667d7f85)|![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 21 04 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6d1e0b1-0a98-4eed-a8bb-4a37ac9cf311)

### Pinned tabs now have the same hover treatment as standard tabs - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210356093688271)

![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 43 36 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ebafb06-3e2f-4590-980e-6aaf14c398b0)

### Other changes

- Update the add tab button and fire button to have the size and rounded borderes like the navigation and address bar buttons - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210340821019429)
- Fix the spacing around the add tab button - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210340821019428)
- Fixes the spacing between the icon and the label inside a standard tab - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210384360528325)
- Removes the drop shadow applied to pinned tabs - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210369354427096)
- Fixes the icon moving when selecting a tab - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210384360528321)

## Changes in the Address Bar

### Replace Logo with Search Icon In New Tab - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210356093689279)

The Dax logo will be removed from inside the address bar, instead we will show the search icon logo.

![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 28 10 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be40c032-784c-4f70-a09e-69f55bf53163)

### Replace address bar shield with new one (without the checkmark) - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210348492887852)

![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 30 03 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b44c227b-6683-40fd-88b4-1640891e1f84)

### Address bar size and focus behavior mismatches - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210345746629545)

- This fixes the whole navigation bar increasing its size when focused, instead of only the address bar.
- It fixes the margins between the privacy shield and ai chat icons
- It also expands the address bar two points wider. I’m using fake views to do this, by adding two views to the current address bar stack view
- I also fixed the corner radius for these views to match the designs.

| No focus | Focused |
| ------ | ----- |
![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 33 15 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49429d17-6653-41fc-be4f-dedf16ea9fe4)|![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 33 03 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc64b8d6-31ad-4369-ad4c-05eb4b661ea1)

### Address bar field should have a shadow when inactive - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210340821019433)

![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 39 16 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d220dafe-f0b5-4636-9127-f11ae8d4c09c)

### Changes to suggestions - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210382198124843)

- Height for rows for on new tab and normal sites are the same
- The highlighted row has different corrner radius
- The suggestion view has a different corner radius
- We changed the spacing in the bottom and the spacing of the first row with the top.
- We updated all the icons to match the new ones

![Screenshot 2025-05-28 at 5 42 13 PM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9a85a35-9e21-4d0c-88e2-b2e5c65a7a06)

## Other changes

- Fixes to the pop-up window - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210403543523690)
- Fixed the size and spacing of the navigation toolbar and tab bar icons - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210345746629571)
- Update the bookmarks bar items hover state radius - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210356093688267)

## Pending changes

- Inactive standard tab text is not ‘disabled’ when window is not in foreground - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210375537857061)
- Update the permission icons to use the new ones - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210388032589569)

## Will not fix

The following issues where found during the implementation of the visual refresh but they were not introduced by it, so I’m going to create task to fix them on O-L but outside this project.

- Close icon animates independently of tab title - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210345746629551)
- The divider between address bar and suggestions is wider - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210393330652316)
- The address bar glitch if you resize it while the suggestion view is shown - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210393330652317)
- Margins on dividers in the URL bar should be consistent - [link](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210358956908894)

---

### Testing Steps

1. Set internal user state
2. Go to Debug -> Feature Flag Overrides, and select the visual refresh flag
3. Restart the app
4. Check the designs are applied and play a bit with the app to find any bugs
5. Remove the Feature Flag overrided and restart the app again
6. Check the legacy visuals are applied and no bugs happen

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
If adding the code to support the visual refresh breaks flows in the legacy UI.

### Quality Considerations
Check the quality of the UI and interactions

### Notes to Reviewer
Nothing specific.
