title: macOS: Privacy Pro Free Trials
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210411465498094

### Description
This PR makes Privacy Pro Free Trials available to all eligible macOS App Store users. Key changes include:
1. Adding a feature flag to enable rollback.
2. Add new Subscription product Ids for debug, review and Testflight macOS builds.
3. Fetching Free Trial `SubscriptionOptions`s for v1 and v2 when the feature flag is enabled.
4. Adding new `AppStoreSubscriptionProduct` and `StoreProduct` types to wrap StoreKit product and allow storing of trial eligibility state.
5. Refresh trial eligibility post-purchase.
6. Add a new UI element, `MenuItemWithBadge` to display a badge on the More Options menu.
7. Display Free Trial promotion in Settings preferences pane and More Options Menu.
8. Add strings and translations.

### Testing Prerequisites
1. Ensure you have no active Subscription
2. Ensure the purchase environment is staging.
3. Set a custom base subscription URL to `https://charmston.duckduckgo.com/subscriptions`
4. Identify a sandbox user without an active subscription.

### Testing Steps
#### Test 1 - Check Feature Flag
1. Remove internal user state
2. Open More Options Menu and ensure no promotion is displayed next to ‘Privacy Pro’
5. Open PP Settings Preference Pane and ensure no promotion is displayed on the purchase button
6. Open the PP paywall and ensure no promotion is displayed on the purchase button

#### Test 2 - Check Stripe displays no Free Trial promotion
1. Set purchase platform to Stripe
2. Set internal user state to enabled
3. Open More Options Menu and ensure no promotion is displayed next to ‘Privacy Pro’
5. Open PP Settings Preference Pane and ensure no promotion is displayed on the purchase button
7. Open the PP paywall and ensure no promotion is displayed on the purchase button

#### Test 3 - Purchase a Free Trial
1. Set purchase platform to AppStore
2. Set internal user state to enabled
3. Open More Options Menu and ensure you see a promotion matching the [designs](https://www.figma.com/design/jd7VXZ3RFFfmidaKWRLslZ/Desktop-Free-Trial?node-id=10-2191&t=EjW1a0Sq2MGmDKnI-4)
4. Click the promotion and when the paywall opens ensure you see the ‘Free Trial’ purchase buttons
6. Close the paywall. 
8. Open PP Settings Preference Pane and ensure the promotion is displayed on the purchase button
9. Open the PP paywall and purchase a Monthly sub with 1 week Free Trial (using a sandbox user)
10. Ensure purchase completes
11. Open More Options Menu and ensure no promotion is displayed next to ‘Privacy Pro’
12. Open PP Settings Preference Pane and ensure it displays “Free Trial Active” under the title
13. On the same screen ensure that under “Subscription Settings" it says “Your free trial ends on {date} & automatically converts to a monthly paid subscription on that day”.
14. Wait 5 mins
15. Reopen the Settings Preference Pane and ensure that now the UI displays the non-trial state (standard subscribed state)
16. …continue in test 4 below…

#### Test 4 - Not Eligible for a Trial a second time
1. Sign in to the same sandbox user on your phone
2. Cancel the subscription
3. Navigate back to the browser
4. Ensure the PP Settings Preference Pane displays the correct state
5. Remove the subscription from the device
7. Ensure the More Options Menu and PP Settings Preference Pane DO NOT display any trial promotional text
8. Open the paywall and ensure the same
9. Purchase a subscription and ensure you are not offered a trial by Apple


### Impact and Risks
High: Could impact Privacy Pro purchase

#### What could go wrong?
Failed purchases

title: Cache Ruby packages in CI workflows
body:
# Background
* Most of our workflows use fastlane now (that includes macOS PR checks that need it for code signing)
* Setting up fastlane (via installing bundler dependencies from Gemfile) takes between 30s and 2 minutes
* These dependencies rarely change - only when bumping fastlane plugin, fastlane itself or updating other packages as prompted by dependabot.
* We can use GHA cache to store Ruby dependencies to speed up workflows.

# Objective
Set up caching for Ruby (separately for macOS and iOS) in a similar way to how it’s done for Swift packages.

title: Cache Ruby packages in CI workflows
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203301625297703/task/1209694315376628?focus=true

### Description:
Implements comprehensive Ruby package caching across all CI workflows to significantly speed up fastlane setup times.

## Problem

Most workflows use fastlane (via bundler) for code signing and release management, with setup taking 30s-2min per run. Ruby dependencies rarely change (only during fastlane updates or dependabot bumps), making them ideal candidates for caching similar to existing Swift package caching.

## Solution

- **Created reusable action** `.github/actions/setup-ruby/action.yml` for consistent Ruby dependency caching
- **Updated all 28 workflows** (11 iOS + 16 macOS + 1 cross-platform) to use cached Ruby setup
- **Follows existing patterns** used for Swift package caching with `actions/cache@v4`

## Implementation Details

**Cache Strategy:**
- Cache path: `{working-directory}/vendor/bundle` (already in `.gitignore`)
- Cache keys: `${{ runner.os }}-{ios|macos}-ruby-${{ hashFiles('*/Gemfile.lock') }}`
- Restore-keys provide fallback for partial cache hits during dependency updates
- Separate caches for iOS and macOS since they have different Gemfiles

**Workflows Updated:**
- All iOS workflows: PR checks, releases, builds, hotfixes, alpha/adhoc distributions
- All macOS workflows: PR checks, releases, builds, DMG creation, end-to-end tests, UI tests
- Cross-platform: `update_code_signing.yml` with dual iOS/macOS caching

**Usage Example:**
```yaml
- name: Setup Ruby and dependencies
  uses: ./.github/actions/setup-ruby
  with:
    working-directory: iOS  # or macOS
    cache-key-prefix: ios-ruby  # or macos-ruby
```

## Benefits

🚀 **Performance**: Eliminates 30s-2min fastlane setup when dependencies unchanged  
🔧 **Maintainability**: Reusable action ensures consistency across all workflows  
📦 **Smart Caching**: Platform-specific caches based on respective Gemfile.lock files  
⚡ **Fallback Support**: Graceful degradation during dependency updates

## Verification

- ✅ All 35+ `bundle install` statements replaced with cached setup
- ✅ No working code deleted - purely additive caching layer
- ✅ Follows repository's existing Swift package caching patterns
- ✅ `vendor/bundle` already excluded by `.gitignore`

Fixes #896.

---

title: Inject suffix from ios_adhoc.yml workflow into build version
body:
# Background
* It's not always clear when an adhoc build has been deployed properly - it's easy to miss and it would be good if you could confirm it easily
* The workflow takes an optional suffix parameter: "Text to append at the end of the build name”
* We could take the suffix parameter and put it in the Settings view next to the version information.

# Objective
Update ios_adhoc.yml so that when `suffix` parameter is provided:
* sets that parameter value for `DDG_ALPHA_BUILD_SUFFIX` key to the Info.plist file for the iOS app.
* retrieves that Info.plist value and append it to `SettingsState.version`

As a result, we should be able to see the suffix it in the Settings about screen, e.g. "7.136.0.0-whatever-i-typed-there" 

This will save having to do this in the app itself and risk committing something you don't mean to.

### Description

* Adds a subfeature for visual updates, allowing to incrementally roll out the visual updates.
* Switches the flag source to `remoteReleaseable`.
* Adjusts the flag state handling so that the visual updates are not toggled during runtime. This is required because the `MainViewController` cannot be easily recreated during runtime, so changing the appearance setting would cause glitches.

### Testing Steps
1. Go to Debug settings, disable internal user flag if it's enabled (this also disabled any flag overrides)
2. Override privacy config to `https://www.jsonblob.com/api/1377975671510458368` (feature enabled)
3. Click around the app features and ensure the change was NOT applied right away.
4. Restart the app, verify the setting is being respected now.
5. Modify `https://www.jsonblob.com/1377975671510458368` and change `experimentalBrowserTheming.onByDefault.state` to "disabled".
6. Go to Settings -> Debug -> Configuration Refresh Info and press reload.
7. Restart the app and verify the visual updates are disabled.

### Impact and Risks

body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1207603085593419/task/1210422858992201?focus=true

### Description

We want to disable login items if the user has no VPN access

Also improves the code and add tests.

### Testing Steps

1. Connect the VPN so login items are loaded.
2. Disconnect it.
3. Restart the app, ensure the login items are restarted but not disabled.
4. Force [this](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/06a80cdad3e04dc878cc096e4179be5a823a4869/macOS/DuckDuckGo/Waitlist/VPNFeatureGatekeeper.swift#L62) to return `false`.
5. Start the App again, the login items should be disabled.

### Impact and Risks

Medium.

#### What could go wrong?

My changes could have some flaw.

### Quality Considerations

I added testing so that this will be more resilient in the future.

### Notes to Reviewer

Instead of trying to hard-disable the VPN I think it's safer to soft-disable it here.  The login items will be disabled, which is what people find annoying.  As long as the user doesn't enable PPro and start the VPN then they won't see anything related to VPN.

title: [iOS] Incorrect URL shown when ad is clicked in SERP and iOS opens a native app
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1209365034718375?focus=true
CC: 

### Description

This PR adds a mechanism to detect when an ad click opens a native app on iOS and closes the resulting empty sketchy tab in DuckDuckGo.

- Introduces `AdClickExternalOpenDetector` to track navigation state and background events to trigger tab closure.
- Integrates the detector into `TabViewController` with lifecycle hooks (startNavigation, finishNavigation, failNavigation) and a mitigation handler that calls closeTab().
- Updates the Xcode project to include the new detector source and reorganize related AdAttribution files.

### Testing Steps

1. Install Amazon/Ebay app.
2. Ensure "Open links in external apps" setting is set in iOS DDG settings (by default it is). 
3. Search for something (tshirt, dress, book etc, suggestion: "Bluetooth speaker") that will show on SERP with an Amazon/Ebay ad.
4. Tap on the app.
5. Go back to DDG
6. The only visible tab should be SERP with the correct URL/Search text

### Impact and Risks & What could go wrong?

The mitigation action closes the new tab that currently is empty and shows the sketchy URL, if the detection heuristic is not correct we could close a valid tab.

---

title: [macOS] SAD/ATT Prompts - Pixels
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210257532277828
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

This PR adds the Pixel implementation for SAD/ATT prompts. 

### Testing Steps
1. Ensure CI is green.

Prerequisites:
Ensure to return `true` in `isDefaultBrowserAndDockPromptFeatureEnabled` defined in `DefaultBrowserAndDockPromptFeatureFlagger`

**Scenario 1 - Popover**
1. Launch the App.
2. Open the 'Debug Menu' → 'SAD/ATT Prompts’ and check the popover show date. 
3. Click ‘Override Today’s Date’ and change the date to match that. 
4. Focus outside the window and focus again. 
5. The SAD/ATT popover is prompted.
6. Ensure that the "m_mac_set-as-default-add-to-dock_popover-shown” is fired.
7. Click the ’Not Now’ button.
8. Ensure the "m_mac_set-as-default-add-to-dock_popover-cancel-action” is fired.
9. Repeat the test and click the confirmation button and ensure that the "m_mac_set-as-default-add-to-dock_popover-confirm-action” is fired.
10. Check that the different content type (both set as default and add to dock, set as default only, add to dock only) reflect the “contentType” parameter correct values “set-as-default-and-add-to-dock”,, “set-as-default”, “add-to-dock”.

**Scenario 2 - Banner**
1. Launch the App.
2. Open the 'Debug Menu' → 'SAD/ATT Prompts’ and check the popover show date. 
3. Click ‘Override Today’s Date’ and change the date to match that. 
4. Focus outside the window and focus again.
5. Click the ’Not Now’ button.
6. Open the 'Debug Menu' → 'SAD/ATT Prompts’ and check banner show date.
7. Click ‘Override Today’s Date’ and change the date to match that. 
8. Focus outside the window and focus again.
9. The SAD/ATT banner is prompted.
10. Ensure that the "m_mac_set-as-default-add-to-dock_banner-shown" pixel is fired.
11. Click the “x” button to dismiss.
12. Ensure that the “m_mac_set-as-default-add-to-dock_banner-cancel-action” is fired.

**Scenario 3 - Banner Number of Impressions**

title: Add feature discovery pixels to Settings
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1210435912253590?focus=true

### Description
This change adds daily pixels to measure displaying settings panes, and a few unique pixels to
learn about discovery of website zoom, browser theme and data clearing features.
This change also introduces a new mode of sending pixels which is "daily without standard/count”
but using `_daily` suffix that is now preferred by the Privacy Team over `_d` suffix.
The pre-existing “daily” mode was renamed as “legacyDailyNoSuffix” and its usage was
updated appropriately.

title: More flakey sync test fixes
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205237866452338/task/1210451347360805?focus=true

### Description

These test were flaking out. They worked on my machine initially, also worked by fluke on CI on my PR, then started failing on main.

I initially merged another PR which attempted to reduce the number of async waits. I even continued to think that was where the issue was here and stopped using some helpers which depended on `XCTExpectations`. However, it hit me that in fact the reason was likely that we're trying to compare two base64 code generated from a serialised `SyncCode.RecoveryKey` when in fact, they could differ because of variations in the order of the JSON KV pairs. This passed on the first try so I'm hoping that this resolves the issue

Green CI

title: Fix location permissions popover not showing up
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1210431866798492?focus=true

### Description

Fixes an issue where the location permission popover isn't coming up correctly.

### Testing Steps

1. Delete the debug build from /Applications/Debug so location permissions are reset for it.  You can check in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services: our debug build shouldn't show up there anymore.
2. Run our debug build and open "https://thetest.com/tests/permissions"
3. Click on "Location: Prompt"
4. Ensure you see the location request popover.
5. Reload the page, do it again.
6. Ensure you see the location request popover.

### Impact and Risks

Low.

#### What could go wrong?

This is already a high priority issue, so we can't really break it "more".

### Quality Considerations

If multiple location prompts are showing up, then only the latest one to be requested will show the popover automatically.  Looking at the code this seems to be by design.

### Notes to Reviewer

NA

body:

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206226850447395/task/1210454132810101
Tech Design URL:
CC: @amddg44 

### Description

Uses value established at launch instead of live feature flag. This prevents prematurely showing visual updates remote message that's based on `visualUpdates` subfeature, in case when the visual updates are not yet applied at runtime (app was not relaunched).

### Testing Steps
1. Run the app, override the remote config with `https://www.jsonblob.com/api/1379474116607926272` (visualUpdates flag enabled)
2. In Debug -> Remote Messaging reset all to start with a clean state.
3. Override RMF config to https://staticcdn.duckduckgo.com/remotemessaging/config/staging/pre/ios-config.json (visual updates message from https://github.com/duckduckgo/remote-messaging-config/pull/189)
4. In Debug -> Remote Messaging there should only be duck.ai message logged.
5. Go to Home Screen and dismiss the duck.ai message if you haven't done it already.
6. Restart the app
7. New UI should be enabled and message visible on New Tab Page.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
RMF could be affected by filtering. For tests I used config with another Remote Message so that this can be validated.

title: macOS: Disable VPN login items on expired subscriptions even if they are manually disabled by the user
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203108348835387/task/1210470416862601?focus=true

### Description

We want to disable the VPN login item when the subscription is expired even if the login item was manually disabled by the user in System Settings.  This helps ensure the VPN menu app won't load when enabled back by the user.

### Testing Steps

1. Connect the VPN so login items are loaded.
2. Disconnect it.
3. Restart the app, ensure the login items are restarted but not disabled.
4. Force [this](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/06a80cdad3e04dc878cc096e4179be5a823a4869/macOS/DuckDuckGo/Waitlist/VPNFeatureGatekeeper.swift#L62) to return false.
5. Go to System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions, and disable our login item
6. Start the App again
7. Go to System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions, and enable our login item.
8. Make sure it's not loaded.

### Impact and Risks

Low

#### What could go wrong?

It's unlikely this change could affect anything.  The enabling and  disabling login items is a fairly lightweight process.

### Quality Considerations

NA

### Notes to Reviewer

NA

title: Refactor FireCoordinator into AppDelegate’s property
body:
# Background
FireCoordinator is a small class with fully-static API. In order to improve testability we should rewrite the static API into non-static, but only keep 1 instance of the coordinator around.

# Objective
* Refactor FireCoordinator’s static API into non-static
* Make FireCoordinator an instance of AppDelegate so that it’s accessible via `NSApp.delegateTyped.fireCoordinator` or `Application.appDelegate.fireCoordinator`
* Refactor FireCoordinator usage across the macOS app so that it uses AppDelegate’s instance.

title: Remove PermissionManager singleton and refactor FireCoordinator from static to instance-based API
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1210503547471270

### Description:
This change refactors the `FireCoordinator` static API to an instance-based approach.
FireCoordinator is now an instance property of `AppDelegate`, accessible via `NSApp.delegateTyped.fireCoordinator`
or `Application.appDelegate.fireCoordinator`, and injected into objects that use it via initializer.
Also the PermissionManager singleton was removed and replaced with a property in AppDelegate.

### Steps to test
1. Verify that CI is green
2. Verify that [UI tests workflow](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/15552120156) is green.
3. Smoke test [the review build](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/15552135588).

---
This PR refactors `FireCoordinator` to improve testability by converting its static API to an instance-based approach while maintaining a single coordinator instance accessible through `AppDelegate`.

## Changes Made

### Core Refactoring
- **Converted static API to instance API**: Removed `static` keywords from `fireViewModel`, `firePopover`, `fireButtonAction()`, and `showFirePopover()` methods
- **Added FireCoordinator property to AppDelegate**: Added `let fireCoordinator = FireCoordinator()` as a property of `AppDelegate`
- **Updated all usage sites**: Replaced all static calls with instance access via `NSApp.delegateTyped.fireCoordinator.*` or `Application.appDelegate.fireCoordinator.*`

### Files Updated (9 total)
- `FireCoordinator.swift`: Converted from static to instance-based class
- `AppDelegate.swift`: Added fireCoordinator property and updated internal usage
- `MainWindowController.swift`: Updated fireViewModel access pattern
- `MainMenuActions.swift`: Updated 5 fire-related menu actions
- `HistoryBurning.swift`: Updated async fire access closure
- `FireViewController.swift`: Updated fireViewModel access pattern
- `OnboardingFireButtonDialogViewModel.swift`: Updated fireButtonAction call
- `DefaultRecentActivityActionsHandler.swift`: Updated async fire access closure
- `ContextualDaxDialogFactoryIntegrationTests.swift`: Updated test firePopover access

## Benefits

- **Improved testability**: FireCoordinator can now be injected as a dependency for unit testing
- **Single instance pattern**: Maintains exactly one FireCoordinator instance managed by AppDelegate
- **Consistent access patterns**: All access goes through well-defined AppDelegate properties
- **Zero functional changes**: Purely structural improvement with no behavioral modifications

## Usage Examples

```swift
// Before (static API)
FireCoordinator.fireButtonAction()
FireCoordinator.fireViewModel.fire.burnAll()

// After (instance API via AppDelegate)
NSApp.delegateTyped.fireCoordinator.fireButtonAction()
NSApp.delegateTyped.fireCoordinator.fireViewModel.fire.burnAll()

// Alternative access pattern
Application.appDelegate.fireCoordinator.fireViewModel.fire
```

Fixes #980.

### Description

Apply a workaround for the iOS 18.4 and 18.5 simulator linking issue.

For convenience, I've attached a copy of the script at the bottom of the description.

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Check that the simulator builds and runs for 18.3 (or 18.3.1)
2. Now do a clean build and try the same for 18.4
3. Finally, do another clean build and test 18.5 

### Impact and Risks
<!-- 
What's the impact on users if something goes wrong?

High: Could affect user privacy, lose user data, break core functionality
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features
None: Internal tooling, documentation
-->

#### What could go wrong?
<!-- Describe specific scenarios and how you've addressed them -->

In theory this change is safe since it only affects the simulator, and only two versions of iOS. Worst case the build will fail, but that's already the case. :)

### Quality Considerations
<!-- 
Focus on what matters for your changes:
- What edge cases exist?
- How does this affect performance?
- What monitoring have you added?
- What documentation needs updating?
- How does this impact privacy/security?
-->

### Notes to Reviewer
<!-- Anything specific you want reviewers to focus on -->

---

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
###############################################################################
#
# Several simulator runtimes (18.4, 18.5, 26.0) ship without the Swift
# overlay libswiftWebKit.dylib. This script copies the missing dylib from the
# runtime into $BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR so the app can launch under those sims.
# Delete the script once Apple ships corrected runtimes.
###############################################################################
set -euo pipefail

readonly DYLIB_NAME="libswiftWebKit.dylib"

###############################################################################
# 1. Guard – run only for *iphonesimulator* builds
###############################################################################

if [[ "${PLATFORM_NAME:-}" != "iphonesimulator" ]]; then
    echo "ℹ️  Skipping $DYLIB_NAME workaround – PLATFORM_NAME='${PLATFORM_NAME:-unset}'"
    exit 0
fi

###############################################################################
# 2. Validate TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION is available
###############################################################################

if [[ -z "${TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    echo "❌ TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION environment variable is not set" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "ℹ️  Target device OS version: $TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION"

###############################################################################
# 3. Configuration for supported versions (Bash 3.x compatible)
###############################################################################

get_build_id_for_version() {
    case "$1" in
        18.4*) echo "22E238" ;;
        18.5*) echo "22F77" ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

get_runtime_dylib_path() {
    local version="$1"
    local build_id
    
    build_id="$(get_build_id_for_version "$version")" || return 1
    
    echo "/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Volumes/iOS_${build_id}/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Profiles/Runtimes/iOS ${version}.simruntime/Contents/Resources/RuntimeRoot/System/Cryptexes/OS/usr/lib/swift/$DYLIB_NAME"
}

###############################################################################
# 4. Check if workaround is needed and find the dylib
###############################################################################

find_matching_runtime() {
    local target_version="$1"
    local runtime_path
    
    runtime_path="$(get_runtime_dylib_path "$target_version")" || {
        return 1
    }
    
    if [[ -f "$runtime_path" ]]; then
        echo "$runtime_path"
        return 0
    else
        echo "⚠️  Runtime dylib not found at: $runtime_path" >&2
        echo "⚠️  Make sure iOS ${target_version%.*} simulator runtime is installed" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

RUNTIME_DYLIB="$(find_matching_runtime "$TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION")" || {
    echo "✅ Runtime iOS $TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION doesn't require $DYLIB_NAME workaround"
    exit 0
}

###############################################################################
# 5. Validate environment and paths
###############################################################################

if [[ -z "${BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR:-}" ]]; then
    echo "❌ BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR environment variable is not set" >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -d "$BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "❌ Build products directory does not exist: $BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
fi

###############################################################################
# 6. Copy the overlay into the build products directory
###############################################################################

DESTINATION="$BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR/$DYLIB_NAME"

# Skip if files are identical
if [[ -f "$DESTINATION" ]] && cmp -s "$RUNTIME_DYLIB" "$DESTINATION"; then
    echo "ℹ️  $DYLIB_NAME already exists and is identical"
    exit 0
fi

echo "🏗️  Copying $RUNTIME_DYLIB → $DESTINATION"

if /bin/cp -f "$RUNTIME_DYLIB" "$DESTINATION" && /bin/chmod 644 "$DESTINATION"; then
    echo "✅ Successfully applied $DYLIB_NAME workaround for iOS $TARGET_DEVICE_OS_VERSION"
else
    echo "❌ Failed to copy $DYLIB_NAME" >&2
    exit 1
fi
```

title: macOS: Update address bar Duck.ai and "x" button placement
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1210474744854326?focus=true

### Description

This PR swaps the position of the Duck.ai and “x” (cancel) buttons when the address bar has focus, so the “x” button is on the right and the Duck.ai button is on the left, closer to the address bar text.

#### Changes

1. Storyboard changes:
   * The bookmark, Duck.ai, and “x” buttons are now contained in a single stack view, to more easily reason about their placement in the address bar.
   * There are now two dividers (leading and trailing Duck.ai dividers) to separate the Duck.ai button from the other buttons when needed.
2. `AddressBarButtonsViewController` changes:
   * The “x” (cancel) button is now an `AddressBarButton` so we can set its position in `updateButtonsPosition()` (to control the background shape in its hover state).
   * We set the size of the cancel button in `setupButtonsSize()`, depending on whether the `visualRefresh` feature flag is enabled.
   * The logic for showing the dividers is updated in `updateAIChatDividerVisibility()` to handle each divider based on its related buttons.

### Testing Steps
1. In Settings > Duck.ai, enable the setting “Show Duck.ai shortcut in the address bar."
2. In a new tab, confirm only the Duck.ai button shows on the right side of the address bar.
3. Enter some text in the address bar and confirm the cancel button now shows to the right of the Duck.ai button, with a divider between them.
4. Visit a website that isn’t bookmarked and confirm only the Duck.ai button shows on the right side of the address bar.
5. Hover over the address bar and confirm the bookmark button now shows to the left of the Duck.ai button, with a divider between them.
6. Visit a website that is bookmarked and confirm the bookmark button shows to the left of the Duck.ai button, with a divider between them.
7. Confirm that toggling the focus on the address bar switches between showing the bookmark/Duck.ai button and showing the Duck.ai/cancel buttons in the expected positions.

Additional scenarios:
* Go to Debug > Feature Flag Overrides, disable the `visualRefresh` feature flag, and repeat the steps above to confirm the buttons are in the correct positions with the expected hover states.
* Go to Settings > Duck.ai, disable the setting “Show Duck.ai shortcut in the address bar," and repeat the steps above, confirming the Duck.ai button and dividers are not shown and the bookmark/cancel buttons always appear in the expected position on the right.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes

#### What could go wrong?
* Incorrect size/shape of buttons when `visualRefresh` feature flag is enabled/disabled. (Handled in `AddressBarButtonsViewController` and included in testing steps above.)
* Incorrect position of buttons or dividers when Duck.ai setting is enabled/disabled. (Handled in `AddressBarButtonsViewController` and included in testing steps above.)

title: macOS Visual Refresh: Only check for the FF once at AppDelegate.init
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210516955340220
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description
This PR optimizes the visual refresh feature implementation by improving performance and adding proper filtering for remote messages. The changes ensure that visual style checks are performed only at launch time instead of repeatedly throughout the app lifecycle, and that remote messages are only displayed to users who are actually seeing the new visual style.

**Key Changes:**
- **Performance Optimization**: Visual style is now determined once at launch rather than being checked repeatedly across all UI components
- **Remote Messaging Filtering**: Added logic to ensure remote messages related to visual updates are only shown to users with the new visual style enabled
- **Code Clarity**: Renamed `VisualStyleManager` to `VisualStyleDecider` for better semantic clarity
- **Testing**: Added comprehensive unit tests for the new remote messaging filtering logic

### Testing Steps

**Check the  Visual Updates are only applied at app launch**
1. You can add a breakpoint to the `DefaultVisualStyleDecider` line 129
2. Run the application, verify it gets called once from the `AppDelete.init`
3. Go to Debug -> Feature Flag Overrides -> and override the `visualUpdatesInternalOnly` and the `visualUpdates`
4. Open new windows, new tabs and play with the app. You should still see the current theme.
5. Close the app and re-open it.
6. Verify the new changes are applied.

**Verify the remote message is not shown if the FF is enabled but the user is seeing the legacy visuals**
1. Before running the application, change the `RemoteMessageClientConfiguration`, to return this in the DEBUG mode: `https://jsonblob.com/api/1380594945500569600`
2.Run the application
3. Go to Debug -> Feature Flag Overrides -> and override the `visualUpdatesInternalOnly` to false 
4. Restart the app to see the legacy view.
5. Go to Debug -> Feature Flag Overrides -> and override the `visualUpdates` to true
6. Go to Debug -> Remote Messaging Framework -> Reset Remote Messages
7. Go to Debug -> Remote Messaging Framework -> Refresh Config
5. You should not see the new RMF in the New Tab Page
8. Go to Debug -> Feature Flag Overrides -> and override the `visualUpdatesInternalOnly` to true again.
9. Restart the application, you should see the new theme
10. Follow steps 6 and 7
11.  You should see the remote message on NTP

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
1. **Visual inconsistencies**: If the style determination logic fails, some UI components might show mixed visual styles
   - *Mitigation*: The refactored code maintains the same decision logic, just moves the evaluation point to launch time. Extensive testing across all UI components has been done.

2. **Remote messages not showing**: The new filtering logic might be too restrictive and prevent legitimate messages from appearing
   - *Mitigation*: Added comprehensive unit tests to verify the filtering logic works correctly. The logic only affects visual-refresh-related messages.

3. **Performance regression**: Changes to the style checking mechanism could potentially impact performance
   - *Mitigation*: This is actually a performance improvement - checking style once at launch instead of repeatedly should reduce CPU usage.

### Quality Considerations
- **Performance Impact**: Positive - reduces repeated style checks throughout the app lifecycle by determining visual style once at launch
- **Edge Cases**: 
  - Internal users vs external users (handled by existing `InternalUserDecider`)
  - Feature flag state changes (requires app restart, which is expected behavior)
  - Mixed visual styles across components (prevented by centralized style determination)
- **Testing**: Added unit tests specifically for `RemoteMessagingConfigMatcherProvider` to verify the new filtering logic
- **Monitoring**: No additional monitoring needed - existing remote messaging analytics will capture message display metrics
- **Privacy/Security**: No impact - this is purely a UI optimization and filtering enhancement

### Notes to Reviewer
- Pay special attention to the remote messaging filtering logic in `RemoteMessagingConfigMatcherProvider.swift` (lines ~184-190)
- The performance improvement comes from replacing multiple `visualStyleManager.style` checks throughout the codebase with a single determination at launch
- The rename from `VisualStyleManager` to `VisualStyleDecider` better reflects that this class decides/determines style rather than manages it
- New unit tests provide good coverage of the edge cases for the remote messaging filtering

title: [iOS] Onboarding - Picture in Picture controller logic
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1108686900785972/task/1210454186090911
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

This PR refactors the VideoPlayer logic to support Picture In Picture (PiP).
It does not contain the logic weather to present PiP or not.

### Testing Steps
**Prerequisites**: Need to be tested on a real device.

**Scenario 1 - Set Default Browser Picture In Picture**
1. Install a fresh build or use Debug Menu.
2. Launch onboarding and get to the browser comparisons screen.
4. Tap the "Choose Your Browser” button.
5. Ensure the app deeplinks into the settings and a Picture in Picture video tutorial is presented on screen and it loops.
6. Ensure that both the <- DuckDuckGo button and the PIP button on the video launch the app and the “Add to Dock” onboarding screen is presented (iPhone).

**Scenario 2 - Background the App on Browser comparison chart**
1. Install a fresh build or use Debug Menu.
2. Launch onboarding and get to the browser comparisons screen.
4. Background and foreground the app multiple times.
5. Ensure that the video and PiP do not start.

**Scenario 3 - Ensure that Add To Dock Video does not play in PIP**
1. Install a fresh build or use Debug Menu.
2. Launch onboarding and get to the browser comparisons screen.
4. Tap the “Skip” button.
5. The “Add to Dock” onboarding screen should appear.
6. Tap the “Show me How” button.
7. Ensure the video plays and it loops.
8. Send the app to the background.
9. Ensure no PiP is visible and that the video pauses.

title: Add dynamic “Complete Your Setup” section to Settings screen
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210410396636449?focus=true Tech Design URL: CC: ### Description Adds new section to the top of the Settings screen with the options to set the browser as default and to import passwords (if certain conditions are met). This is behind a feature flag and may only be a short-lived change, depending on metrics. Rules: 1/ Users can swipe to hide either option. If both options are dismissed, we will hide the entire section. 2/ If a user taps “Default Browser,” we’ll check if we are the Default Browser when they first return to our Settings. - If set as default, we'll move the Default Browser setting back to Protections. - If not, we'll keep the Default Browser option until users import or add =< 25 passwords. 3/ The import option will be automatically removed once users import or add =< 25 passwords ### Testing Steps 1. Testing on device, with less than 25 passwords saved 2. Go to the Settings screen and confirm the “Complete Your Setup” section is not present 3. From the Debug > Feature Flags screen, enable flag `showSettingsCompleteSetupSection` 4. Swipe down to dismiss and re-open Settings, confirming the “Complete Your Setup” section is now present (as you have < than 25 passwords saved) 5. Swipe “Set As Default Browser” and tap the hide icon. Confirm the row is removed from this section and that “Default Browser” is back in it’s usual position under “Privacy Protections” 6. Swipe “Import Passwords” and tap the hide icon. Confirm the “Complete Your Setup” section is gone 7. Go to the bottom of the Debug screen and tap “Reset Settings > Complete Setup” to reset state 8. Add enough passwords so that you have 25+ saved (can use Debug > Autofill > Add Test Autofill Data as shortcut) 9. Go back to Settings and confirm the “Complete Your Setup” section is not present (now that you have >= 25 passwords saved) 10. Delete all passwords and repeat step 7 to reset state. 11. Tap “Import Passwords”, complete an import and confirm the entire “Complete Your Setup” section is removed after importing any amount of data 12. Repeat step 10 13. Tap “Set As Default Browser” and ensure DDG is set as the default browser 14. Come back to Settings and confirm the “Set As Default Browser” row is removed from the “Complete Your Setup” section (and that “Default Browser” is back in it’s usual position under “Privacy Protections”) 15. Repeat step 7 to reset state 16. Tap “Set As Default Browser” and choose any other app than DDG as the default browser 17. Come back to Settings and confirm “Set As Default Browser” is still present in the “Complete Your Setup” section ### Impact and Risks Low: minor visual update that is behind a feature flag — ###### Internal references: [Definition of Done](https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207634633537039/f) | [Engineering Expectations](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/199064865822552) | [Tech Design Template](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/184709971311943)

title: macOS Duck.ai Sidebar: 4. Support for state restoration, sidebar on pinned tabs and moved between windows, placement param
body:

Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209671977594486/task/1210012482760771?focus=true
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209671977594486/task/1210354678311517?focus=true
CC: @Bunn 

### Description
This PR adds:
-  support for state restoration and expand button via `chatID` URL parameter (only when saving recent chats is enabled)
- better in-memory model for representing open sidebars allowing to consistent behaviour of sidebars in pinned tabs and on tabs moved between different windows
- when Duck.ai is loaded in the sidebar a `placement=sidebar` is added to the URL, and when opened in a new tab the parameter is stripped

### Testing Steps
**I. State restoration (depends on pending FE changes that add `chatID` URL parameter)**
1. Ensure that restoring tabs from previous session is enabled in settings
2. Open multiple tabs with websites
3. Reveal Duck.ai sidebar and start new or load previous conversation
4. Repeat 2. for different tabs
5. Close the app
6. Open the app
7. Check if sidebars is open on the tabs where it was before closing the app and the same conversation is loaded

**I. Expand button (depends on pending FE changes that add `chatID` URL parameter**
1. Open Duck.ai sidebar on a tab with website
2. Click expand button
3. Check if new tab was open with the Duck.ai and it loaded correctly previous conversation 

**III. Pinned tabs**
1. Open Duck.ai sidebar on a tab with website
2. Pin the tab with sidebar
3. Check if sidebar's state remained unchanged with the same conversation loaded
4. Unpin the tab with sidebar
5. Check if sidebar's state remained unchanged with the same conversation loaded
6. Check the same for both pinned tab settings: "global" and "per window"

**IV. Sidebar on a tab moved between windows**
1. Open Duck.ai sidebar on a tab with website
2. Drag the tab to another window
3. Check if sidebar's state remained unchanged with the same conversation loaded
4. Drag the tab back to previous window
5. Check if sidebar's state remained unchanged with the same conversation loaded

**V. Sidebar loads URL that includes `placement=sidebar`**
1. Open Duck.ai sidebar on a tab with website
2. Inspect the URL of the sidebar and confirm it includes `placement=sidebar`
3. Using expand button open the conversation in a new tab
4. Check the URL and confirm that the `placement=sidebar` was removed from the URL

### Impact and Risks 
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features


#### What could go wrong?
All changes gated by internal-only feature flag 

### Notes to Reviewer
Most of the changes to be tested require FE changes to dynamically update Duck.ai with `chatID` parameter added to URL and also support loading previous conversation based on presence of that parameter.

title: Fix update expiration bug and increase update expiration frequency
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203108348835387/task/1210473306220879?focus=true

### Description

This PR:
- Fixed a bug with the expiration logic that was causing downloads to be interrupted.
- Reduce the time for a build to expire (1 hour for internal users, 24 hours for public users).

### Testing Steps

1. Modify BuildNumber.xcconfig to set a low build number like `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 400`
2. Launch the app
3. [OPTIONAL] If you want to test automatic updates, make sure you enable feature flag Updates > `autoUpdateInDEBUG`
4. Go to Settings > About and ensure you see an update available.  Feel free to install it if you're on manual updates, but don't click "Restart to Update"
5. Make sure you're an internal user
6. Once the update is downloaded, go to System Settings > Date & Time, and move the time forward 45 minutes.
7. Go back to the app, alt+tab a few times, and make sure you are still shown the same update.
8. Go to System Settings > Date & Time, and move the time forward 61 minutes.
9. Go back to the app, alt+tab a few times, and make sure the update is expired / re-offered / re-downloaded.

Re-test as an external user but using 24 hours as the threshold.

### Impact and Risks

Low

#### What could go wrong?

The time expiration logic could be off and cause trouble, but it's easy to test with the provided steps.

### Quality Considerations

Worst case scenario we can turn this off making a hotfix, but to be honest this has been live internally for a while and we haven't seen any issues.

title: macOS: Convert Freemium PIR from Experiment to Full Feature (PR # 1)
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210613732778386
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/481882893211075/task/1210585101748756

### Description
This PR (1 of 2) implements the core changes to convert Freemium PIR from an experiment to a full feature. Core changes here are:
1. Remove all experiment-related code and convert experiment pixels to feature pixels
2. Iterate on `FreemiumDBPFeature`, improving eligibility checks and observation of dependencies.
3. Update more options menu UI, separating Privacy Pro and Freemium items
4. Add `areProductsAvailablePublisher` and `canPurchasePublisher` (and related plumbing) to propagate product availability 
5. Convert non-localized strings to localized (translations will follow in a separate PR) 

### Testing Prerequisites
1. Remove any subscription
2. Reset any previous Freemium state -> Debug Menu -> Freemium -> `Reset all Freemium Feature State`
3. Set Feature Flag override -> Debug Menu -> Freemium -> `Override Feature Flag -> ON`
4. Set Storefront override -> Debug Menu -> Freemium -> `Override Storefront -> USA`
5. Relaunch

### Testing Steps
##### Test 1 - Freemium Entry Points
1. Launch the browser
2. Ensure the new tab and more options menu Freemium entry points are visible (New tab shows a `Personal Information Removal` banner, more options menu shows a `Personal Information Scan` item under the `Privacy Pro` entry)

Screenshot here -> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84bde1a7-832e-4ad0-9b07-16888e8ffc46

##### Test 2 - Accessing Freemium
1. Tap the new tab banner button and ensure the Freemium PIR page opens
2. Close it
3. Tap the more options menu `Personal Information Scan` and ensure the Freemium PIR page opens

Screenshot here -> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/522d5315-fa18-4f0e-a5e7-2f611663c99f

##### Test 3 - Run a scan and get new tab results banner
1. On the Freemium PIR page, tap `Start Your Free Scan` and follow the instructions to start a scan
2. Ensure a scan starts (if it does not check your system settings for login items, and check that the debug app has the 
needed entitlements)
3. Wait for the scan to complete
4. Relaunch the browser
5. Ensure you see a banner on the new tab page displaying scan results
9. Tap the view results button and ensure it opens the Freemium PIR page

##### Test 4 - Freemium Unavailable
1. Reset the Feature Flag and Storefront overrides previously set via Debug menu -> `Reset …Override`
10. Reset any previous Freemium state -> Debug Menu -> Freemium -> `Reset all Freemium Feature State` 
11. Relaunch the browser
12. Ensure the new tab and more options menu Freemium items are not present

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt PIR

#### What could go wrong?
Users who are not eligible for Freemium PIR could see it as a feature.

title: Auto-Clear alignment with Windows
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1148564399326804/task/1210331857638286?focus=true

### Description
Alignment of Auto-Clear behavior on macOS with the Windows platform. This includes:

- Preserving the session restoration setting when Auto-Clear is enabled 
- Updating the warning message below the session restoration toggle to: "Your session won't be restored if data is cleared when exiting."
- Ensuring that if a user chooses not to burn on exit and session restoration is enabled, their session is restored accordingly

### Testing Steps
**Test label presentation**
1. Go to duck://settings/dataClearing
2. Enable Auto-Clear
3. Go to duck://settings/general
4. Set "Open a new Window" for "On Startup"
5. Verify there is no info dialog
6. Set "Reopen all windows from last session"
7. Verify there is an info dialog saying "Your session won't be restored if data is cleared when exiting."
8. Make sure clicking on "Open Data Clearing Settings" brings you to duck://settings/dataClearing

**Test session restoration logic**
1. Open bunch of tabs
2. Apply this Setting: Disable session restoration ("Open a new Window"), enable Auto-Clear, disable Auto-Clear warning 
4. Quit and reopen the app.
5. Verify that session isn't restored and data are cleared

Repeat the test with following Setting configurations: 
A) Session restoration enabled, Auto-Clear enabled, Auto-Clear warning disabled
B) Session restoration disabled, Auto-Clear enabled, Auto-Clear warning enabled
When quitting the app, select "Clear and Quit"
C) Session restoration enabled, Auto-Clear enabled, Auto-Clear warning enabled
When quitting the app, select "Clear and Quit"
_In all previous tests, session must not be restored and data have to be cleared_


1. Repeat test with configuration B but select "Quit without Clearing"
2. Make sure that session isn't restored when reopening the app but browsing data are preserved



1. Repeat the test with configuration C but select "Quit without Clearing" 
2. Make sure that session is restored when reopening the app and also browsing data are preserved


### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
Session restoration

https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1200194497630846/task/1210592290522867?focus=true

## Description
This PR adds comprehensive GitHub Actions workflow management rules and PR creation guidelines to improve developer productivity and prevent common CI/CD issues encountered during workflow automation.

The changes include:
- **GitHub Actions Rules**: Complete reference for all 38 workflows with categorization, CLI pager fixes, branch targeting safety, and agent automation guidelines
- **PR Creation Guidelines**: Updated with username branch naming convention (username/feature-name format) and comprehensive template structure

## Testing Steps

### 1. Test Cursor Prompts for GitHub Actions
Test that these natural language requests work correctly with the new rules:

**Workflow Triggering:**
- "run gha notarized build" → Should trigger `macos_build_notarized.yml` on current branch
- "make notarized build with gha" → Should use proper branch targeting and parameters
- "trigger ios testflight build" → Should use `ios_release.yml` with correct destination
- "run macos ui tests" → Should trigger testing workflows properly

**Branch Management:**
- "add new #feature# branch" → Should create branch with username prefix (alex/feature-name)
- "create branch for new feature" → Should follow username/description format
- "checkout new branch from main" → Should use proper naming convention

**Monitoring and Status:**
- "check workflow status" → Should use `gh run list | cat` to avoid pager issues
- "what's the build status" → Should provide clean, readable output
- "monitor the build" → Should use proper run viewing commands

### 2. Test GitHub CLI Reliability
Verify the documented fixes work:
- Run `gh run list --limit 5 | cat` → Should work without "head: |:" errors
- Run `gh run view RUN_ID | cat` → Should display clean output
- Test workflow triggering with `--ref $(git branch --show-current)`

### 3. Verify Branch Naming Convention
- Confirm this branch follows `alex/improve-github-actions-rules` format
- Test that PR creation prompts include username prefix guidance
- Verify examples in documentation are clear and actionable

### 4. Agent Automation Testing
Test that AI agents can reliably:
- Always check current branch before triggering workflows
- Use proper `| cat` commands to prevent pager issues
- Target the correct branch with `--ref` parameters
- Follow the complete workflow reference for any of the 38 available workflows

## Impact
**Medium Impact** - Improves developer tooling and cursor prompt reliability

**Benefits:**
- Enables reliable natural language workflow triggering
- Prevents CI/CD errors from unclear automation
- Standardizes branch naming to prevent conflicts
- Fixes GitHub CLI pager issues that cause command failures
- Provides comprehensive automation guidelines for cursor/AI interactions

title: Refactor favicon logic into TabContent+DisplayedFavicon extension
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1202406491309510/task/1210582984664837?focus=true
Tech Design URL: 
CC: 

### Description

Refactors favicon logic that was duplicated between `TabViewModel` and `PinnedTabView` into a centralized `TabContent+DisplayedFavicon` extension. This eliminates ~50 lines of duplicated code while preserving all existing behavior.

**Problem**: The same complex favicon determination logic existed in two places:
- `TabViewModel.updateFavicon()` and `errorFaviconToShow()` methods  
- `PinnedTabView.faviconImage` computed property

**Solution**: Created a single `TabContent.displayedFavicon()` method that handles all favicon scenarios including error states, special content types, special URLs, and feature flag considerations.

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->

**Prerequisites**: 
- Clean DuckDuckGo browser installation
- Access to various test sites (HTTP/HTTPS, certificate errors, etc.)

**Test Scenarios**:

1. **Regular Tab Favicons**:
   - Open new tabs and navigate to various websites
   - Verify favicons load correctly in tab bar
   - Expected: Same behavior as before

2. **Pinned Tab Favicons**:
   - Pin several tabs with different content types
   - Navigate to sites with favicons
   - Expected: Pinned tabs show correct favicons

3. **Error State Favicons**:
   - Navigate to site with invalid SSL certificate
   - Expected: Red alert circle icon appears
   - Visit malicious site (test URL)
   - Expected: Red alert circle icon appears
   - Simulate web content process crash
   - Expected: Orange alert circle icon appears

4. **Special Content Type Favicons**:
   - Open Settings tab
   - Expected: Settings multicolor icon
   - Open Bookmarks tab  
   - Expected: Bookmarks folder icon
   - Open History tab (if feature enabled)
   - Expected: History favicon
   - Open AI Chat
   - Expected: AI Chat icon

5. **Special URL Favicons**:
   - Navigate to DuckPlayer URL
   - Expected: DuckPlayer icon overrides site favicon
   - Navigate to AI Chat URL
   - Expected: AI Chat icon appears
   - Navigate to Email Protection URL
   - Expected: Email Protection icon appears

6. **Burner Tab Behavior**:
   - Enable Burner Mode
   - Open new tab
   - Expected: Fire icon (new style) or burner favicon (old style)

7. **Cross-Platform Verification**:
   - Test all scenarios on macOS
   - Verify no behavior differences from before refactoring

### Impact and Risks

**Impact Level: Low** - Pure refactoring with no user-facing behavior changes

#### What could go wrong?

**Scenario 1: Favicon Logic Discrepancy**
- Risk: Subtle differences in favicon selection between old and new implementation
- Impact: Users see wrong favicons or missing icons
- Mitigation: Comprehensive testing of all scenarios, line-by-line logic verification

**Scenario 2: Import/Module Issues**  
- Risk: Build failures or runtime crashes due to incorrect imports
- Impact: App crashes or compilation failures
- Mitigation: Build verification, proper module imports tested

**Scenario 3: Memory/Performance Regression**
- Risk: New extension method could have different performance characteristics
- Impact: UI lag or memory issues
- Mitigation: Same underlying logic, no additional object creation

**Scenario 4: Test Coverage Gaps**
- Risk: Missing edge cases in new centralized logic
- Impact: Bugs in specific favicon scenarios
- Mitigation: Preserved all existing logic paths, comprehensive test scenarios

### Quality Considerations

**Code Quality**:
- ✅ Eliminates 50+ lines of duplicated code
- ✅ Single source of truth for favicon logic
- ✅ Improved testability with pure function approach
- ✅ Better maintainability - future changes only need to be made once
- ✅ Follows DuckDuckGo architecture patterns (MVVM, extension organization)

**Performance**:
- ✅ No performance impact - same logic, better organization
- ✅ No additional object allocation
- ✅ Same method call overhead as before

**Privacy/Security**:
- ✅ No changes to privacy behavior
- ✅ Same error handling for certificate/security issues
- ✅ Preserved all security-related favicon indicators

**Compatibility**:
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing APIs
- ✅ All existing method signatures preserved
- ✅ No impact on external dependencies

**Edge Cases Handled**:
- ✅ Certificate errors and malicious site detection
- ✅ Feature flag-based favicon selection (History view)
- ✅ Burner mode considerations for new tab favicons
- ✅ Special URL detection (DuckPlayer, AI Chat, Email Protection)
- ✅ Fallback behavior when no favicon available

**Documentation**:
- ✅ Comprehensive method documentation with parameters
- ✅ Clear code organization with MARK comments
- ✅ Preserved existing inline comments

### Notes to Reviewer

**Key Areas to Focus On**:
- **Error State Handling**: This was the most complex logic to preserve - please verify red/orange alert circles appear correctly for certificate errors, malicious sites, and web content crashes
- **Feature Flag Integration**: The History view favicon depends on `.historyView` feature flag - ensure this still works
- **Special URL Detection**: DuckPlayer, AI Chat, and Email Protection URLs should override normal favicons

**Architecture Decision**:
- Chose to extend `TabContent` rather than create a separate service because favicon selection is inherently tied to the content type
- Method signature allows for dependency injection of error and favicon parameters rather than accessing tab properties directly

**Known Limitations**:
- Extension requires `MaliciousSiteProtection` import - this is consistent with other tab-related files
- Two identical files exist (Model and ViewModel directories) - keeping both for now pending clarification on preferred location

**Testing Approach**:
- Focused on behavior preservation rather than implementation testing
- All test scenarios designed to catch regressions in favicon display logic

title: Restore BWIntegration Objective-C implementation as local package
body:
Task/Issue URL:https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1210594346730347?focus=true
CC: @tomasstrba

### Description

Restores BWIntegration Objective-C implementation by moving it from the main macOS project to the CommonObjCExtensions local package. This change reorganizes the Bitwarden encryption functionality into a proper local package structure while maintaining all existing functionality.

**Key Changes:**
- Moved BWEncryption from Swift to Objective-C implementation in CommonObjCExtensions local package
- Added forward declarations for OpenSSL types in header files to maintain clean public interface
- Created BWEncryptionOutput.m implementation file with proper copyright
- Updated Package.swift with appropriate C settings for Objective-C compilation
- Maintained compatibility with existing OpenSSL framework from main project

### Testing Steps

1. Build the DuckDuckGoDBPBackgroundAgent target in Debug configuration
2. Validate Bitwarden integration works end-to-end:
   - Test Bitwarden app detection and connection
   - Verify password sharing between DuckDuckGo and Bitwarden
   - Test encryption/decryption of shared keys
   - Confirm autofill functionality works with Bitwarden passwords
3. Test BWEncryption functionality (RSA key generation, AES encryption/decryption, HMAC computation)
4. Verify no regression in existing Bitwarden password manager integration workflows

### Impact and Risks

Impact Level: Medium - This affects the Bitwarden integration architecture and build system

#### What could go wrong?

- **Bitwarden integration fails**: The most critical risk is that moving the encryption code could break the communication between DuckDuckGo and Bitwarden
- **Build failures**: If Package.swift configuration is incorrect, compilation could fail
- **Runtime encryption issues**: Forward declarations or linking problems could cause encryption/decryption to fail
- **Performance impact**: Minor impact from Swift to Objective-C conversion

**Mitigation**: Thorough testing of complete Bitwarden integration workflow, maintaining identical API surface

### Quality Considerations

- **Architecture**: Follows proper local package structure with separate header/implementation files
- **Security**: Maintains same encryption functionality and security properties
- **Compatibility**: Preserves existing API for BWManager integration
- **Build system**: Uses proper Swift Package Manager conventions for C/Objective-C code
- **Code quality**: Follows DuckDuckGo copyright and formatting standards

### Notes to Reviewer

- This is primarily an architectural change to move BWIntegration to a local package
- The conversion to Objective-C was necessary for proper local package integration
- All existing Bitwarden functionality should be preserved
- Please verify that the Package.swift settings are appropriate for the local package structure

title: DuckDuckGo-Bitwarden integration doesn't work with DDG 1.143.0
body:
While addressing an incompatibility in Bitwarden 2025.5.X that was breaking the integration ([link to our issue](https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/issues/15104)), I discovered what appears to be a bug in DuckDuckGo Browser 1.143.0. With this version, the Bitwarden desktop app integration fails consistently across all Bitwarden versions I’ve tested. Reverting to DDG 1.142.0 restores functionality.

I've tested this against two Bitwarden versions:
- 2025.4.2, from [Github release](https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/releases/tag/desktop-mac-v2025.4.2)
- 2026.6.1 – the current release candidate, which includes a fix for the 2025.5.X issue, from [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/actions/runs/15767785930)

•	1.143.0 – fails with both Bitwarden versions. [Download link](https://staticcdn.duckduckgo.com/macos-desktop-browser/duckduckgo-1.143.0.458.dmg)

This is all tested on a MacOS 15.5 computer.

The issue I'm seeing is during the initial connection step with DDG 1.143.0. After clicking `Yes` on the Bitwarden popup, nothing happens:

Since the issue is reproducible only on DDG 1.143.0 and not on 1.142.0, it seems likely to be related to a change in DDG. I’m unsure how to investigate this further, any suggestions?

### Impact and Risks 
What's the impact on users if something goes wrong?
This refactoring affects configuration URL resolution but for production users, behavior should be identical since they don't have access to custom URL functionality.

#### What could go wrong?
1. Configuration Fetching Failures: If ConfigurationURLProvider dependency injection fails during app startup, production users could lose access to critical configurations:
- Privacy Configuration: Could disable tracker blocking and privacy protections
- Tracker Data Set: Could break content blocking rules
- Bloom Filters: Could affect HTTPS upgrade functionality
- Remote Messaging: Could prevent important app notifications
2. App Startup Crashes: Missing ConfigurationURLProvider in the dependency chain could cause crashes on app launch for all production users.
3. Silent Configuration Failures: If the provider returns incorrect URLs, production users might fetch stale or invalid configurations without obvious error symptoms.

### Notes to Reviewer
1. Verify Default URLs: Double-check that AppConfigurationURLProvider returns exactly the same URLs as before for all Configuration cases
2. Test Dependency Injection: Ensure ConfigurationURLProvider is properly created in both:
3. iOS/AppDependencyProvider (line 143)
4. macOS/AppDelegate (line 680)
5. Configuration Fetcher Integration: Verify that ConfigurationFetcher properly receives and uses the ConfigurationURLProvider dependency

title: Fix WebKit ResponsivenessTimer crash on app startup
body:
Task/Issue URL: <\!-- Please provide Asana task URL -->
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

This PR fixes a crash that occurs during app startup when `WKWebView` is created on a background thread. The crash manifests as a WebKit ResponsivenessTimer error.

The issue occurs in the static initialization chain:
- `SyncService.init` → `Favicons.shared` → `DefaultUserAgentManager.shared` → creates `WKWebView`

Since this initialization can happen on any thread during app launch, but `WKWebView` must be created on the main thread, the app crashes.

### Testing Steps
1. Build and run the app on a device or simulator
2. Force quit the app and launch it again multiple times
3. Verify the app launches successfully without crashing
4. Check that user agent functionality still works correctly (web pages load with proper user agent)

### Impact and Risks

**Impact Level: High** - This crash affects app startup and could prevent users from launching the app.

#### What could go wrong?
- If the main thread is blocked during startup, using `DispatchQueue.main.sync` could potentially cause a deadlock. However, this is unlikely as the initialization happens early in the app lifecycle before complex UI operations.
- The synchronous dispatch adds a small delay to initialization, but this is negligible compared to the crash prevention benefit.

### Quality Considerations
- **Edge cases**: The fix handles both main thread and background thread scenarios
- **Performance**: Minimal impact - only adds thread switching overhead when needed
- **Thread safety**: Ensures WebKit requirements are met by guaranteeing main thread execution

---

title: Add WiFi hotspot authorization permission system
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1202406491309510/task/1210940150727931?focus=true  
Tech Design URL:  
CC: @ayoy

## Description

Adds WiFi hotspot authorization permission system that detects captive portals and shows a permission dialog to users. When a navigation fails, the system tests to determine if the user is behind a captive portal. If detected, it shows a permission dialog allowing users to authorize access to the captive portal page, which opens in a popup window.

Key features:
- Hotspot detection service that monitors network connectivity
- Permission dialog system for user authorization
- Captive portal popup management with automatic closure
- Auto-reload of affected tabs when connectivity is restored
- Debug menu for testing with local test server endpoints
- Comprehensive test coverage for various scenarios

## Testing Steps

**Prerequisites:**
- Build and run DEBUG version of DuckDuckGo browser
- Feature flag `hotspotDetection` should be enabled for internal users
- Access Debug menu via **Debug → WiFi Hotspot Detection**

**Test Scenario 1: Basic Hotspot Detection with Debug Server**
1. Open Debug menu → **WiFi Hotspot Detection → Local Tests Server (Redirect to Hotspot)**
2. Verify tests server starts automatically (menu shows "Stop Tests Server [Running]")
3. Turn OFF WiFi completely
4. Navigate to `https://duckduckgo.com/?q=test+search`
5. **Expected:** Page fails to load AND permission dialog appears asking "Open WiFi authentication page"
6. Click **"Allow"** in permission dialog
7. **Expected:** Popup window opens showing redirect page with localhost:8085 URL
8. Turn ON WiFi and reconnect to network
9. In Debug menu, switch to **Local Tests Server (Success)**
10. **Expected:** Popup window closes automatically and original tab reloads with search results

**Test Scenario 2: Multiple Tabs Auto-Reload**
1. Debug menu → **Local Tests Server (Redirect to Hotspot)**, turn OFF WiFi
2. Open Tab 1: `https://duckduckgo.com/?q=tab1+search` → permission dialog appears, click "Allow", popup opens
3. Open Tab 2 and Tab 3 with different searches (tabs show error pages)
4. Close Tab 1 by clicking X button on tab (popup remains open)
5. Turn ON WiFi, then Debug menu → **Local Tests Server (Success)**
6. **Expected:** Popup closes AND both remaining tabs reload automatically

**Test Scenario 3: Permission Denial**
1. Debug menu → **Local Tests Server (Hotspot)**, turn OFF WiFi
2. Navigate to any site, permission dialog appears
3. Click **"Don't Allow"**
4. **Expected:** No popup opens, tab remains on error page
5. Reload page (Cmd+R) → permission dialog appears again (not permanently blocked)

**Test Scenario 4: Normal Browsing Unaffected**
1. Debug menu → **Local Tests Server (Hotspot)**, ensure WiFi connected
2. Navigate to `https://duckduckgo.com/?q=normal+search`, `https://example.com`, `https://github.com`
3. **Expected:** All pages load normally with NO permission dialogs

**Test Scenario 5: Server vs Network Errors**
1. Debug menu → **Local Tests Server (Failure)**, WiFi connected
2. Navigate to any site → **Expected:** Server error response with NO permission dialog
3. Debug menu → **Local Tests Server (Hotspot)**, turn OFF WiFi
4. Navigate to any site → **Expected:** Network failure AND permission dialog appears

**Test Scenario 6: HTTP Errors Don't Trigger Detection**
1. Debug menu → **Firefox** (normal endpoint), WiFi connected
2. Navigate to `https://duckduckgo.com/nonexistent-page-404`, `https://httpstat.us/500`
3. **Expected:** HTTP errors (404, 500) with NO permission dialogs

**Alternative Real Network Testing:**
1. Connect to actual WiFi network with captive portal (hotel, airport, cafe)
2. Debug menu → **Firefox** (real endpoint)
3. Navigate to `https://duckduckgo.com`
4. **Expected:** Permission dialog appears, click "Allow", captive portal opens in popup
5. Complete authentication → popup closes and original tab reloads

## Impact and Risks

**Impact Level: Medium** - New feature that affects user workflows when connecting to networks with captive portals.

#### What could go wrong?

* **False positives**: Network issues could trigger hotspot detection when not on captive portal
* **ATS bypass**: HTTP exception for detectportal.firefox.com could be misused
* **Permission spam**: Multiple failed navigations could show repeated permission dialogs
* **Tab proliferation**: Users might accidentally create many captive portal tabs

**Mitigations:**

* One-shot permission (not persisted) prevents repeated dialogs
* Specific domain exception limits ATS bypass scope
* Check prevents multiple concurrent hotspot detections
* Popup management handles deduplication and automatic closure
* Auto-reload only affects tabs that detected hotspot

## Quality Considerations

**Privacy & Security:**

* Permission is one-shot only (not stored persistently)
* ATS exception limited to specific detectportal.firefox.com domain
* No user data transmitted during hotspot detection
* Follows existing permission system patterns
* Popup uses disposable Fire session for privacy

**Performance:**

* Hotspot detection only triggered on navigation failures
* HTTP request to detectportal.firefox.com is lightweight
* Background task doesn't block UI
* Prevents multiple concurrent checks
* Auto-reload only affects tabs that need it

**Architecture:**

* Follows MVVM pattern with TabExtension architecture
* Uses dependency injection for testability
* Integrates with existing PermissionModel system
* Proper singleton removal and dependency management
* Comprehensive test coverage including edge cases

**Edge Cases:**

* Network timeouts handled gracefully
* Multiple navigation failures don't trigger multiple checks
* Works with existing permission authorization flow
* Handles missing dependencies gracefully
* Multiple tabs scenario properly handled

## Notes to Reviewer

* This is a new permission type that doesn't persist (one-shot only)
* ATS exception is required for HTTP captive portal detection
* TabExtension pattern follows existing architecture
* Debug menu provides comprehensive testing capabilities
* All affected tabs auto-reload when connectivity is restored
* Singleton anti-pattern has been eliminated with proper dependency injection

Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/481882893211075/task/1209397034199086

### Description
This PR (2 of 2) implements the remaining changes to convert Freemium PIR from an experiment to a full feature. Changes here are:
1. Add `isUserEligibleForFreeTrial` property to `DBPUIHandshakeUserData` model and add plumbing to set the value. (**NOTE**: This can't be manually tested as it’s not used on the frontend yet, but we can rely on unit tests. Also by testing Freemium PIR works as expected, this is confirming that this property is just additive, i.e not breaking anything)
2. Add copy translations.

### Testing Prerequisites
1. Remove any subscription
3. Reset any previous Freemium state -> Debug Menu -> Freemium -> `Reset all Freemium Feature State`
4. Set Feature Flag override -> Debug Menu -> Freemium -> `Override Feature Flag -> ON`
5. Set Storefront override -> Debug Menu -> Freemium -> `Override Storefront -> USA`
6. Relaunch

### Testing Steps
##### Test 1 - Freemium Entry Points
1. Launch the browser
2. Ensure the new tab and more options menu Freemium entry points are visible (New tab shows a `Personal Information Removal` banner, more options menu shows a `Personal Information Scan` item under the `Privacy Pro` entry)

Screenshot here -> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84bde1a7-832e-4ad0-9b07-16888e8ffc46

##### Test 2 - Accessing Freemium
1. Tap the new tab banner button and ensure the Freemium PIR page opens
2. Close it
3. Tap the more options menu `Personal Information Scan` and ensure the Freemium PIR page opens

Screenshot here -> https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/522d5315-fa18-4f0e-a5e7-2f611663c99f

##### Test 3 - Run a scan and get new tab results banner
1. On the Freemium PIR page, tap `Start Your Free Scan` and follow the instructions to start a scan
2. Ensure a scan starts (if it does not check your system settings for login items, and check that the debug app has the 
needed entitlements)
3. Wait for the scan to complete
4. Relaunch the browser
5. Ensure you see a banner on the new tab page displaying scan results
9. Tap the view results button and ensure it opens the Freemium PIR page

##### Test 4 - Freemium Unavailable
1. Reset the Feature Flag and Storefront overrides previously set via Debug menu -> `Reset …Override`
10. Reset any previous Freemium state -> Debug Menu -> Freemium -> `Reset all Freemium Feature State` 
11. Relaunch the browser
12. Ensure the new tab and more options menu Freemium items are not present

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt PIR

#### What could go wrong?
Users who are not eligible for Freemium PIR could see it as a feature.

title: macOS: Add pixels for navigation engagement metrics (align with Windows)
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1210638013987333?focus=true

### Description

Implements pixels that exist on Windows to track user engagement.

Privacy Triage: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210650613141252

### Testing Steps

Remember to test with the visual updates ON and OFF.

1. Filter Xcode's console by "m_mac_navigation"
2. Run the app
3. Type a URL in the address bar that doesn't offer a suggestion and press enter so it loads.  Make sure you see this pixel:

```
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_url_source-address-bar ["appVersion": "1.145.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg"]
```

4. Type in a URL that shows a suggestion that's not a bookmark, select it and press enter.  Make sure you see this pixel:

```
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_url_source-suggestion ["pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "appVersion": "1.145.0"]
```

5. Create a bookmark.
6. Open it through the bookmarks menu.

```
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_bookmark_source-menu ["pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "appVersion": "1.145.0"]
```

7. Open it through bookmarks manager list:

```
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_bookmark_source-list-interface ["pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "appVersion": "1.145.0"]
```

8. Type in the address bar the URL for the bookmark.  Select it.

```
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_url_source-suggestion ["pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "appVersion": "1.145.0"]
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_bookmark_source-suggestion ["pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "appVersion": "1.145.0"]
```

9. Make the bookmark a favorite.
10. Open it through the bookmarks menu.

```
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_favorite_source-menu ["pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "appVersion": "1.145.0"]
```

11. Open it through bookmarks manager list:

```
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_favorite_source-list-interface ["pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "appVersion": "1.145.0"]
```

12. Type in the address bar the URL for the bookmark.  Select it.

```
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_url_source-suggestion ["pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "appVersion": "1.145.0"]
👾[Standard-Fired] m_mac_navigation_favorite_source-suggestion ["pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "appVersion": "1.145.0"]
```

### Impact and Risks

Low.

#### What could go wrong?

Might have broken existing logic although the changes are quite atomic and contained.

### Quality Considerations

NA

### Notes to Reviewer

NA
