title: Add support for new survey url parameter last_search_state
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201462886803403/task/1210574421664047?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description
Adds  `last_search_state` parameter if included in RMF config as per the following rules:
- Did not search in the past week / has never searched - `last_search_state=none`
- Searched in the past 2-7 days - `last_search_state=week` 
- Searched in the past 1-2 days - `last_search_state=day`


### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Go to `RemoteMessagingClient` for the macOS target and update the debug URL on L51 to point to https://staticcdn.duckduckgo.com/remotemessaging/config/staging/macos-config.json
2. Launch the app and confirm the remote message is presented on a new tab page
3. Perform a search
4. Go to a new tab page and tap to start the survey
5. Confirm the url includes the parameter `last_search_state` with the value `day`

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

Existing survey parameters could be affected (although unlikely). Unit tests have been added

title: macOS: Prevent Non Activated Freemium Users From Accessing Freemium (Freeze Rollout)
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210660568857763

### Description
Freemium is currently rolled out at 50% (production). We have merged work which will enable it for all users. However, we are in the process of improving our FE UI (adding Free Trial copy). So we want to wait until we have these copy changes done before making Freemium available to all eligible users. 

The changes in this PR essential ‘freeze’ the rollout, allowing current Freemium users to continue to access Freemium, while preventing new potential users from accessing it. 

In the final feature PR we will revert all changes in this PR.

### Testing Prerequisites
1. Ensure no Subscription

### Testing Steps
#### Test Freemium NOT available if you are NOT activated
1. Launch and go to Debug Menu -> Freemium. Then, Reset all Freemium Feature State
2. Go to Debug Menu -> Freemium. Then, Set Override Feature Flag -> ON and Override Storefront -> USA.
3. Relaunch
4. Ensure Freemium is not available (i.e not on new tab and more options menu)

#### Test Freemium available if you are activated
1. Launch and go to Debug Menu -> Freemium. Then, Set Freemium DBP Activated State TRUE
2. Relaunch
3. Ensure Freemium is available (i.e on new tab and more options menu)

### Impact and Risks
Low

#### What could go wrong?
Freemium is removed for current freemium users.

### Notes to Reviewer

title: Reload NTP favorites’ favicons at app launch once favicons become available
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1210531635402444?focus=true

### Description
This change implements a new NTP message that notifies FE about favicons cache being ready.
This allows FE to reload favorites’ favicons once favicons become available at app launch
and avoid displaying two-letter placeholders.

### Testing Steps
Test with [this review build](https://staticcdn.duckduckgo.com/macos-desktop-browser/a81f9679-e41d-404d-81a6-fd4a461d82f7/testbuilds/5021ab8/duckduckgo-1.145.0.467.dmg) or with Xcode.
1. Have a number of favorites and display favorites widget on NTP.
2. Enable state restoration and open a bunch of tabs.
3. Keep relaunching the app a few times and verify that each time the favorites’ favicons are displayed properly.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

#### What could go wrong?
It’s an additive change, and not adjusting any data, so not much. Also favicons cache loaded event is published once per app launch so any message flooding is also out of the question.

### Quality Considerations
No unit tests because it’s a “notification” type of message. None of these messages are tested because there’s not much to be tested anyway and testing is tricky (potentially flaky) because of Combine + Swift concurrency being used at the same time.

---

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/856498667320406/task/1210672892676451?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

Statistic Loader can trigger two async operations (fetches) that could take some time to complete. When done, notification is posted, that can invoke `AutofillPixelReporter` and cause SecureVault fetches. If that coincide with transition from Background to Suspended, app is getting killed as it is not allowed to hold an active lock on a DB file.

### Testing Steps

This is actually impossible to trigger with debugger attached, and nearly impossible to trigger in general unless you prolong the operations - so just sanity check for the logic is needed here.

Current setup does not cancel the in flight requests in case of the timeout, assuming it will be extremely rare situation for that handler to be invoked.

title: [iOS][Set As Default Browser] Integration + Debug View
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210636953633421
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

This PR implements:
- The services needed by DefaultBrowserPrompt feature that are injected by the client.
- The debug view to facilitate testing.
- The integration with main coordinator to present, if necessary, the modal sheet when the app comes to foreground.

### Testing Steps

**Prerequisites**
- Ensure that 'Internal User' state is on in the ‘Debug Menu’.
- Ensure DDG is not set as default browser.

**Scenario 1 - New/Returning User**
1. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
2. Select 'New' or ‘Returning’ user.
3. In the 'Activity Log’ section you should see when the first modal will show. (1 day after installation date)
4. Override current date by tapping on in ’Simulate Today’s Date’ and select a date 1 day in the future. Do not worry about time.
5. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
6. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
7. A modal should appear.
8. Tap the ‘Close’ button or manually dimiss it by pulling it down.
9. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
10. Ensure the modal is not showed again.
11. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
12. The activity log should show that the next modal will show after 4 active days.
13. Increase active day counter by tapping ‘Increment number of active days’ and increment to a number lower than 4.
14. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
15. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
16. Ensure the modal is not shown.
17. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
18. Increase active day counter to 4.
19. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
21. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
22. Ensure the modal is shown.
23. Tap the ‘Close’ button or manually dimiss it by pulling it down.
24.  Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
25. The activity log should show that the next modal will show after 14 active days.
13. Increase active day counter by tapping ‘Increment number of active days’ and increment to a number lower than 14.
14. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
15. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
16. Ensure the modal is not shown.
17. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
20. Increase active day counter to 14.
21. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
22. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
26. Ensure the modal is shown.
27. Tap ’Set Default Browser’ Button.
28. Ensure the app deeplinks to the settings.
29. Set DDG as default browser.
30. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
31. Increase number of active days to 14.
32. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
33. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
34. Ensure no modal is shown.

Reset Safari as Default browser and repeat the scenario by selecting ’Don't Ask again’ after showing the first modal and ensure no modal are shown again.

**Scenario 2 - Existing User
1. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
2. Select 'New' or ‘Returning’ user.
3. In the 'Activity Log’ section you should see when the first modal will show. (1 day after installation date)
4. Override current date by tapping on in ’Simulate Today’s Date’ and select a date 1 day in the future. Do not worry about time.
5. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
6. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
7. A modal should appear.
8. Tap the ‘Close’ button or manually dimiss it by pulling it down.
9. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
10. Ensure the modal is not shown again.
11. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
12. The activity log should show that the next modal will show after 14 active days.
14. Increase active day counter by tapping ‘Increment number of active days’ and increment to a number lower than 14.
15. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
16. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
18. Ensure the modal is not shown.
19. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
20. Increase active day counter to 14.
21. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
22. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
26. Ensure the modal is shown.
27. Tap ’Set Default Browser’ Button.
28. Ensure the app deeplinks to the settings.
29. Set DDG as default browser.
30. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
31. Increase number of active days to 14.
32. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
33. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
34. Ensure no modal is shown.

Reset Safari as Default browser and repeat the scenario by selecting ’Don't Ask again’ after showing the first modal and ensure no modal are shown again.

### Impact and Risks
Low as the feature is internal only. 
If the feature is turned on, only if the logic is not implemented correctly. Users can choose to never be asked again which should reduce the risk if anything goes wrong.

#### What could go wrong?
If the logic is not implemented correctly there’s a risk we could present the modal sheet more often than expected.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1210630080754242?focus=true
CC: @miasma13 @diegoreymendez 

### Description

This PR removes the entitlementsDidChange notification fired for Subscription Entitlements and centralizes entitlement change handling by introducing a payload object for notifications and updates all producers and consumers to use it, fixing issues around missing or mis-parsed entitlements.

- Event handlers now use EntitlementsDidChangePayload instead of manual userInfo parsing.
- Notification emitters post the new payload’s notificationUserInfo rather than raw entitlement arrays.
- Legacy code paths and temporary mappings for entitlement notifications have been removed or updated.

### Testing Steps

This will need a full AuthV2 re-test

### Impact and Risks

High: Subscription can be impacted

#### What could go wrong?

- Subscription could disappear
- VPN could not work

title: Use expectations instead of CombineTestHelpers
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205237866452338/task/1210659317398376?focus=true

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9eb817c0-895d-4974-9abe-28e9601c4fc6)

### Description

A long time ago, I created some `CombineTestHelpers`. Because they were so useful for creating concise tests, I ended up relying on them quite a lot. However, I started to notice that the more complex the publisher chain, the more likely these were to just completely flake. 

I couldn't find anything particularly wrong with their implementation, but what I did find from running tests thousands of times was that using as few publisher functions as possible in the tests would help stabilise them.

Rather than wasting any more time trying to figure out exactly what was going on, I adapted all tests that were using the `CombineTestHelpers` or similar patterns to just use assertions like:

```
.sink {
  if $0 {
    expectation.fulfill
  }
}
```

CC:

### Description

Timeout handling for scans and opt-outs. 
- `BrokerProfileJob` now invokes scans/opt-outs in `withTimeout` block to enforce a global timeout of 5 mins each (configurable in ExecutionConfig)
- `Scan/OptOutSubJobRunner` wrap their execution in `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` to handle cancellation. `ScanSubJobRunner` is updated to check for cancellation between each action in the same way as `OptOutSubJobRunner`.
- Adds a timer to `DataBrokerProtectionFeature` to periodically check for cancellation every 1 second when executing C-S-S action which may take up to 60 seconds (default action response timeout).
- When the background task expires, the queue manage will cancel all ongoing operations and reset the mode to idle. This should propagate down and trigger error 109 (.cancelled) or 115 (.jobTimeout) for expired jobs.

title: macOS: Import Chrome new tab shortcuts as favorites
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1210706281466357?focus=true

### Description

This PR updates the bookmarks import feature to import Chrome new tab shortcuts as favorites in the new tab page. This new behavior is behind a feature flag and is disabled by default.

#### Implementation

* We have a new local feature flag `updatedBookmarksFavoritesImport` to control the new behavior.
* We read the shortcuts settings from Chrome preferences to determine how the Chrome new tab page is set up.
* If Chrome shortcuts are enabled, we fetch the shortcuts (from preferences for custom shortcuts or from the Top Sites database for the auto-generated “most visited” shortcuts) and merge them with the Chrome bookmarks.
* When the bookmarks are imported, we now collect the favorited bookmarks and add them to favorites all at once. This allows us to preserve the order of the Chrome shortcuts (while retaining the same ordering for other source browsers).

### Testing Steps

#### New behavior (feature flag enabled)

Set up Chrome:
1. Create a new Chrome profile.
2. Add at least one bookmark (e.g. visit a site and tap the star to bookmark it).
3. Choose one of the following setup options:
   * Visit several sites and confirm they appear on the New Tab Page, but don’t edit the shortcuts list.
   * Open the New Tab Page and add some shortcuts using the + button or edit the shortcuts list using the “…” menu on each shortcut.
   * Tap “Customize Chrome” in the bottom right corner and disable the “Show shortcuts” setting.
   * Tap “Customize Chrome” in the bottom right corner and select the “Most-visited sites” option.
4. Follow the steps below to test the import.

Test the import:
1. Go to Debug menu > Feature flag overrides > Other > enable `updatedBookmarksFavoritesImport` flag.
2. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks.
3. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Chrome bookmarks.
4. Confirm your new tab Favorites section shows the same items as the Chrome new tab shortcuts.

Additional scenarios:
* Import twice and confirm your bookmarks are imported a second time but you don’t have duplicate favorites.
* Import bookmarks from a non-Chromium browser and confirm they work as before.

#### Previous behavior (feature flag disabled)

Set up Chrome:
1. Create a new Chrome profile.
2. Add a least one bookmark in the bookmarks bar: Visit a site, tap the star, and select “Bookmarks Bar” as the folder.
3. Add at least one bookmark in another folder: Visit a site, tap the star, and select “Other Bookmarks” as the folder.
4. Follow the steps below to test the import.

Test the import:
1. Go to Debug menu > Feature flag overrides > Other > disable `updatedBookmarksFavoritesImport` flag.
2. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks.
5. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Chrome bookmarks.
6. Confirm your new tab Favorites section shows the same items as the Chrome bookmarks bar.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
The following scenarios have been testing manually and covered with unit tests:
* Shortcuts are imported and/or bookmarks bar is not imported as favorites when feature flag is disabled
* Shortcuts are not imported and/or bookmarks bar is imported as favorites when feature flag is enabled
* Shortcuts are merged incorrectly with bookmarks or added in wrong order to favorites

### Quality Considerations
* We plan to add success/failure pixels for importing these favorites (under review)
* If a Chromium browser does not implement the new tab shortcuts this way, they won’t be imported.

title: [iOS][Set As Default Browser] Ship Review Changes
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206329551987282/task/1210683081153607?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

This PR implements the following changes for Default Browser Prompt:
- Apply design changes discussed during ship review for small screen devices.
- Add string translations.
- Refactor service logic to make Main Coordinator present the dialog.
- Set the feature flag remote releasable.

### Testing Steps

**Prerequisites**
- Change the Privacy Config URL to https://www.jsonblob.com/api/1390576819966763008
- To facilitate testing feel free to override remote feature settings in “setAsDefaultAndAddToDock” and change 
`secondModalDelayDays` & `subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays` values to a shorter number of days. E.g. 2 and 3.
- Ensure DDG is not set as default browser.
- Comment out lines 39-42 and 44 in `DefaultBrowserPromptService` to use real date provider.

**Scenario 1 - New/Returning User**
1. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
2. Select 'New' or ‘Returning’ user.
3. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
4. Change the system settings date to 1 day in advance. Ensure that 24h have passed to be safe you can change the date 2 days in advance.
5. Bring the app back to foreground.
7. A modal should appear.
8. Tap the ‘Close’ button or manually dimiss it by pulling it down.
9. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
10. Ensure the modal is not showed again.
11. The next modal should display in ‘x’ days depending on the remote config settings ‘secondModalDelayDays' as stated in the prerequisites. 
12. Send the app in the background and advance of 1 day. Bring the app to foreground. This will record an active day.
13. Repeat step 12 depending on the number of days specified in ‘secondModalDelayDays'.
15. When bringing the app to foreground, ensure the modal is shown when the number of active days matches ‘secondModalDelayDays’.
16. Tap the ‘Close’ button or manually dimiss it by pulling it down.
17. The next modal should display in ‘x’ days depending on the remote config settings 'subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays ‘ as stated in the prerequisites. 
18. Send the app in the background and advance of 1 day. Bring the app to foreground. This will record an active day.
19. Repeat step 18 depending on the number of days specified in ‘subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays'.
20. When bringing the app to foreground, ensure the modal is shown when the number of active days matches ‘subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays’.
21. Tap ’Set Default Browser’ Button.
22. Ensure the app deeplinks to the settings.
23. Set DDG as default browser.
24. The next modal should display in ‘x’ days depending on the remote config settings 'subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays ‘ as stated in the prerequisites. 
25. Send the app in the background and advance of 1 day. Bring the app to foreground. This will record an active day.
26. Repeat step 25 depending on the number of days specified in ‘subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays'.
27. When bringing the app to foreground, ensure the modal is NOT SHOWN when the number of active days matches ‘subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays’.

Reset Safari as Default browser and repeat the scenario by selecting ’Don't Ask again’ after showing the first modal and ensure no modal are shown again.

**Scenario 2 - Existing User
1. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
2. Select ‘Existig’ user and Reset the prompt settings.
3. Dismiss the Debug Menu.
4. Change the system settings date to 1 day in advance. Ensure that 24h have passed to be safe you can change the date 2 days in advance.
5. Bring the app back to foreground.
7. A modal should appear.
8. Tap the ‘Close’ button or manually dimiss it by pulling it down.
9. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
10. Ensure the modal is not showed again.
11. The next modal should display in ‘x’ days depending on the remote config settings 'subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays ‘ as stated in the prerequisites. 
12. Send the app in the background and advance of 1 day. Bring the app to foreground. This will record an active day.
13. Repeat step 18 depending on the number of days specified in ‘subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays'.
14. When bringing the app to foreground, ensure the modal is shown when the number of active days matches ‘subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays’.
15. Tap ’Set Default Browser’ Button.
16. Ensure the app deeplinks to the settings.
17. Set DDG as default browser.
18. The next modal should display in ‘x’ days depending on the remote config settings 'subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays ‘ as stated in the prerequisites. 
19. Send the app in the background and advance of 1 day. Bring the app to foreground. This will record an active day.
20. Repeat step 19 depending on the number of days specified in ‘subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays'.
27. When bringing the app to foreground, ensure the modal is NOT SHOWN when the number of active days matches ‘subsequentModalRepeatIntervalDays’.

Reset Safari as Default browser and repeat the scenario by selecting ’Don't Ask again’ after showing the first modal and ensure no modal are shown again.

**Scenario 3 - Translations**
1. Select a language different from English and ensure modal is correctly translated.

### Impact and Risks
Medium. Users could be prompted with the modal more times than necessary if the logic is not implemented correctly. However, users can opt out by tapping “Don’t ask again" button which should reduce the risk of bad ux if anything goes wrong.

#### What could go wrong?
If the logic is not implemented correctly there’s a risk we could present the modal sheet more often than expected.

### Quality Considerations
The business logic is extensively tested to ensure modal are only presented at the right time.

body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1210718749358230
CC: @miasma13 @diegoreymendez 

### Description

The migration is now performed in 2 steps
1. While using V1 we migrate to V2 and store the new token, but we continue to use V2
2. When V2 feature flag is enabled, we start using V2 which is already migrated

### Testing Steps

Cases:
1. AuthV1, start without subscription, should use V1
2. AuthV2, start without subscription, should use V2
3. AuthV1, subscribed, should use V1
4. Enable AuthV2, subscribed, not migrated, should use V1
5. Restart AuthV2, subscribed, migrated, should use V2
6. (Roll-back) disable V2, restart, should use V1
---
- Install the previous app version and use AuthV2
- subscribe
- Install the new version on top without changing FF
- Everything should work as expected
---
- Install the previous app version and use AuthV1
- subscribe
- Install the new version on top without changing FF

- AuthV1, subscribe
- Enable AuthV2
- Enable Network link conditioner: 100% loss
- Restart the app
- See that in console authv1 token is not migrated
- Kill the app
- Disable Network link conditioner
- Restart the app
- See that, in console, subscription **v1**  is still used

title: Send daily macOS import pixels
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1202926619870900/task/1210716551781611?focus=true

⚠️ DO NOT MERGE UNTIL PRIVACY TRIAGE APPROVED ⚠️

### Description

There are already pixels sent for the browsers' bookmarks, passwords and favicons import flows. However, given the nature of the errors, it's likely that some users will be trying to import over and over, inflating the error rate.

In order to better understand these scenarios, I propose adding daily equivalents for each of the import pixels.

### Testing Steps
1. Go to File -> Import Bookmarks and Passwords
2. Carry out a successful import flow with bookmarks and passwords
3. **Both `_daily` and regular import success pixels should be sent**
4. Repeat steps 1 & 2.
5. **Only a regular import success pixel should be sent**
6. Go to File -> Import Bookmarks and Passwords
7. In the Review debug section, set a Bookmarks and Passwords import error
8. Proceed with import
9. **Both `_daily` and regular import failure pixels should be sent**
10. Repeat steps 6-8
11. **Only a regular import failure pixel should be sent**

## Post triage test
1. Download a rarer browser (e.g [Vivaldi](https://vivaldi.com/download/))
2. Import Passwords / Bookmarks from it
3. Check that any pixels sent say `other` instead of `vivaldi` in the pixel name

title: macOS: Update behavior for Safari bookmarks import
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1210726801397642?focus=true

### Description

This PR updates the bookmarks import feature for Safari: 

* “Favorites” from Safari are still imported in the Bookmarks root.
* “Bookmarks” from Safari are still imported into a folder off the root, but with the name “Bookmarks” (previously “Other bookmarks”)
* “Favorites” are still marked as favorites (e.g. on the new tab page), up to a limit of 12. This includes topping up the favorites list if there are already favorites.

This new behavior is behind a feature flag and is disabled by default.

⚠️ These changes are based on https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/1235 ⚠️ 

### Testing Steps

#### New behavior (feature flag enabled)

1. Go to Debug menu > Feature flag overrides > Other > enable `updatedBookmarksFavoritesImport` flag.
2. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks.
3. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Safari bookmarks.
4. Confirm your new tab Favorites section show up to 12 of your favorites from Safari.

Additional scenarios:

- Add some favorites and then import from Safari, and confirm your Safari favorites are still imported (up to 12 total).
- Import twice and confirm your bookmarks are imported a second time but you don’t have duplicate favorites.
- Import bookmarks from a non-Safari browser and confirm they work as before.

#### Previous behavior (feature flag disabled)

1. Go to Debug menu > Feature flag overrides > Other > disable `updatedBookmarksFavoritesImport` flag.
2. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks.
3. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Safari bookmarks.
4. Confirm your new tab Favorites section is the same as your Safari favorites.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?

The following scenarios have been tested manually and covered with unit tests:

* The specified number of favorites are imported when a limit is set and the bookmark store is empty.
* Favorites are topped up to the limit when the bookmark store already contains favorites.

### Quality Considerations

* The new string will be localized after copy review.

### Notes to Reviewer

Safari favorites | Imported favorites

title: Malicious site protection datasets serialization fix
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206329551987282/task/1209638992004956?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

I found an issue where background tasks could run in parallel and fetch data while another update was in progress. This pull request ensures that if there are ongoing updates, we skip the background update.

This is an attempt to fix the [Malicious Site Protection crash](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206329551987282/task/1209638992004956?focus=true) we have been monitoring.

Regardless, I believe it would make sense to build a serializer for tasks so that no matter how many tasks are initiated, we can enqueue them and execute them sequentially.

I’m currently targeting the release branch so the fix can reach the users. Let me know if we want to spend more time testing the fix internally first. 

### Testing Steps

### Impact and Risks
Risk is low given this crashes in some scenarios.

The fix does not fix the crash

title: Fix Duck Player audio continuing in background tabs
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1207252092703676/task/1210059188286314
Tech Design URL: N/A
CC: N/A

### Description
Duck Player tabs opened with "Open in New Tab" setting did not pause audio when switching tabs.  This was because Duck Player's custom HTML implementation bypassed normal browser audio management.

It also seems that not pausing audio prevented tab dealloc when closing, tabs, which caused audio to continue playing even if the tab was visually closed.

### Testing Steps ⚠️  **Use iPad simulator**
1. Enable Duck Player "Open in New Tab" setting
2. Open a YouTube video from search results (opens in new Duck Player tab)
3. Switch back to original tab
4. Verify audio pauses (previously continued playing)
5. Switch back to Duck Player tab
6. Verify audio can resume
7. Close DuckPlayer tab
8. Verify audio stops

### Impact and Risks
Low: Bug fix for existing feature, improves user experience

#### What could go wrong?
- Audio might not resume when switching back to Duck Player tab
- Performance impact from audio suspension calls
- Addressed by using iOS 15+ native APIs designed for this purpose

### Quality Considerations
- Uses iOS 15+ native setAllMediaPlaybackSuspended API
- Matches standard browser behavior for background tab audio
- Only affects Duck Player tabs with "Open in New Tab" enabled
- Minimal performance impact (single API call per tab switch)

### Notes to Reviewer
Focus on the tab switching behavior - ensure audio properly pauses/resumes when switching to/from Duck Player tabs opened in new tabs.

title: macOS: Import Firefox new tab favorites when bookmarks are imported
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1210649154360516?focus=true ### Description This PR updates the bookmarks import feature to import Firefox new tab shortcuts as favorites (instead of importing the bookmarks toolbar as favorites). This new behavior is behind a feature flag and is disabled by default. Here’s how the import works: * In `FirefoxPreferences` we check various settings related to the Firefox new tab favorites: * Whether the favorites section is enabled on the new tab * How many favorites are shown (default is 8) * An ordered list of pinned favorites * A list of hashed URLs that are blocked from being shown in favorites * In `FirefoxHistoryReader` we fetch a list of “frecent” sites from browsing history. “Frecent” is frequently + recently visited — this is what Firefox uses to populate the new tab favorites, in addition to pinned sites. * In `FirefoxDataImporter` we assemble the favorites list and merge it with the bookmarks being imported: * We filter and de-dupe the frecent sites list (using the same approach as Firefox). * We merge the pinned and frecent sites into a list of favorites. * We merge the favorites and bookmarks and import them. ⚠️ These changes are based on https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/1336 ⚠️ ### Testing Steps #### New behavior (feature flag enabled) 1. Install Firefox or go to `about:profiles` to create a new Firefox profile. (You can also test with an existing profile if you have bookmarks and favorites already set up; in that case, skip to step 8 to test the import.) 2. Add at least one bookmark. 3. Open the new tab page and look at the favorites below the search bar. 4. Firefox starts with several sponsored favorites (marked “Sponsored”). We don’t import these sponsored favorites (the list varies and is not accessible to us). You can select the “…” menu on each one to dismiss it or select the settings icon in the bottom right > click “Manage more settings” > uncheck “Sponsored shortcuts” to remove them all at once. 5. Firefox also starts with a set of default favorites that aren’t sponsored. We don’t import these default favorites (the list varies and is not accessible to us) unless they are pinned. You can select the “…” menu on each favorite to either pin or dismiss it. 6. Choose one of the following setup options: * Open the new tab page and click the settings icon in the bottom left. Disable the “Shortcuts” option. * Manually add and organize a set of pinned favorites using the “Add shortcut” button. * Visit a number of sites repeatedly (to increase their “frecency” score) until they appear in your favorites. (Note that the favorites section is not updated immediately so you may need to wait and relaunch Firefox to see them on the new tab.) * Put together a mix of pinned and frecent sites. You can drag and drop the shortcuts to reorder them. 7. Close Firefox. 8. Go to Debug menu > Feature flag overrides > Other > enable `updateFirefoxBookmarksImport` flag. 9. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks. 10. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Firefox bookmarks. 11. Confirm your new tab Favorites section shows the same items as the Firefox new tab. Additional scenarios: * Import twice and confirm your bookmarks are imported a second time but you don’t have duplicate favorites. * On the Firefox new tab page, tap the settings icon and change the number of Shortcuts rows. After importing your bookmarks, confirm the expected number of favorites are imported. #### Previous behavior (feature flag disabled) 1. Install Firefox or go to `about:profiles` to create a new Firefox profile. (You can also test with an existing profile if you have bookmarks and favorites already set up.) 2. Add at least one bookmark. 3. Go to Debug menu > Feature flag overrides > Other > disable `updateFirefoxBookmarksImport` flag. 4. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks. 5. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Firefox bookmarks. 6. Confirm your new tab Favorites section shows the same items as the Firefox bookmarks bar. ### Impact and Risks Low: behind a feature flag #### What could go wrong? * If we miss scenarios or Firefox changes their method for adding frecent sites, we could import a different set of favorites. This seems like a reasonable risk since we are still using the most frequently, recently visited sites to decide what to import. ### Quality Considerations * If the Firefox favorites includes sponsored favorites or unpinned, default favorites, those won’t be imported. As a result, we may import additional frecent sites that don’t appear in the Firefox favorites section. ### Notes to Reviewer * Pixels will be added in a separate task (for success and failure while importing favorites). ### Description

In order to fix the layout there were multiple things that needed adjustments:
* ActionBar is now attached directly to safe area, without adjusting for padding.

* SuggestionTrayManager was extended with two properties, that allowed to customize it to be shown inside the new input screen
* Bottom of the SuggestionTrayVC's view was attached to the keyboardLayoutGuide, working around an issue when the keyboard was shown when the FavoriteOverlay was not present when the keyboard was presented, which caused it not to apply proper content insets.
* FavoritesOverlay contentInset calculation for keyboard was improved, taking into account the safe area - it should be universal and not break existing production state.

### Testing Steps
1. Enable Search Input under AI Features Settings
2. While new input is active for both top and bottom address bar settings do the following:
3. With favorites that extend the beyond viewport height, scroll to the bottom, make sure the insets are allowing to scroll above the ActionBar.
4. Type something to get the suggestions, clear - favorites should be properly inset from the keyboard
5. Type again to get the suggestions, switch to duck.ai, switch back to search and clear the input. Check insets again.
6. Repeat from pt. 3 with multiline input. 
---
7. Disable Search Input.
8. Check the suggestions and favorites are displayed properly on iPhone and iPad and are correctly inset from the keyboard for both landscape, portrait and both address bar positions.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

Production state of suggestions / favorites overlay could be broken because the constraints and insets calculation was modified. Check for iPad and both top/bottom address bar settings with Search Input disabled.

title: macOS: Release updated bookmarks/favorites import experience
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1210786955879363?focus=true

### Description

These are the remaining changes to release the new experience for importing bookmarks and favorites from Chrome, Safari, and Firefox:

* Adds pixels for successful/failed favorites import, see [this task](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210676933580475?focus=true) for details. (These pixels will be fired every time they are called and once a day, like other data import pixels.)
* Adds localized text for new strings
* Updates the feature flags to failsafe remote feature flags (enabled by default, can be disabled remotely)

⚠️ Translations have been requested for the localized strings; translations need to be imported before merging ⚠️ 

### Testing Steps

You can do multiple imports in sequence or go to Debug > Reset Data > Reset Bookmarks between each test to do a fresh import.

#### Chrome

**Set up Chrome:**
1. Install Chrome if needed.
2. Add at least one bookmark (e.g. visit a site and tap the star to bookmark it).
3. Open the New Tab Page and add some shortcuts using the + button.

**Successful import:**
1. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks.
2. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Chrome bookmarks.
3. Confirm your new tab Favorites section shows the same items as the Chrome new tab shortcuts.
4. Confirm the event `m_mac_data-import-succeeded_favorites_chrome` is fired with the expected parameters:
   * `saved_favorites` with the expected bucket (e.g. `none` for 0 favorites, `few` for 1-5, `some` for 6-11, and `many` for 12+.)
   * `source_browser_version` with the Chrome version.

**Failed import:**
1. Go to `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/` (or e.g. `Profile 1` for a different Chrome profile).
2. Temporarily move the `Top Sites` file out of the folder; this will force a favorites import failure.
3. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks.
4. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Chrome bookmarks.
5. Confirm your bookmarks are imported but no favorites are imported.
6. Confirm the event `m_mac_data-import-failed_favorites_chrome` is fired with error parameters and `source_browser_version` with the Firefox version.

#### Safari

**Set up Safari**
1. Install Safari if needed.
2. Add at least one bookmark (e.g. visit a site > select the share icon in the top right > select Add Bookmark and choose any bookmarks folder).
3. Add at least one bookmark to your Favorites folder (e.g. visit a site > select the share icon in the top right > select Add Bookmark and choose the Favorites folder).

**Successful import:**
1. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks.
2. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Safari bookmarks.
3. Confirm your new tab Favorites section shows up to 12 of your Safari favorites.
4. Confirm the event `m_mac_data-import-succeeded_favorites_safari` is fired with the expected parameters:
   * `saved_favorites` with the expected bucket (e.g. `none` for 0 favorites, `few` for 1-5, `some` for 6-11, and `many` for 12+.)
   * `source_browser_version` with the Safari version.

**Failed import:**

There isn’t a failure scenario for importing favorites from Safari, because we are just importing bookmarks from the bookmarks bar as favorites. Any failures will be due to bookmark import failures (e.g. failed bookmarks parsing) and the relevant bookmark import failure pixel will be fired in that case.

#### Firefox

**Set up Firefox**
1. Install Firefox if needed.
2. Add at least one bookmark.
3. Open the New Tab Page and add some shortcuts using the + button or pin existing shortcuts with the “…” menu on a shortcut.

**Successful import:**
1. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks.
4. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Firefox bookmarks.
6. Confirm your new tab Favorites section shows the same items as the Firefox new tab shortcuts.
7. Confirm the event `m_mac_data-import-succeeded_favorites_firefox` is fired with the expected parameters:
   * `saved_favorites` with the expected bucket (e.g. `none` for 0 favorites, `few` for 1-5, `some` for 6-11, and `many` for 12+.)
   * `source_browser_version` with the Firefox version.

**Failed import:**
1. Go to `~/Library/Application Support/Firefox/Profiles/{profile}/`.
2. Temporarily move the `prefs.js` file out of the folder; this will force a favorites import failure.
3. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks.
4. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Firefox bookmarks.
8. Confirm your bookmarks are imported but no favorites are imported.
9. Confirm the event `m_mac_data-import-failed_favorites_firefox` is fired with error parameters and `source_browser_version` with the Firefox version.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
* Bookmarks and favorites may not be imported as expected:
   * Feature changes have been tested (manually + unit tests) in separate PRs
   * Remote failsafe feature flags are available for each browser to disable the changes if needed

### Quality Considerations
* If a source browser version does not use the data storage we expect (i.e. we can’t access its favorites for import) we will track that as a favorites import failure with the browser and version for investigation.

### Notes to Reviewer

title: macOS: Fixes for Firefox favorites import
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210813660392292?focus=true

### Description

This PR contains fixes for the Firefox favorites import, based on ship review feedback:

1. It checks if sponsored shortcuts are enabled in Firefox. We can’t import these shortcuts (they aren’t available to us) so instead we reduce the number of favorites to import to account for them. This way, the imported favorites list ends at the same point as (or slightly earlier than) the Firefox list.
2. It updates the search host filtering in `FirefoxHistoryReader` to better match Firefox’s filtering for top (“frecent”) sites. Their filtering allows subdomains (except “www”) of these hosts, which we were previously filtering out.
3. It updates the shortcut URL used for specific search sites in the top sites. Instead of using the exact URL from the history, Firefox uses a root domain (but retains the specific title from history).
4. It updates the bookmarks and favorites merging in `FavoritesImportProcessor` to only mark the first matching bookmark as a favorite. Otherwise, if there are multiple bookmarks for the same URL, they will all be marked as favorites (so the site will appear multiple times in Favorites).

Note: This also enables the bookmarks import feature flags for internal users, to facilitate internal testing. This PR should be merged before https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/1367, which updates the feature flags to release the features.

### Testing Steps

**Set up Firefox:**
1. Install Firefox or go to `about:profiles` to create a new profile.
3. Open the new tab page and select the settings icon in the bottom right > click “Manage more settings” > check “Sponsored shortcuts” to test an import with sponsored shortcuts.
5. Tap the “…” on the default shortcuts and pin or dismiss them.
6. Optionally, tap the + to add a custom shortcut.
7. Repeatedly visit a subdomain of a search host, such as https://start.duckduckgo.com/, until it appears in your new tab shortcuts. (Note that the shortcuts section is not updated immediately so you may need to wait and relaunch Firefox to see it on the new tab.)
8. Repeatedly visit a search site such as amazon.com and perform a search a few times, until it appears in your new tab shortcuts. Optionally: Dismiss this shortcut so it’s hidden.
9. Go to Bookmarks > Manage bookmarks and add two bookmarks with the same URL as one of your shortcuts (so you have duplicate bookmarks matching the shortcut URL).
10. Close Firefox.

**Test the import:**

1. Go to Bookmarks menu > Import bookmarks in DuckDuckGo.
2. Follow the prompts in the UI to import Firefox bookmarks from the profile you set up.
3. Confirm your bookmarks are imported as expected in the Bookmarks menu.
4. Open the new tab page and confirm your shortcuts appear as expected:
   * There are no extra shortcuts at the end of the list
   * There are no duplicate shortcuts
   * A favorite for the subdomain of the search host (e.g. start.duckduckgo.com) is included
   * The search site (e.g. amazon.com) has a root domain as the URL, or if you dismissed it from your shortcuts it is not imported at all.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

#### What could go wrong?
These are small fixes to refine the Firefox favorites import.

### Quality Considerations
These fixes are based on ship review feedback and have been tested manually to confirm they fix the discovered issues, and unit tests are updated.

body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210812088652956?focus=true

## Description

This PR splits `VPNSubscriptionStatusPixel` into two focused classes: `VPNSubscriptionClientCheckPixel` for app-initiated entitlement checks (startup, wake/foreground) and `VPNSubscriptionStatusPixel` for subscription service notifications. The new client check class adds a failed case to track operational issues like network failures during startup. This separation improves maintainability, enables better debugging of client check failures, and unifies iOS implementation to eliminate code duplication. All existing pixel names are preserved for backward compatibility.

## Testing

### Test Client Check Failures
- Easiest approach: Temporarily throw an error in subscriptionManager.isFeatureEnabled(.networkProtection)
- macOS: Check for `m_mac_vpn_subs_client_check_failed` and `m_mac_vpn_subs_client_check_on_wake_failed`

```
👾[Daily-Fired] m_mac_vpn_subs_client_check_failed_daily ["d": "test", "appVersion": "1.148.0", "isSubscriptionActive": "true", "authVersion": "v2", "e": "1", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg"]
👾[Daily-Fired] m_mac_vpn_subs_client_check_failed_count ["appVersion": "1.148.0", "e": "1", "isSubscriptionActive": "true", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "d": "test", "authVersion": "v2"]
```

- iOS: Check for `m_vpn_subs_client_check_failed` and `m_vpn_subs_client_check_on_foreground_failed`

### Impact and Risks

Low

#### What could go wrong?

There could be an unintentional change in the logic.

NA

body:

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205237866452338/task/1210781292959353?focus=true
CC: @bwaresiak 

### Description
- Brings data race safety improvements over Swifter HTTPServer class by reusing its code with added locks and wrapping unsafe calls into `queue.sync` closures
- Intended to fix the occasional test failures due to probable memory corruption issues causing the server failing to start: https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/16246162968
- The original failure log contains "Unrecognized selector sent to NSDate" during the test setUp which leads me to a conclusion there was a memory corruption issue; Turning data race safety checks indicated some issue in the HTTPServer implementation
- Since the project is archived and migrating to another solution seems not reasonable, I decided to copy the original code code into our codebase (BSD-3 Claude license which should be compatible with Apache) modifying the problematic places
- Increase test event didFail delivery deadline time and separate from didFinish event delivery flag to fix tests like testSimulatedRequestAfterCustomSchemeRequestWithFailureAfterWillStartNavigation (https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/16324456730)

### Testing Steps
1. Open BSK Package Scheme; Tests, Open Test Plan, Configuration tab, activate data race checks; 
2. Run the Navigation test suite repeatedly, validate the tests pass and there's no data race issues

title: [iOS] Remove DefaultBrowserManager and Service from the iOS project and use the one defined in local Swift Package
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210636953633415
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

This PR removes the manager and service used to check if the browser is the default defined in the iOS project.
These classes had previously been moved in a Package but we did not remove it yet as we were running an experiment.
Now that the experiment is completed we can safely remove the duplicate code.

### Testing Steps
1. Ensure CI tests pass.

Smoke Test (Test on a real device)
1. Remove any previous builds installed.
2. Ensure that DDG is not set as the default browser.
3. Complete onboarding.
4. Go to system settings and change the date to a couple of days in the future.
5. Foreground the app.
6. Ensure a modal promo is prompted asking to to set DDG as default browser.

### Impact and Risks
Low: The changes to the onboarding flow are safe as the experiment is not currently running. 

#### What could go wrong?
The DefaultBrowserInfoStore is the only class that changed. This was mapping between two identical type. Now the compiler ensures safety and unit test covers that it still works.

### Description
Ports #1321 to iOS. Notable changes:
- Moved pixel firing logic to the `AutoconsentManagement` singleton. This is because this will coordinate early firing of the summary pixel when the app is closed or backgrounded (see the linked TD for more info).
- Added special handling for "autoconsent" pixels in PixelKit. This is because on iOS the 'm' prefix is not automatically added. title: Names of downloaded files have no whitespaces (iOS)
body:
Hi.

I've noticed that the names of downloaded files does not have whitespaces. So if file has a name `long name with spaces.xls` it will be saved as `longnamewithspaces.xls` to the DuckDuckGo downloads directory.

Not sure if this is intentional or a bug.

Does not matter if I am downloading a file with a direct `<a>` download link (with the name set in the `download` property) or if I am downloading `Blob` using `createObjectURL`.

I am using iPhone 12 Pro with iOS 18.5 and DuckDuckGo iOS browser v7.177.0.5.

title: iOS: Add in-browser prompt to import passwords
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210598592976256?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description
Adds ability to show a prompt offering to import their passwords from Safari at a time when it's most useful to the user: when they've hit a login form and they haven't imported before.

### Testing Steps
1. Starting with a clean install (or delete all credentials & reset import promos via debug menu)
2. Visit https://fill.dev/form/login-simple
3. Tap on username field; verify you do not see an import prompt (feature flag not yet enabled)
5. Enable the feature flag `canPromoteImportPasswordsInBrowser`
6. Visit https://fill.dev/form/login-simple
7. Tap on username field; verify you see the prompt letting you import passwords
8. Tap on Set Up Later in Settings button; verify the prompt dismisses
9. Visit https://autofill.me/form/login-simple and tap on the username field; verify the prompt does not show again
10. Reset import promos via debug menu
11. Save a credential for fill.dev via the passwords screen
12. Visit https://fill.dev/form/login-simple and decline the autofill prompt. Tap on the username field and verify the import prompt does not show
13. Delete the saved credential and visit https://fill.dev/form/login-simple again. Tap on the username field and follow the import flow, confirming it completes successfully and that if you imported credentials for fill.dev you are now prompted to autofill this newly imported credential 
14. Disable Sync (if enabled)
15. Reset import promos via debug menu and repeat 13, except at the end of the flow tap the “Sync & Back Up Passwords” button and confirm you are taken to the Sync screen

title: Fix key4reader firefox import bug with simple PBKDF2
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210798627853099?focus=true

### Description

Firefox Key4 database import was failing for profiles with simplified encryption (1 iteration [PBKDF2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBKDF2)) because the code was trying to parse a complex nested ASN.1 structure that didn't exist in these simpler profiles.

The changes here make it so that, rather than throwing an error and failing the whole key parsing when an unexpected structure is found, we fall back to other methods, ending with the simplest single iteration PBKDF2 (which, in reality, seems to be an edge case).

### Testing Steps
1. Make sure you have [Firefox downloaded](https://www.firefox.com/en-US/browsers/desktop/mac/)
2. Put the profile I sent to you in `~/Libraries/Application\ Support/Firefox/Profiles`
3. Launch this build and go to _File -> Import Bookmarks and Passwords..._
4. Select Firefox with profile `6ohek66d.dev-edition-default-1578554113529` (the one I just sent you)
5. Start the import
6. **Import should succeed with 4 passwords**

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
- The added code could result in other errors being missed by returning nil instead of throwing them
- The added code could cause errors that I didn't anticipate (unlikely as it's a final fallback)

title: Firefox login import JSON decoding bug
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1202926619870900/task/1210798627853091?focus=true

### Description

Firefox password import is failing with DecodingError.keyNotFound for hostname field during JSON parsing. This is because the import code attempts to decode deleted login entries that lack required fields like hostname. These are common entries for users who have synced.

I've fixed this by excluding "deleted": true entries as well as skipping over any entries that don't parse rather than failing the whole import.

### Testing Steps
1. Download Firefox https://download.mozilla.org/?product=firefox-stub&os=win&lang=en-US
2. Save some logins (Nav menu -> Passwords)
3. Click Sign In to Sync
4. Either sign up yourself or ask me for my test credentials
5. Delete >=1 login
6. Open DuckDuckGo
7. Go to File -> Import Bookmarks and Passwords
8. Import from Firefox (making sure you select the synced profile if you have multiple. If you have one, the profile picker will not show)
9. **Import should complete with the number of non-deleted logins**

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
More complicated parsing could be more brittle. However, I've kept the parsing the same and only parsed what is absolutely needed.

title: Fix loc_export.sh scripts to properly isolate platform exports
body:
Task/Issue URL: N/A
Tech Design URL: N/A
CC: N/A

### Description
Fixed both iOS and macOS `loc_export.sh` scripts to ensure they only export strings from their respective platforms when run from the repository root directory.

The issue was that running these scripts from the root directory (e.g., `macOS/scripts/loc_export.sh`) could result in xcodebuild detecting and using the workspace file, which would export strings from both iOS and macOS platforms.

### Testing Steps
1. From the repository root, run `macOS/scripts/loc_export.sh`
2. Verify that only macOS strings are exported (no iOS phantom strings)
3. From the repository root, run `iOS/scripts/loc_export.sh`
4. Verify that only iOS strings are exported
5. Run the scripts from within their respective directories and verify they still work correctly

### Impact and Risks
**Low**: This is a build script improvement that ensures proper isolation of platform-specific localization exports.

This PR adds retry mechanism support to the SubscriptionTokenKeychainStorageV2 class to handle transient keychain access failures. The implementation includes configurable retry logic with exponential backoff and improved error handling.

body:

### Description
* We previously attributed subscriptions to freemium using client-side logic which determined if the user has performed a free scan
* We are now removing this logic and using the standard method of origin attribution by extracting it from the URL

### Testing prerequisites 
* Remove any active subscription 
* Go to the debug menu → Personal Information Removal → Web UI → Set the custom URL to https://vkraucunas.duckduckgo.com/dbp
* Set a breakpoint at the following line in `SubscriptionPagesUseSubscriptionFeatureV2` -> `subscriptionSuccessPixelHandler.origin = await originFrom(originalMessage: message)` _(Or the equivalent line in `SubscriptionPagesUseSubscriptionFeature` if not using Auth v2)_

### Testing Steps
1. Launch Freemium via more options menu (hamburger) → Free Personal Information Scan
2. Perform a free scan. 
3. Click the "Try for Free" CTA on the scan results page. 
4. On the subscription purchase page, being to purchase a subscription. 
5. Observe the breakpoint and ensure that the origin is being set to `funnel_freescan_macos`

### Impact and Risks
Low

title: Connect New Tab Page Duck.ai shortcut setting to NTP
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1210867989812277?focus=true
CC: @tomasstrba 

### Description
This change connects native Duck.ai settings to New Tab Page Omnibar configuration to hide the Duck.ai
input prompt if the user wishes so.
NewTabPageOmnibarModeProvider was renamed to NewTabPageOmnibarConfigProvider (because config
is now more than just the mode). The provider was updated with AI chat settings to be able to pass
AI settings to NTP.
AIChatMenuConfiguration was moved to App Delegate and it’s injected to all classess using it.

### Testing Steps
1. Launch the app and open NTP and Settings tabs. Open another window with NTP.
2. Go to AI Features settings and toggle NTP switch. Verify that Duck.ai visibility on NTP is properly updated.
3. Toggle global AI flag and verify that Duck.ai visibility is properly updated (global AI flag overrides NTP setting).
4. Open Customization Panel on NTP and click “Hide Duck.ai” and “Show Duck.ai”. Verify that it updates Duck.ai visibility in all NTP tabs and in the Settings screen.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

### Quality Considerations
Tests are updated.

title: Set concurrency requirements for CI workflows
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203301625297703/task/1210878342031201?focus=true

### Description
This change sets up rules related to running various workflows concurrently, aiming to reduce the number
of unneeded workflow runs (e.g. made redundant by a new commit to a branch) and to guard us from errors
such as requesting internal release bump twice in a quick succession (e.g. by different team members that
haven’t communicated with each other).

### Testing Steps
1. Verify that these workflow runs have been cancelled (that’s because I pushed a commit while they were running):
  * [bsk_pr_checks](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/16497725260?pr=1479)
  * [dbp_pr_checks](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/16497725273?pr=1479)
  * [ios_pr_checks](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/16497725267?pr=1479)
  * [macos_pr_checks](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/16497725304?pr=1479)
2. Verify that concurrency definition for other workflows matches requirements in the linked Asana task. Release workflows use `cancel-in-progress: false` to allow current runs to finish before starting new runs.
 
### Impact and Risks
None: Internal tooling, documentation

title: Attempt fixes for occassional blank webView issue
body:
<!--

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/414709148257752/task/1210155968610460?focus=true

### Description
Attempts to fix an issue where users would see blank tabs after switching between tabs, requiring them to switch away and back to restore visibility. Investigation revealed the webView was getting stuck in an inconsistent state where it was hidden but no error message was being displayed. Added a defensive fix: automatically restore webView visibility when the inconsistent state is detected.

### Testing Steps
- Open multiple tabs with different websites loaded
- Switch between tabs rapidly, including tabs that may have loading errors or interrupted navigation
- Verify that tabs never appear completely blank (should show either web content or a proper error message)
- Test error scenarios by navigating to invalid URLs to ensure error pages still display correctly (https://privacy-test-pages.site/network-error/)

### Impact and Risks
Low - This is a defensive bug fix that should improve the reliability of tab switching and error handling.

### What could go wrong?

The automatic state correction in `checkWebViewVisibilityConsistency()` calls the existing `hideErrorMessage()` method, so it follows the same code path as normal error recovery.

### Quality Considerations

The existing debug pixel (`debugWebViewInVisibleTabHidden`) will continue to fire when the inconsistent state is detected, providing monitoring of how often this issue occurs and whether the fix is effective. Edge case consideration: error messages that are whitespace-only are now treated the same as empty messages. Performance impact is minimal as these are defensive checks in existing code paths.

CC:

### Description
weak ref to WKFrameInfo disappears immediately after the message is processed, causing the reference to be null when the 'autoconsentDone' message is triggered shortly after. Instead we can safely make selfTestFrameInfo not weak, as it's own reference to WKWebView is weak.

title: Use async expectations to reduce flake in burn tests
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1202926619870900/task/1210891822092133?focus=true
Tech Design URL: N/A
CC: N/A

### Description
Converted 6 test functions in `FireTests.swift` from using the legacy `waitForExpectations(timeout:)` pattern to the modern async/await pattern with `await fulfillment(of:timeout:)`. This change addresses flaky test behavior by using XCTest's more reliable async testing infrastructure.

**Changes made:**
- Added `async` modifier to 6 test function signatures
- Replaced `waitForExpectations(timeout: X, handler: nil)` with `await fulfillment(of: [expectationName], timeout: X)`
- Replaced `waitForExpectations(timeout: X)` with `await fulfillment(of: [expectationName], timeout: X)`
- Maintained all existing `@MainActor` annotations and test logic

**Affected test functions:**
- `testWhenBurnAll_ThenAllWindowsAreClosed()`
- `testWhenBurnAll_ThenPinnedTabsArePersisted()`
- `testWhenBurnAll_ThenAllWebsiteDataAreRemoved()`
- `testWhenBurnAllThenBurningFlagToggles()`
- `testWhenBurnVisitIsCalledForTodayThenAllExistingTabsAreCleared()`
- `testWhenBurnVisitIsCalledForOtherDayThenExistingTabsRemainOpen()`

### Testing Steps
1. Run the `FireTests` test suite to ensure all converted tests pass consistently
2. Run the tests multiple times to verify the flaky behavior has been resolved
3. Verify that test execution time remains reasonable with the async patterns
4. Check that all expectations are properly fulfilled in the async context

### Impact and Risks
**Impact Level: Low**

#### What could go wrong?
- **Test timeouts**: If expectations aren't fulfilled properly in the async context, tests could hang until timeout
- **Race conditions**: Incorrect async handling could introduce new timing issues
- **Test execution order**: Changes to async behavior might affect test isolation

**Mitigation strategies:**
- All existing test logic and assertions remain unchanged
- Using XCTest's built-in async testing infrastructure which is more reliable than legacy patterns
- Maintained same timeout values to preserve existing behavior

### Quality Considerations
- **Test reliability**: Modern async/await pattern reduces timing-related flakiness
- **Maintainability**: Async/await is more readable and follows current XCTest best practices
- **Performance**: No significant performance impact expected; may actually be slightly faster due to better async handling
- **Documentation**: Code is more self-documenting with async function signatures
- **Future-proofing**: Aligns with modern Swift testing patterns and XCTest evolution

### Notes to Reviewer
The conversion is straightforward - we're simply adopting XCTest's recommended async testing approach while preserving all existing test logic and assertions. The main benefit is improved test reliability by eliminating timing-related flakiness that can occur with the legacy `waitForExpectations` pattern.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1202926619870900/task/1210889673670469?focus=true
cc: @quanganhdo 

### Description

**Fix SIGKILL crash during app startup caused by blocking SecureVault initialization**

A crash was introduced in `7.167.0+ios` where tab restoration triggers synchronous SecureVault initialization during favicon loading, possibly blocking the main thread with heavy PBKDF2 crypto operations. Fixed by making SecureVault initialization async and optimizing execution flow (fast bookmark check first, then async autofill check). Added proper `@MainActor` annotations for thread safety.

### Testing Steps

1. Launch app with restored tabs containing fireproof domains and verify no SIGKILL crashes during favicon loading
2. Navigate to sites with saved autofill credentials and confirm favicon loading still works
3. Test edge cases: e.g many (10+) restored tabs

### Impact and Risks

**Medium:** Fixes critical crash affecting app launch reliability. Failure could result in continued app termination during startup.

#### What could go wrong?

Async timing issues could prevent fireproof favicons from being set properly. Race conditions between multiple favicon requests during startup could interfere with each other.

### Quality Considerations

- **Performance:** Eliminates main thread blocking during crypto operations and reduces app launch time. 
- **Edge Cases:** Handles empty favicon cache, autofill feature flag toggling, and SecureVault initialization failures.
- **Monitoring:** Watch crash reports for SIGKILL reduction in `CCKeyDerivationPBKDF` stack and monitor app launch performance metrics.

### Notes to Reviewer

- **Key Focus:** Verify async/await patterns and fix the negation bug in `deleteFireproofFavicon()` method. 
- **Testing Priority:** App startup with tab restoration (high crash risk scenario) and favicon functionality. 
- **Risk:** Low regression risk - maintains existing functionality with better performance, no external API changes.

title: Show correct URL on SERP after opening URL in external app
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1209365034718375?focus=true CC: ### Description This change addresses two distinct scenarios where users interact with advertisements within search engine results pages (SERPs), which currently lack optimal handling: - **Product Advertisement Click:** Upon clicking on a product advertisement, the Bing.com URL is opened in a new, empty tab. - **SERP Advertisement Click:** In the case of a search result for Amazon, clicking on the first advertisement for amazon.co.uk opens the Bing.com URL in the same tab while simultaneously removing the content of the SERP. In both scenarios, the intention is to avoid opening a new tab or displaying an incorrect URL. Instead, the desired outcome is to maintain the current state of the browser before clicking on the advertisement. ### Testing Steps #### Preparation 1. Install the Amazon iOS app #### Test 1 1. Search "Bluetooth speaker" 2. Click on an Amazon ad 3. The native Amazon app should be opened 4. Go back to DDG 5. The only tab open should be SERP and the address bar should show the search terms or the DDG URL #### Test 2 1. Search "Amazon" 2. Click on the first, sponsored result for Amazon 3. The native Amazon app should be opened 4. Go back to DDG 5. The only tab open should be SERP, and the address bar should show the search terms or the DDG URL #### Try to break the mitigation - If you test on a device while using a keyboard, try to run one of the test scenarios, and as soon as the DDG app goes in the background CMD+Tab back to it. - Try to open links in tabs manually and immediately send the app to the background. Also, without a connection to simulate a load error. ### Impact and Risks If the mitigation is executed in the wrong case, we could close a tab that shouldn't be closed. #### What could go wrong? The tab is closed in the wrong circumstances because the user's action manages to fool the state machine. --- ###### Internal references: [Definition of Done](https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207634633537039/f) | [Engineering Expectations](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/199064865822552) | [Tech Design Template](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/184709971311943)

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1148564399326804/task/1210871346730418?focus=true

### Description
Measuring new tab page loading times. Given that New Tab Page is currently shared between tabs, if the New Tab Page is already loaded, we report the time of webview switch. If it's already presented, the reported time is 0

### Testing Steps

Add `m_mac_new-tab-page_loading_time` to the console filter and verify reported pixels in following states:
- New Tab Page is selected tab after the application start (hundreds or thousands of ms)
- New Tab Page is not selected tab after the application start, but it's selected right after the current tab loads (hundreds or thousands of ms)
- New Tab Page is already loaded, a regular URL is loaded in the current tab, and user opened a new NTB (tens of ms)
- New Tab Page is already loaded and selected, and user opened a new NTB (0)

title: Subscription keychain error 25291 mitigation
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1210830784500963?focus=true
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210830784500963/comment/1210963320974998?focus=true
CC: @diegoreymendez @miasma13 

### Description

This PR implements a mitigation for keychain error 25291 (-25291, which is errSecNotAvailable) by introducing a new KeychainManager that provides automatic retry capabilities for subscription keychain operations. When the keychain is unavailable, operations are queued in a writing backlog and automatically retried when the keychain becomes available again.

Introduction of a new KeychainManager class with thread-safe keychain operations and automatic retry mechanism
Refactoring of SubscriptionTokenKeychainStorageV2 to use the new KeychainManager instead of direct keychain operations
Addition of new pixel events with improved error tracking using PixelKit's error field instead of string descriptions

KeychainManager is fully tested

### Testing Steps

- Subscription should work as usual
- Probably the best way of testing this is to hardcode an `errSecNotAvailable` error in the KeychainManager `store(data...)`
- in console filter for "KeychainManager" categoty for seeing the keychain use across main app and system extension

title: Revert "Fix Duck Player audio continuing in background tabs"
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1210379416433601/task/1210922940139837?focus=true

## Description
This PR reverts the changes from #1310 that prevented Duck Player audio from continuing in background tabs.

## What changed?
- Removed media playback suspension when tabs become inactive
- Removed media playback resumption when tabs become active  
- Reverted `WebDuckPlayerNavigationHandler.swift` to allow audio to continue playing when switching between tabs

## Why?
The previous implementation that paused media when switching tabs was causing issues with the intended Duck Player experience. Users expect audio to continue playing in background tabs, similar to standard web video players.

## Testing:
Make sure CI is green.  No new functionality added.

--

title: Loading New Tab Page in regular browsing webview
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1148564399326804/task/1210854362299269?focus=true
Tech Design: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/481882893211075/task/1210854362299278?focus=true
CC:

### Description
This PR reimplements the New Tab Page so that each browser tab maintains its own independent New Tab Page state. This is achieved by loading the New Tab Page in a regular browsing webview, rather than using one shared webview for each New Tab Page across all tabs in a window.

### Testing Steps
**Test original implementation with the `newTabPagePerTab` feature flag disabled**
1. Make sure the new tab page opens without any issues after the start of the app
2. Verify you can open additional tabs with NTP loaded without any issues

**Test new implementation with feature flag enabled**
1. Verify the new tab page loads after the browser start
3. Smoke test features like customization, search bar, or favorite list
4. Verify the pre-loader works by opening new tabs and observing no or very little loading times
5. Make sure there are no visual glitches when opening new tabs especially after resizing of the window or changing the appearance mode

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
Loading of New Tab Page or its functionality can be broken

### Notes to Reviewer
The PR adding monitoring pixels will be merged to the main branch and to the release branch soon

title: Feature Request: Support "ddgquicklink://..." URI for the macOS app
body:
Hi,

`ddgquicklink://...` is currently only supported by the DuckDuckGo app for iOS, but it would be great if it's supported by the macOS version as well.

## Use case

I'm a developer of a browser extension that lets users redirect one website to another using a user-defined rule, and one of my users shared a rule setting in the community: https://github.com/mshibanami/redirect-web/discussions/83

Their rule is for opening YouTube videos in the DuckDuckGo app. It works on iOS, but I noticed it doesn't work on macOS because Safari cannot open it as it considers the link invalid. So I hope it will be also supported for the macOS app.

I confirmed that running `open -a "/Applications/DuckDuckGo.app" "ddgquicklink://..."` from Terminal works fine while [there isn't a related setting in info.plist](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/blob/4671875d7649af2f5a72dcca62fe7149f21be8f5/macOS/DuckDuckGo/Info.plist#L462-L493), which might mean that just adding a new CFBundleURLTypes case in Info.plist for `ddgquicklink` is needed.

title: Add device-specific test configurations for iOS end-to-end tests
body:
Task/Issue URL: N/A
Tech Design URL: N/A
CC: 

### Description
Enhanced the iOS end-to-end testing framework to support device-specific test execution, allowing tests to run on appropriate simulators (iPhone vs iPad) based on test tags. This improvement enables better test coverage for device-specific features and UI behaviors.

### Changes Made
1. **Updated GitHub Actions workflow** (`ios_end_to_end.yml`):
   - Modified test matrix to use explicit device configurations
   - Added support for excluding tests based on device tags
   - Configured separate test runs for iPhone and iPad devices

2. **Added device tags to all Maestro test files**:
   - Added `iphone` tag to all existing test files (79 files updated)
   - Preserved existing `ipad` tag on iPad-specific tests
   - Maintained all original test tags (release, privacy, securityTest, etc.)

### Testing Steps
1. Run `./run_ui_tests.sh` with any test folder to verify local device selection works
2. Check that tests with `ipad` tag run on iPad simulator
3. Check that tests with `iphone` tag run on iPhone simulator
4. Verify GitHub Actions workflow runs tests on correct devices in CI

### Impact and Risks
**Impact Level: Low**
- This is an enhancement to the testing infrastructure
- No changes to production code
- Existing tests remain functionally unchanged

#### What could go wrong?
- **Risk**: Tests might run on wrong device if tags are misconfigured
  - **Mitigation**: All test files have been systematically updated with appropriate tags
- **Risk**: CI pipeline might fail if device models are unavailable
  - **Mitigation**: Using standard device models (iPhone-16, iPad-Pro-6th-gen) that are commonly available

### Quality Considerations
- **Edge cases**: Tests without device tags will default to iPhone (backward compatible)
- **Performance**: No impact on test execution time per test, but enables parallel device testing in future
- **Documentation**: Test file tags serve as self-documentation for device requirements
- **Monitoring**: Workflow logs clearly indicate which device is being used for each test

### Notes to Reviewer
- The changes follow the existing pattern in `run_ui_tests.sh` which already supports device selection based on tags
- All test files now explicitly declare their device requirements via tags
- The workflow changes are backward compatible - existing test runs will continue to work as before
