title: macOS: Improve Quality of Direct User Feedback
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1210990797327013?focus=true
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/481882893211075/task/1210859240378092
CC:

### Description
We are changing how we ask for feedback from our users. Instead of showing a dialog with some options and then the input text box, we will display different problems/new features and let them select the ones they are interested in, providing more text if necessary. The reason is that we want more qualitative feedback, and we are not getting that with the current flow.

**Technical**
- I’ve taken the opportunity to also remove the `FEEDBACK` preprocessor flag from the code, given that is not currently being used (we have it in all builds)
- There is a Technical Design on how we will send the data to the backend. TLDR; we will use the `sub-category` parameter from the backend, and send the different selected options as Asana tags, so then we can easily filter and query the feedback.

**Demo**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca5ffd65-4176-4cb7-a0b5-e46f1c83b7c3



### Testing Steps
1. Open the More Options menu -> Send Feedback
2. From there, select the Report a Browser Problem or Request New Feature options
3. Play with the form
4. Submit your feedback. NOTE: The feedback is working, so the feedback you submit will end in the `macOS Feedback` project, make sure to delete it after testing.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
We are aware that this could have an impact on feedback quantity, but at the moment, we are prioritizing quality over quantity.

### Quality Considerations
Nothing in particular.

title: Prevent TabSwitcher collection inconsistency when adding new tab
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

⚠️ If you're an external contributor, please file an issue before working on a PR. Discussing your changes beforehand will help ensure they align with our roadmap and that your time is well spent.
-->

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206226850447395/task/1210977113880963
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

Prevents performing batch updates with invalid internal state after the model has been modified by adding a new tab. 

This is a **speculative fix**, as I couldn't reproduce it manually. It can be reproduced by adding the following code at the very top of `TabSwitcherViewController.didChange(tab:)` and closing all of new tabs in tab switcher:
```
let hasNewTab = tabsModel.tabs.contains { $0.link == nil }
if !hasNewTab {
    addNewTab()
}
```

What it does is it's modifying data model just before the batch updates caused by notifying observer is performed (e.g. after refresh or redirect happens for one of tabs), simulating the specific events timing that triggers the inconsistency.

The assumption is that the flow which is causing the crash is as follows:
1. Have a tab (or a bunch of tabs) which are reloading in background. This may be http://privacy-test-pages.site/features/auto-refresh.html.
2. When user is on `TabSwitcherViewController`, the `didChange(tab:)` is being called every time the link is updated.
3. Pressing New Tab button on tab switcher, so calling `TabSwitcherViewController.addHomeTab()` just before the batch updates in `didChange(tab:)` causes the model to update and diverge from the internal state of UICollectionView. 

### Testing Steps
1. Smoke test around tab switcher and adding a new tab specifically.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

#### What could go wrong?
Batch updates are not done after one of background tabs is being refreshed, but that should be negligible as we're about to dismiss the tab switcher anyway.

### Notes to Reviewer
I've considered doing a more robust fix with using `performBatchUpdates` in the `addNewTab` function, but this has negative side effects like introducing unnecessary animation. Given the fact we already have `canUpdateCollection` in place using it seemed like the easiest and safest solution.

Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/481882893211075/task/1210649122070619?focus=true
CC:

### Description

This PR fixes an important edge case in the following scenario:
1. eligible user launches the app for the first time
2. they go through the onboarding and set the browser as default
3. upsell button won’t show up

Before this PR, `setup` also evaluated `isFeatureOn`, but that was prone to timing issues - the remote config might not update before we get to this evaluation. I fixed that by moving `isFeatureOn` evaluation directly before setting the upsell state to `.visible`. Since this only affects the first launch, it gives more than enough breathing room for a remote config refresh.

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app —>
1. Make sure `vpnToolbarUpsell` flag is disabled (so remove the override)
2. Reset upsell state via `Debug > VPN > Upsell > Reset Upsell State`
3. Relaunch the browser
4. Skip onboarding
5. Now use the debug menu to change the remote config url to this: https://jsonblob.com/api/jsonBlob/1403306814828896256 (no restart required)
6. Now set the browser as default
7. The upsell shortcut should appear within 10 seconds.

title: [iOS][Set As Default Browser] Implement logic for Inactive Users Prompt
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1210723746045885
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

This PR implements the logic to show the modal to set the browser as default for inactive users.

### Testing Steps

**Prerequisites**
- Ensure DDG is not set as default browser.
- Use configuration at https://jsonblob.com/api/1404333739999420416
FYI, this is the configuration that has been added.
```
 "settings": {
        ...
        "inactiveModalNumberOfDaysSinceInstall": 28,
        "inactiveModalNumberOfInactiveDays": 7
},
"scheduledDefaultBrowserPromptsInactiveUser": {
   "state": "enabled",
 }
```

:white_check_mark: **Scenario 1 - Inactive user modal shows properly as first modal**
 Use configuration at https://jsonblob.com/api/1404333739999420416
1. Delete existing app. Please do not use an alpha build as it can’t be set as default browser.
2. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
3. Override Today’s date 28 days (or more) in advance.
4. Dismiss the debug menu.
5. Dismiss the settings.
6.Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
7. A modal showing Dax and Browser comparison chart should appear.
8. Ensure "m_set-as-default-prompt_inactive-user-modal-shown” is fired.
9. Tap “Even more protections…” button.
10. Ensure that a modal shows and load "https://duckduckgo.com/compare-privacy” and "m_set-as-default-prompt_inactive-user_modal-more-protections-button-action” pixel is fired.
11. Tap “Close” to dismiss the Even More protection modal.
12 Tap set default browser.
13. Ensure “m_set-as-default-prompt_inactive-user_modal-set-as-default-browser-button-action” is fired
14. Ensure that the app deeplink to the system settings and the PiP video appear.
15. Go Back to the app.
16. Ensure the video is not playing anymore and the prompt is dismissed.
17. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
18. Ensure the modal is not shown again.

Repeat the test by tapping on “X” and “Continue Browsing” and ensure that "m_set-as-default-prompt_inactive-user_modal-closed-button-action” pixel is fired. 

:white_check_mark: **Scenario 2 - Do not show two type of modals in the same day**
1. Delete existing app. Please do not use an alpha build as it can’t be set as default browser.
2. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
3. Override Today’s date 28 days (or more) in advance.
4. Dismiss the debug menu.
5. Dismiss the settings.
6.Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
7. Ensure a modal for inactive users showing Dax and Browser comparison chart is prompted.
8. Close the modal.
9. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
10. Override Today’s date 1-2 days in advance.
11. Dismiss the debug menu.
12. Dismiss the settings.
13. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
14. Ensure the modal for active users is prompt.

:white_check_mark: **Scenario 3 - Active user modal take into consideration inactive user modal to calculate active days**
 Use configuration at https://jsonblob.com/api/1404333739999420416  
1. Delete existing app. Please do not use an alpha build as it can’t be set as default browser.
2. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
3. Select 'New' or ‘Returning’ user.
4. In the 'Activity Log’ section you should see when the first modal will show. (1 day after installation date)
5. Override current date by tapping on in ’Simulate Today’s Date’ and select a date in the future. E.g 2 days in the future. Do not worry about time.
6. Dismiss the Debug and Setting Menu.
7. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
8. Ensure the the modal show.
9. Tap the ‘Close’ button or manually dimiss it by pulling it down.
10. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
11. Override Today’s date and select a date > 28 days in the future to simulate inactive user.
12. Dismiss the Debug and Setting Menu.
13. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
14. The modal for inactive users should show. 
15. Close the modal.
16. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
17. Override current date by tapping on in ’Simulate Today’s Date’ and advacne one day in the future.
17. Increase the number of active days to 3.
18. Dismiss the Debug and Setting Menu.
19. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
20. The modal for active users should show. 

:white_check_mark: **Scenario 4 - Inactive user modal does not show if active user modal was dismissed permanently**
 Use configuration at https://jsonblob.com/api/1404333739999420416
1. Delete existing app. Please do not use an alpha build as it can’t be set as default browser.
2. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
4. Select 'New' or ‘Returning’ user.
5. In the 'Activity Log’ section you should see when the first modal will show. (1 day after installation date)
6. Override current date by tapping on in ’Simulate Today’s Date’ and select a date in the future. E.g 2 days in the future. Do not worry about time.
7. Dismiss the Debug and Setting Menu.
8. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
9. Ensure the the modal show.
10. Tap ’Never Ask Again’ button.
11. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
12. Override current date by tapping on in ’Simulate Today’s Date’ and select a date in the future e.g. 1-2 months to simulate an inacive user.
13. Dismiss Debug and Setting Menu.
14. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
15. Ensure no modal is shown for inactive user.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt the prompt to set the browser as default we show to active users.

#### What could go wrong?
If the logic is wrong, could present this modal to active users. I added automated test to validate the correctness of the behaviour.

title: [iOS][Picture In Picture] Attempt Fix crash
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206329551987282/task/1211011039245367?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

The [stack trace](https://errors.duckduckgo.com/organizations/ddg/issues/506092/?project=8&query=is%3Aunresolved+firstSeen%3A-9d&referrer=issue-stream&sort=freq&statsPeriod=14d&stream_index=0) shows that the service introduced to show the PiP video crashes for several users when the app launches. The crash happens in AVPictureInPictureController.init. This PR attempts to fix the crash by deferring the initialisation of the video components till they’re needed.

### Testing Steps
Prerequisites:
- Ensure to test on a physical device. PiP is not supported on iOS simulator

**Scenario 1 - “Onboarding"**
1. Open Debug Menu.
2. Select ‘Onboarding’.
3. Tap ‘Preview Onboarding Intro’ button.
4. Progress linear onboarding till ‘Protections Activated!’ screen.
5. Tap ‘Choose Your Browser’ button.
6. Ensure that the app deeplinks to the settings and PiP Video is playing.
7. Go back to the App.
8. Ensure that the PiP video is not playing anymore and the onboarding flow has progressed to:
  a. Add me to your Dock’ screen for iPhone.
  b. 'Choose App Icon color’ screen for iPad.
9. On the 'Add me to your Dock’ screen tap the ’Shoe Me How’ button.
10. Ensure the 'Add to Dock' video plays fine.
11. Send the app to the background and ensure NO pip video plays.

**Scenario 2 - “Settings"**
1. Open Settings Menu.
2. Tap ‘Default Browser’ button from ‘Privacy Protections’ section.
3. Ensure that the app deeplinks to the settings and PiP Video is playing.
4. Go back to the App.
5. Ensure that the PiP video is not playing anymore.

**Scenario 3 - “Promo Modal”**
1. Delete and re-install the app.
2. Open the Debug menu and select ‘Default Browser Prompt’.
3. Select 'New' or ‘Returning’ user.
4. In the 'Activity Log’ section you should see when the first modal will show. (1 day after installation date)
5. Override current date by tapping on in ’Simulate Today’s Date’ and select a date in the future. E.g 2 days in the future. Do not worry about time.
6. Dismiss the Debug and Setting Menu.
7. Send the app to background and bring it back to foreground.
8. Bring the app to foreground.
9. Once the modal show tap ’Set Default Browser’ button.
10. Ensure that the app deeplinks to the settings and PiP Video is playing.
11. Go back to the App.
12. Ensure that the PiP video is not playing anymore.

Low: Crash already exist

title: [iOS][Set As Default Browser] Fix prompt presentation when other modals are on screen
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211030690383959?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

The inactive modal will not be presented if any other modal is on the screen. This affects monitoring, as we will report showing the prompt, but since the prompt is only displayed once, the user may never see it.

This PR addresses the issue by presenting the full-screen prompt on top of any currently displayed modal, preserving the user's ongoing operation. When the prompt is dismissed, we will ensure that only the prompt is removed, and any previous modal remains on the screen.

### Testing Steps

1. In `DefaultBrowserModalPresenter` comment lines 43-48 and 50 to force inactive modal to appear when the app comes to foreground.
2. Open settings menu.
3. Background and foreground the app.
4. Ensure prompt for inactive users is presented.
5. Tap “Even More Protections…” button and check the webpage is presented correctly.
6. Dismiss the webpage.
7. Close the prompt.
8. Ensure Settings is still on screen.

Repeat the steps by tapping the “Open Links With DuckDuckGo” button.

title: Abort public release when there are unreleased commits on the release branch
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1210994795858969?focus=true
Fastlane plugin PR: https://github.com/duckduckgo/fastlane-plugin-ddg_apple_automation/pull/51

### Description
This change updates ios_tag_release_update_asana.yml and macos_publish_dmg_release.yml to stop when
there are unreleased commits on the release branch while making a public release. An extra argument is provided,
called `ignore-unreleased-changes`, that can be used to force making the release. In any case, public release workflow
will attempt merging the release branch to main before deleting it, and if that merging fails, the workflow will stop and ask
the release DRI to merge branches manually and re-run the workflow.

### Testing Steps
Verify the following workflow runs:
iOS:
1. [iOS public release workflow](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17041565770) identifying unreleased commits
  * [Asana comment](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211078512731369/comment/1211079578894888?focus=true)
  * [Asana task to handle unreleased commits](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1211079719524006?focus=true)
2. [iOS public release workflow](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17041596593) failing to merge release branch to main
  * [Asana comment](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211078512731369/comment/1211079730711339?focus=true)
  * [Asana task to merge branches manually](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1211079576074338)
3. [Successfull iOS public release workflow](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17041638762)
  * [Asana comment confirming success](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211078512731369/comment/1211079727092968?focus=true).

macOS:
1. [macOS public release workflow](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17038197398) identifying unreleased commits
  * [Asana comment](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211073355121332/comment/1211078239345320?focus=true)
  * [Asana task to handle unreleased commits](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1211078199439770)
2. [macOS public release workflow](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17038354497) failing to merge release branch to main
  * [Asana comment](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211073355121332/comment/1211078336208015?focus=true)
  * [Asana task to merge branches manually](https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1211078345489341)

title: Fix DuckPlayer test search query to include videos keyword
body:
Task/Issue URL: N/A
Tech Design URL: N/A
CC: N/A

### Description

This PR fixes failing DuckPlayer UI tests by correcting the search query URL. The issue was that the search URL was using a malformed parameter `ia=web videos` which created invalid URL syntax.

**Changes Made:**
- Updated the search query in `DuckPlayerTests.swift` to include the "videos" keyword in the search term itself rather than using malformed URL parameters
- Changed from `q="DuckDuckGo+vs+Google:+5+Reasons+You+Should+Switch"` to `q="DuckDuckGo+vs+Google:+5+Reasons+You+Should+Switch+videos"`
- This ensures the search results will include video content that the tests can interact with

### Testing Steps

:white_check_mark: **Scenario 1 - Search results load properly**
1. Run the DuckPlayer UI tests
2. Verify that the search URL loads correctly
3. Confirm that video results appear in search results
4. Verify that the "Videos" tab link is clickable

:white_check_mark: **Scenario 2 - DuckPlayer tests pass**
1. Run `test_DuckPlayer_AlwaysEnabled_Opens_FromSERPOrganic`
2. Run `test_DuckPlayer_AlwaysEnabled_Opens_FromSERPVideos` 
3. Verify both tests can find expected elements and complete successfully

### Impact and Risks

Low: This is a test-only change that fixes broken UI tests. No production code is affected.

#### What could go wrong?
The search query might return different results, but since we're including "videos" in the search term, it should be more reliable for finding video content.

### Quality Considerations

- Improves test reliability by using proper URL syntax
- Makes the search query more explicit about expecting video results
- No impact on production code or user experience

### Notes to Reviewer

The key insight is that `ia=web videos` is invalid URL syntax - the `ia` parameter should be either `web` or `videos`, not both. By including "videos" in the search query itself, we get more reliable video results while keeping proper URL syntax.

title: macOS: Open Fire Window by default
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1204006570077678/task/1209904613939706?focus=true Tech Design URL: CC: ### Description We are introducing a new feature that allows our users to set the Fire Window as their default. What do these mean? - When opening a new window (tapping CMD+N), it will open a Fire Window instead of a non-Fire one. - Shortcuts will be swapped (CMD+N will open a Fire Window instead of a non-Fire) - Menu items will be swapped in order (if the setting is ON, Open Fire Window will be first) - Users can still open non-Fire windows, and the restore session works with this setting enabled. The change is behind a feature flag, which is currently internal for users. #### Setting image #### Demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57396f09-5a59-4e1f-af09-316fdeb729cf ### Testing Steps 1. Open the application, and make sure you are an internal user 2. Go to Settings -> Data Clearing, check the ‘Open Fire Window by default’ 3. Open the File menu, check that `New Fire Window` comes before `New Window`, and CMD+N is set to open a Fire Window. Use CMD+N to verify that it opens a Fire window; ensure that CMD+SHIFT+N opens a non-Fire window. 4. The above should also be checked for the `MoreOptionsMenu`. Also the right tapping the application if in the dock, should show the items in the new order (check the demo video if in doubt) 5. Check that General -> On Startup -> `Reopen all windows from last session` is off. 6. Restart the application 7. Make sure that a Fire Window is opened by default 8. Open a couple of non-Fire windows and turn on General -> On Startup -> `Reopen all windows from last session`. 9. Restore the application; the non-Fire windows should be restored. 10. Go to Settings -> Data Clearing, uncheck the ‘Open Fire Window by default’ 11. Check that shortcuts are in the menu items and positions are back to normal ### Impact and Risks Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows #### What could go wrong? Edge cases that weren’t addressed. ### Quality Considerations I do not know of any edge cases that might exist. ### Notes to Reviewer Given your experience, Tom, make sure I’m not missing anything. — ###### Internal references: [Definition of Done](https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207634633537039/f) | [Engineering Expectations](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/199064865822552) | [Tech Design Template](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/184709971311943)

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1211088979568167?focus=true

### Description

This PR implements a user-friendly alert message for DDG internal subscriptions when users attempt to manage their subscription. Previously, when a subscription had no platform associated with it (DDG internal subscriptions), the "update plan or cancel" button would do nothing.

- Adds standardized alert messaging for both iOS and macOS platforms
- Replaces assertion failure with proper user feedback for internal subscriptions
- Implements consistent UI flow across both platforms

### Testing Steps

1. Restore your internal privacy pro subscription (the one on your ddg email)
2. Click/tap on Subscription > Subscription Settings > Update plan or cancel
3. You should see the new alert
4. Remove subscription
5. Subscribe with Apple sandbox account
6. Click/tap on Subscription > Subscription Settings > Update plan or cancel
7. You should be redirected to App Store

### Impact and Risks

Low, the new alert is visible only when a subscription has no platform associated with it, which happens only for DDG internal subscriptions.

```json
{
  "platform": "mobile",
  "tool": "translation",
  "translation": {
    "text": "Selected text to translate",
    "sourceURL": "https://example.com", 
    "sourceTitle": "Page Title",
    "sourceLanguage": null,
    "targetLanguage": "en"

}
```

title: [iOS] [App Intent & App Shortcut] Add Support for Search Intents and Shortcuts
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/276630244458377/task/1211107420315000?focus=true ### Description This PR adds two new `AppIntents` with corresponding `AppShortcut` along with pixel for tracking: - Search AppIntent – enables launching DDG search from Siri, Spotlight, and the Shortcuts app. - Duck.ai AppIntent – enables launching Duck.ai from Siri, Spotlight, and the Shortcuts app. As a result, users can now discover and trigger these features directly from system entry points like Siri Suggestions, Spotlight Search, and Shortcuts. #### Benefits - Bakes DDG app into iOS workflows (Siri, Spotlight, Shortcuts). - Surfaces DDG search and Duck.ai where users already look, increasing discoverability. - Potential to drive more app launches and searches with minimal friction. #### Note: - iOS supports only one `AppShortcutsProvider` per app. I renamed `VPNAutoShortcutsiOS17` to a more generic `AppShortcuts` to centralize all available app shortcuts. - Similar intents (`OpenSearchIntent`, `OpenAIChatIntent`) exist under `Widgets/ControlWidgetConfigurable`. I chose not to reuse them because: - Their titles/descriptions are widget-specific. - Making them reusable would require exposing public `inits`, overriding memberwise initializers and introducing extra complexity. Since this is a Quick Wins Day task, I prioritized shipping value quickly over deep refactoring. - While Apple’s ML model and user context decides when intents are shown, defining them significantly improves the **chances** of DDG surfacing in system entry points. #### Possible next steps: - Revisit the intent framework to consolidate duplicates and improve reusability. ##### Before ##### After ### Testing Steps 1. Build app and run 2. Open the Shortcuts app and verify new actions are available 3. In Spotlight, type “search" → verify DuckDuckGo appears in Search in Apps with the correct icon and title. 4. Trigger Siri phrase: “Search in DuckDuckGo” or other phrases listed under “phrases" → confirm intent executes correctly. 5. [Regression test] Click on search widget → confirm widget intent executes correctly ### Impact and Risks #### Impact: - Improves app discoverability and launch rate through system level entry (Spotlight, Siri, Shortcuts). Provides new convenient ways for users to search or open links. #### Risks: - Low risk. If the intent fails, users may not see the entry, which is status quo #### What could go wrong?

title: Build and tag releases at a specific commit, not at branch HEAD
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1211100722861853?focus=true
Fastlane plugin PR: https://github.com/duckduckgo/fastlane-plugin-ddg_apple_automation/pull/54

### Description
This change updates release workflows to build and tag a specific commit rather than the release branch HEAD.
This will prevent inconsistencies that could be occurring when new commits were pushed to the release branch
while the build was in progress.

### Testing Steps
Verify the following:
1. macOS:
  * code freeze workflow [records commit sha](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17111925455/job/48535150795#step:4:46) after incrementing build number (this step is not present in the iOS code freeze)
  * tag release [checks out that commit](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17111925455/job/48535173810#step:2:2695) and proceeds with tagging (the tag has since been removed from the repository).
2. iOS:
  * code freeze workflow [records commit sha](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17118632626/job/48554457194#step:4:588) after preparing the branch.
  * tag release [checks out that commit](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17111925455/job/48535173810#step:2:2695) and proceeds with tagging
  * [release/ios/0.100.0 branch](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/commits/release/ios/0.100.0/) has 3 extra commits on top that I added between creating a branch and tagging the release, but the [0.100.0-0+ios tag](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/releases/tag/0.100.0-0%2Bios) points to the commit before the extra commits.

### Impact and Risks
None: Internal tooling, documentation

#### What could go wrong?
I’ve thoroughly tested code freeze workflows. Bump and hotfix workflows aren’t tested (due to higher effort required to test them) but they use the same mechanism that has been verified to work with code freeze.

title: Fix content appearing when foregrounding app and before authentication
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201392122292466/task/1211024438380986?focus=true

### Description

### Testing Steps
1. Open any site.
2. Have authentication and data clearing turned off.
3. Background the app.
4. Open App Switcher and notice the site is visible.
5. Open the app and notice the site is immediately visible.

## Authentication ON
1. Turn on authentication.
2. Background the app.
3. Open App Switcher and notice the site is NOT visible.
4. Open the app and notice the site is NOT visible until authenticated.

## Data Clearing ON
1. Turn off authentication and turn on data clearing (5 minutes). You can change this line of code  `return elapsedTime > 5 * 60` to `return elapsedTime > 2` and wait 2 seconds instead of 5 minutes.
2. Also, add this line: `try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 5_000_000_000)` under `await autoClear.clearDataDueToTimeExpired(applicationState: .active)` in AutoClearService.swift to simulate long data clearing process.
3. Background the app.
4. Open App Switcher and notice the site is NOT visible.
5. Open the app and notice the site is NOT visible until data clearing completes (5 seconds).

## Authentication ON and Data Clearing ON
1. Turn on authentication and turn on data clearing (5 minutes). You can change this line of code  `return elapsedTime > 5 * 60` to `return elapsedTime > 2` and wait 2 seconds instead of 5 minutes.
2. Also, add this line: `try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 5_000_000_000)` under `await autoClear.clearDataDueToTimeExpired(applicationState: .active)` in AutoClearService.swift to simulate long data clearing process.
3. Background the app.
4. Open App Switcher and notice the site is NOT visible.
5. Open the app and notice the site is NOT visible until data clearing completes (5 seconds) and until user authenticates.

### Impact and Risks
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
Overlay screen not being dismissed/not appearing in some scenarios.

title: [QWD][iOS] Autogenerate app size report and fire pixels for release build
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203301625297703/task/1211098882149655
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

Add iOS App Size Tracking to CI Workflows

**Summary**
  - Implemented app size measurement for iOS ad-hoc builds and release builds
  - Created reusable GitHub Action to parse App Thinning Size Reports and send pixel metrics
  - Integrated with existing workflows

**Changes Made**

New GitHub Action: measure-app-size
- Script: Parses "App Thinning Size Report.txt" to extract universal variant sizes
- Outputs: Download size (compressed) and installation size (uncompressed)
- Pixels: Automatically sends pixel metrics to improving.duckduckgo.com/t/ with app version and build number parameters

Workflows Integrations

 ios_release.yml
  - Added: Optional measure-app-size boolean input (default: false) for different workflows (ios_bump_internal_release.yml & ios_code_freeze.yml) to use.
  - Conditional: Only measures when explicitly requested
  - Use: measure-app-size custom github action with the following parameters:
     - m_ci_apple_ios_release_download_size 
     - m_ci_apple_ios_release_installation_size
     - app_version 
     - build_number

 ios_bump_internal_release.yml & ios_code_freeze.yml
  - Added: measure-app-size: true when calling ios_release.yml
  - Coverage: This will ensure we will send the pixel metrics on a Monday when the internal release is created and on subsequent internal bumps if neeeded

ios_adhoc.yml
  - Added: App size measurement after successful archive for testing purposes.

### Testing Steps
**Test Script works**
1. Save the content of the [App Thinning Size Report.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21927962/App.Thinning.Size.Report.txt) locally.
2. In terminal run ./.github/actions/measure-app-size/parse_app_size.sh <path_to_file> and ensure the values printed are the expected ones.

**Test Ad Hoc Build**
1. Run the ios_adhoc workflow pointing at this branch with the following command:
`gh workflow run ios_adhoc.yml --ref alessandro/qwd-ci-app-size-ios --field suffix="app-size-test-6" --field asana-task-url="https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203301625297703/task/1211098882149664\?focus\=true" --field build-type=Release`
You can probably omit the `asana-task-url` and can pick your `suffix`
 
**Ensure Pixels are sent with right parameters**
- In Kibana check for m_ci_apple_ios_release_download_size & m_ci_apple_ios_release_installation_size pixels and ensure they have the expected parameters.

### Impact and Risks
None: Uses `continue-on-error: true` to prevent workflow failures.

title: Refactor urlsToRemove to use Set for O(1) lookups
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201392122292466/task/1210977112671092?focus=true
CC: @dus7

### Description
This PR refactors urlsToRemove(excluding:) to replace the nested .contains calls with a Set lookup.
Previously the function performed in O(N × M) time (files × tabs), which could cause high CPU usage or memory pressure for large datasets.
With a Set of excluded UIDs, lookups are now O(1), making the operation significantly faster and reducing the risk of watchdog/jetsam kills.

### Testing Steps
1. Unit tests should not fail.

### Impact and Risks
What's the impact on users if something goes wrong?
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows

#### What could go wrong?
Potentially removing wrong or not removing cached interaction states.

title: Add kbg=-1 parameter to search URLs when DuckAI is disabled

### Description
Implements automatic addition of `kbg =-1` parameter to DuckDuckGo search URLs when DuckAI is disabled in user settings, following the existing pattern established by the `ko=-1` parameter for search headers.

### Description

The macOS browser's sync functionality was previously tightly coupled to the sync settings screen through a monolithic SyncPreferences class. This architecture made it difficult to launch sync device connection flows from other parts of the application preventing sync onboarding in contexts where it would be most valuable.

The refactoring addresses the need to display sync device connection flows from multiple entry points throughout the app, not just the dedicated sync settings screen. title: iOS: Add Experimental Omnibar Pixels for Duck.ai Usage Measurement
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1211121614418052?focus=true
CC: @Bunn 

### Description
  Implements 8 pixels to measure Duck.ai discovery, usage patterns, and rollout safety for the experimental omnibar feature.

##### Pixels Added

Experimental Omnibar (5 pixels):
  - `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_shown` (daily) - Discovery measurement
  - `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_prompt_submitted` (daily_count) - AI chat usage
  - `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_query_submitted` (daily_count) - Search usage
  - `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_mode_switched` (count) - Mode switching behavior
  - `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_session_both_modes`(daily_count) - Seamless both-mode usage

Legacy Omnibar Baseline (3 pixels):
  - `m_aichat_legacy_omnibar_shown` (daily) - Baseline comparison
  - `m_aichat_legacy_omnibar_query_submitted` (daily_count) - Baseline search usage
  - `m_aichat_legacy_omnibar_aichat_button_pressed` (daily_count) - Baseline AI chat usage

### Testing Steps
#### Test Case 1: Basic Discovery & Usage
1. Focus experimental omnibar (keyboard appears) → `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_shown`
2. Type "duck" and submit as search → `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_query_submitted.daily` + `.count`
3. Toggle to AI mode → `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_mode_switched`
4. Type "hi" and submit as AI prompt → `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_prompt_submitted.dail`y + `.count`, `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_session_both_modes.daily` + `.count`

#### Test Case 2: Session Reset After Backgrounding
1. Complete Test Case 1, then background/foreground app
2. Focus omnibar, search "test" → `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_query_submitted.count`
3. Toggle to AI mode → `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_mode_switched`
4. Submit "help" → `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_prompt_submitted.count`, `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_session_both_modes.count`

#### Test Case 3: Legacy Omnibar Baseline
1. Focus legacy omnibar (keyboard appears) → `m_aichat_legacy_omnibar_shown`
2. Search "cats" → `m_aichat_legacy_omnibar_query_submitted.daily` + `.count`
3. Focus omnibar again, tap AI chat button → `m_aichat_legacy_omnibar_aichat_button_pressed.daily` + `.count`

Low, pixels with some minor helper code

title: Add support for freezing the release branch when submitting to App Store review
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1211100722861854?focus=true
Fastlane Plugin PR: https://github.com/duckduckgo/fastlane-plugin-ddg_apple_automation/pull/56

### Description
This change adds release branch freezing while promoting the TestFlight build to App Store,
typically run on Friday. The freeze option is optional but enabled by default - in rare cases
when we’re asked to promote the app during the week (such as to allow marketing team
to update App Store listing assets) the freezing can be disabled for the promote workflow run.
Freezing is done by creating a draft public release in GitHub.

Bump internal release workflows are now checking for branch freeze and if present,
they stop running and are notifying the release workflow.

Release publishing workflows (macos_publish_dmg_release.yml and ios_tag_release_update_asana.yml)
when run for public releases try to unfreeze the branch (by deleting the draft public release)
before creating a proper public release.

### Testing Steps
* [Workflow that’s freezing the branch](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17245956626/job/48935583087#step:4:31) - you can navigate to the draft release that’s linked there.

title: macOS: Show session restore prompt after app closes unexpectedly
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1211047835568337?focus=true Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1211047835568335?focus=true CC: @tomasstrba ### Description Goal: Offer to restore session after a crash for users without automatic session restore enabled. This PR adds the logic to detect when the app previously crashed, the UI for the session restore prompt, and coordinates displaying the prompt when it's triggered on app startup. Implementation notes: * The logic for deciding when the prompt is needed is in `AppStateRestorationManager`, along with other state restoration logic. * The work to coordinate showing the prompt is in `SessionRestorePromptCoordinator`, to ensure the UI is ready for the prompt to be displayed. (Otherwise it will be triggered before the window is ready for it.) * The prompt is shown as a popover from `NavigationBarViewController` and is only dismissed by interacting with the buttons on the prompt (although it does not block other interactions with the browser). * Unit tests are added for the logic around detecting a previous crash, when to trigger the prompt, and coordinating when the prompt is shown. ### Testing Steps 1. Build the app, set internal user state, and ensure automatic session restore is disabled in Settings → General. 2. Open one or more websites (so there is something to restore). 3. Go to Debug > Simulate crash > select any crash type. 4. Reopen the app: the prompt appears and you can restore the session or not. Additional scenarios: * When automatic session restore is enabled in Settings → General, no prompt is shown. * When the app is closed normally, no prompt is shown. * When there is nothing to restore (e.g. no sites were left open in the previous session), no prompt is shown. * When there is a potential crash loop (e.g. the app crashed, you selected “Restore Session”, and the app crashed again immediately), no prompt is shown. * When the `restoreSessionPrompt` feature flag is disabled (currently only enabled for internal users) no prompt is shown. ### Impact and Risks Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows Note: UI is behind a feature flag #### What could go wrong? * Could show prompt when not expected (e.g. when the app closed normally, when there is no session to restore) * Could trigger prompt before UI is ready (so it doesn’t appear) * Prompt buttons could trigger incorrect actions Unit tests cover expected logic for triggering the prompt, and the UI has been manually tested in all expected scenarios. ### Quality Considerations * Translations for new strings will be uploaded before merging. * Pixels to be implemented in another PR. ### Notes to Reviewer Screenshots: — ###### Internal references: [Definition of Done](https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207634633537039/f) | [Engineering Expectations](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/199064865822552) | [Tech Design Template](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/184709971311943)

title: Bump internal release on push to the release branch
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201899738287924/task/1211100722861850?focus=true

### Description
This change updates concurrency rules to group code freeze and bump internal release for iOS and macOS
(disallow for running both code freeze + bump on any of the platforms), removes schedule triggers from
bump internal release workflows and replaces them with push to the respective release branch.
Concurrency rules don’t cause stopping workflows in progress, but they rather queue new workflows
to be run after the previous ones finished.

### Testing Steps
These aren’t part of the changes in this PR, but just to verify that running bump internal release workflow from a release branch without specifying an Asna Task URL (previously unused mode of triggering the workflow):
* [macOS Bump Internal Release](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17268866793/job/49007776518) workflow run from `release/macos/1.154.0` branch found the release task and proceeded to running tests.
* [iOS Bump Internal Release](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/17268979991) workflow run from `release/ios/7.184.0` branch found the release task and proceeded to running tests.

### Notes to the reviewer
The warnings from Cursor about is_scheduled_release can be ignored for now. We really need the extra checks in place only for truly scheduled runs, and runs on push should work the same as triggered manually.

title: [iOS] Schedule Inactivity Push Notification + Pixel Firing
body: @alessandroboron Sorry for the HUGE pr. Feel free to look at the last 2 commits to see new changes after your last review. Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211003501974964?focus=true + https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211003501974968?focus=true Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/481882893211075/task/1211032403913073?focus=true ### Description **Update 8/28 (Thursday)** - Responded to comments - Added `UNUserNotificationCenterRepresentable` and `MockUNUserNotificationCenter` for injecting `UNUserNotificationCenter` related attributes for testing - Added more test cases in unite test file `InactivityNotificationSchedulerServiceTests`, including stress test, error path tests and unit test for `resume`, `schedule` and `requestAuthorization` - Added integration test in `InactivityNotificationSchedulerServiceIntegrationTests` - Tested locally via local override ------------- This PR creates a `InactivityNotificationSchedulerService` with it’s helpers: **InactivityNotificationSchedulerService:** Cancels any existing request and reschedules a local notification when authorization status is .provisional. **NotificationServiceManager:** Small refactor to centralize `UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate` **Pixel firing:** Added pixel new cases aligned with https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/1731 **Unit tests:** Added unit tests for helper methods in `InactivityNotificationSchedulerService` ### Testing Steps Hard to test at the moment. Will introduce debug menu item for manual testing in https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211035568337399?focus=true Tested via local override: ![IMG_8973](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79558316-d3ac-4b7b-b12f-10b3af022847) ### Impact and Risks Medium: Affects VPN notifications and tap flows due to changes in `UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate` in `NotificationServiceManager`. The new feature is guarded behind feature toggle. #### What could go wrong? - Misconfiguration of daysInactive (non-numeric or unexpected shape) Mitigation: Parser is defensive; on error we log and fall back to default (7 days) so we don’t spam or under-notify. - Duplicate or repeated notifications after rapid app relaunches Mitigation: We cancel pending requests for our identifier before scheduling, ensuring at most one pending inactivity notification. - User annoyance from unexpected notifications Mitigation: Remote kill-switch; conservative default; staged rollout; easy rollback if feedback or metrics indicate issues. ### Quality Considerations - Performance: The scheduler always cancels by identifier, then reschedules one request on resume(). In rare situations (e.g., rapid foregrounding), this can result in multiple remove/re-add cycles within a session. Work is O(1) and limited to a single identifier, so impact is limited; logic is idempotent to prevent growth of pending requests. - Edge cases: Missing/empty config; malformed JSON; non-numeric daysInactive. Parser is defensive and falls back to default (7 days). - Trigger validity: UNTimeIntervalNotificationTrigger requires timeInterval >= 1. Our default ensures this; malformed config logs an error and falls back, avoiding invalid triggers. - Observability: Errors on parsing/scheduling are logged; tap engagement is measured via the pixel. Remote feature control provides an immediate kill-switch if metrics or feedback regress. ### Notes to Reviewer Sorry for the _HUGE_ pr. Most are tests. --- ###### Internal references: [Definition of Done](https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207634633537039/f) | [Engineering Expectations](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/199064865822552) | [Tech Design Template](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/184709971311943)

### Description

This PR introduces changes to the following internal models to support Data Broker removal by adding `removedAt`:
- `BrokerDB`
- `DataBroker`
- `DBPUIDataBroker`

The addition to `BrokerDB` requires a database migration, that’s also part of this PR

### Testing Steps

There are two expected test scenarios:

#### Upgrading the app version from `main` (migration v7) to the version that supports Data Broker removal (migration v8)
1. Nuke the Vault DB from `~/Library/Group\ Containers/HKE973VLUW.com.duckduckgo.macos.browser.dbp.debug/DBP`
2. Delete PIR profiles and Privacy Pro Subscription
3. Switch over the Privacy Pro API from production to staging
4. Restore your Privacy Pro subscription
5. Create a new PIR profile
6. On the DB Browser, make sure Data Brokers don’t have a `removedAt` property
7. Switch to this branch and re-run the app
8. On the DB Browser, make sure Data Brokers now have a `removedAt` property and it’s populated with `nil` (DB Browser shows a `-`).
9. Change the `DBP API` service root to `branches/abuliga-remove-been-verified`, which has the broker BeenVerified set as removed.
10. Force Data Broker JSON update 
11. On the DB Browser, make sure the BeenVerified data broker now has a timestamp stored on the `removedAt` property 

#### Installing directly the version that supports Data Broker removal (migration v8) on a clean system
1. Follow the same setup steps as mentioned above up until step 5, but starting directly from the code on this branch
2. On the DB Browser, make sure the BeenVerified data broker has a timestamp stored on the `removedAt` property 

### Impact and Risks

This PR includes a DB migration, which can have some impact

#### What could go wrong?

PIR broker JSON updates could be impacted in case the migration fails. This PR includes extensive unit test coverage to de-risk this aspect.

### Quality Considerations

Please focus on migration testing, since the `removedAt` property won’t be used by the code yet.

title: macOS: Pixels for session restore prompt after app closes unexpectedly
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1211047835568341?focus=true
Tech Design URL: 
CC: @tomasstrba

⚠️ PR depends on https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/pull/1791 ⚠️  

### Description

Goal: Offer to restore session after a crash for users without automatic session restore enabled.

This PR adds pixels for the session restore prompt:
* When a crash (or other unexpected app termination) is detected.
* When the prompt is shown.
* When the prompt is dismissed (with/without restore).
* When the app is closed while the prompt is visible.

These pixels match the behavior and naming used in the Windows implementation; privacy triage task: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/69071770703008/task/1211080915255354?focus=true

### Testing Steps

1. Build the app, set internal user state, and ensure automatic session restore is disabled in Settings → General.
2. Open one or more websites (so there is something to restore).
3. Go to Debug > Simulate crash > select any crash type.
4. Reopen the app: Confirm the pixel `m_mac_unclean-exit_detected` is fired.
5. Prompt opens: Confirm when the prompt is shown, the pixel `m_mac_unclean-exit_popup_shown` is fired.
6. Test each of the following options (repeating steps 1-5 each time):
   * Select “No Thanks” and the pixel `m_mac_unclean-exit_popup_dismissed_without-restore` is fired.
   * Select “Restore Session” and confirm the pixel `m_mac_unclean-exit_popup_dismissed_with-restore` is fired.
   * Leave the prompt open and quit the app, and confirm the pixel `m_mac_unclean-exit_popup_browser-closed` is fired.

### Impact and Risks
None: Internal tooling, documentation

#### What could go wrong?
Pixels may not fire as expected; added unit test coverage.

### Quality Considerations
Need privacy triage

### Notes to Reviewer

title: Enables the Bitwarden Web Extension for internal users
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1206580121312550/task/1211182965070662?focus=true

### Description

Enables the Bitwarden Web Extension for internal users

### Testing Steps

#### Feature flag OFF

1. Turn the "webExtensions" feature flag off.
2. Ensure you're an internal user.
3. Restart the app.
4. Run the app, make sure password managers in both DMG and Sparkle builds work as usual.

#### Feature flag ON

Test in both DMG and App Store.

1. Turn the "webExtensions" feature flag on.
2. Ensure you're an internal user.
3. Restart the app.
4. Run the app - install extensions through the debug menu and make sure they work reasonably well.
5. Uninstall all extensions.
6. Go to App Settings > Passwords & Autofill > Select "Bitwarden Extension"
7. Make sure the Bitwarden extension works

### Impact and Risks

Low: only risk is if any of the code when the feature flag is OFF has been changed unintentionally.

#### What could go wrong?

Mostly focus on ensuring the code with the feature flag OFF is the same as it was before.
If we're affecting internal users with issues we can tackle as bugs, so it's slightly less problematic.

### Quality Considerations

NA

### Notes to Reviewer

Apologies for the large-ish PR: there's a lot of noise coming from moving the build configuration to feature flag, and other small adjustments across files.

This PR should be fine as long as we ensure the code with the feature flag OFF works as usual.  Please keep this in mind during review.

title: Only lock passwords view when non-empty DB
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1210881113393590?focus=true

### Description

iOS and Android only require authentication once you have an item stored in the password manager. Both macOS and Windows require authentication even when empty. Seems we should remove this requirement and match the mobile apps.

### Testing Steps
1. If necessary, clear your secure vault data by going to Debug -> Reset Data -> Reset Autofill Data
2. Open More menu -> Passwords and Autofill
3. **You should immediately see the empty state with no unlock prompt**
4. Add an item either by saving a login or directly in the Passwords and Autofill screen
5. (if necessary) Close the Passwords and Autofill popover and reopen (step 2 again)
6. **You should be prompted to unlock**

Also @amddg44 feel free to do some other smoke tests as you know this stuff better than me! 😅 

### Impact and Risks
High: Could affect user privacy, lose user data, break core functionality

#### What could go wrong?
If the logic is wrong, the screen could be unlocked when there are in fact passwords. However, I've made the logic such that the screen is completely inaccessible until the actual data in the database has been fetched. So I think this is pretty unlikely

title: Send debug pixel when BrowserServicesKit fails to load JS file
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1211054087327709
Tech Design URL:
CC: @ayoy @bwaresiak 

### Description

This updates `UserScript.loadJS(_:from:withReplacements:)` (in `BrowserServicesKit`) to throw an error when it fails to load the JS from the provided file/bundle. The thrown error bubbles up to the iOS and macOS clients (and their local DBP packages), which then fire a corresponding pixel and crash the app.

This pixel contains the JS file name, path, and underlying error to help us investigate the underlying cause of the crash that sometimes occurs when loading JS files.

Notable changes:
* Introduces `UserScriptError` to throw the relevant information (JS file name, path, and underlying error) so they can be included in the pixel.
* Introduces an extension to `UserScriptError` in each client to fire the pixel and wait a second, so the pixel has time to be fired before the app crashes.

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Confirm iOS and macOS apps build and run as expected.
2. Force an error to be thrown in each app (see notes to reviewer) and confirm the expected pixel is fired and the app crashes with the expected `fatalError`.

### Impact and Risks
<!-- 
What's the impact on users if something goes wrong?

High: Could affect user privacy, lose user data, break core functionality
Medium: Could disrupt specific features or user flows
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features
None: Internal tooling, documentation
-->
None: Should not affect users (app already crashes at this point)

#### What could go wrong?
<!-- Describe specific scenarios and how you've addressed them -->
There is potential for introducing different kinds of crashes (instead of the expected `fatalError`) if the app ends up in a bad state because of the thrown error, e.g. if an init method throws before its properties are initialized.
I have manually tested the points where a `fatalError` is called to confirm when the expected error is thrown it fires the pixel and results in the expected crash. I also added unit tests to confirm the expected error is thrown and the helper methods fire the expected pixel for each client.

### Quality Considerations

- How does this impact privacy/security?

### Notes to Reviewer
<!-- Anything specific you want reviewers to focus on -->

You can force a failure in testing by e.g. adding a deliberate `throw` to `UserScript.loadJS(_:from:withReplacements:)` and triggering it from one of the points in the app that calls this method:

```swift
    public static func loadJS(_ jsFile: String, from bundle: Bundle, withReplacements replacements: [String: String] = [:], forceThrow: Bool) throws -> String {

        let path = bundle.path(forResource: jsFile, ofType: "js")!

        if forceThrow {
            let error = NSError(domain: "Test", code: 1)
            throw UserScriptError.failedToLoadJS(jsFile: jsFile, path: path, error: error)
        }
```

title: iOS: New Search/Duck.ai Input - Metric - 6 Step Funnel
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1211206058788129?focus=true

### Description
Implements the following 6-step funnel: Settings Discovery → Feature Enablement → First Interaction → Search Submission → Prompt Submission → Full Conversion.

Technical Details: `SwitchBarFunnelStep` enum defines each step with dependencies, storage keys, and pixel mappings. Each step validates prerequisites automatically before firing pixels, ensuring accurate progression without complex eligibility logic.

New Pixels::
* `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_first_settings_viewed` (count) - First time viewing settings page with new input
* `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_first_enabled` (count) - First time enabling the new input
* `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_first_interaction` (count) - First text entry after enabling
* `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_first_search_submission` (count) - First successful search query
* `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_first_prompt_submission` (count) - First successful Duck.ai prompt
* `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_full_conversion_user` (count) - User achieves full conversion (used both search AND Duck.ai)

Note: When testing filter the Xcode console on “m.aichat” to see relevant pixels. Ignore pixels which are not part of this work.

### Testing Steps
#### Complete Funnel Flow
* **Prereqs**: Delete app from sim, launch app
* **Steps**: Navigate to settings → Enable feature → Type text → Submit search → Submit prompt
* **Expected**: All 6 pixels fire once in sequence: first_settings_viewed, first_enabled, first_interaction, first_search_submission, first_prompt_submission, full_conversion_user

#### Pre-Enabled User (No Funnel)
* **Prereqs**: Delete app from sim, set `showAIChatExperimentalSearchInputDefaultValue = true` in `AIChatSettings.swift`
* **Steps**: Navigate to settings → Use feature → Submit search/prompt
* **Expected**: NO funnel pixels fire (dependencies prevent progression without settings_viewed)

#### Reset and Restart
* **Prereqs**: Complete first enable step
* **Steps**: Disable feature → Leave settings → Return to settings → Re-enable → Complete funnel
* **Expected**: New funnel journey begins, all pixels fire again

#### Disable/Enable Without Leaving Settings
* **Prereqs**: Delete app from sim, launch app
* **Steps**: Navigate to settings → Enable feature → Disable feature → Re-enable feature (stay on settings page) → Use feature
* **Expected**: First enable fires settings_viewed + feature_enabled pixels. Disable resets funnel storage. Re-enable does NOT fire feature_enabled pixel again (blocked by missing settings_viewed dependency).

### Impact and Risks
Low. Mostly pixels.

title: Add more metrics and diagnostics to better understand bookmarks lost structure issue
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1211050177427683?focus=true
CC: @brindy 

### Description
1. Added 5 diagnostic parameters to identify root causes (sync status, recent errors, file marker presence)
2. Replaced 1 generic database error pixel with 10 specific error pixels for precise failure identification
3. Added pixel to track sync attempts to delete root folders
4. Added pixel to correlate structure loss with app crashes
5. Refactored legacy fatalError calls to structured error throwing with detailed tracking
6. Added file marker system to possibly distinguish backup restores from actual db corruption

### Testing Steps
1. Since there is no straightforward way to confirm that all errors are handled, the recommended approach is to review each error type originating from the Terminating class related to bookmarks. Attempt to reproduce conditions that trigger these errors and verify that they are properly propagated back to the Terminating class.
2. After triggering an error, recompile the app and simulate the structure_lost case. Verify that the recent-bookmark-error-* parameters are populated (non-nil).
3. Enable sync and confirm that the structure_lost pixel includes the parameter sync-enabled with the value true.
4. Use the Crash App option in the Debug menu, then recompile the app and again simulate the structure_lost case. Verify that the debugBookmarksStructureLostAfterCrash pixel is sent.

### Impact and Risks
What's the impact on users if something goes wrong?
High: Could affect user privacy, lose user data, break core functionality

#### What could go wrong?
Some app startup paths may have changed, and we might now be crashing in places we didn’t before.

title: macOS: Prevent post-crash restore prompt from interfering with UI tests
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1209825025475019/task/1211255127092280?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC: @tomasstrba 

### Description

There is a new post-crash restore prompt that is triggered when the app does not terminate as expected. This can be triggered by sudden app terminations in test runs, causing the prompt to appear and interfere with unrelated UI tests.

This PR disables the prompt during UI tests by skipping the check for unexpected app terminations. This is a bit risky because it alters the app behavior during UI tests, but as of now we aren’t doing any explicit UI testing of this prompt and it causes spurious failures. This allows the prompt to continue working normally outside of UI tests, e.g. in normal runs of debug/review builds. (I’ll raise this in the project postmortem for further discussion about potential risks/followups.)

### Testing Steps
<!-- Assume the reviewer is unfamiliar with this part of the app -->
1. Confirm UI tests pass and the prompt does not appear during UI test runs.
2. Build the app normally and ensure automatic session restore is disabled in Settings → General.
3. Open one or more websites (so there is something to restore).
4. Go to Debug > Simulate crash > select any crash type.
5. Reopen the app and confirm the popover appears.

### Impact and Risks

title: PixelKit new approach to errors
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1205842942115003/task/1211256910531201
CC: @diegoreymendez @bwaresiak @ayoy 

### Description

This PR modernizes PixelKit's error handling approach by consolidating the dual error system into a unified approach. The changes replace PixelKitEventV2 with PixelKitEvent and move error extraction to the protocol level using reflection.

Key Changes

- Removes PixelKitEventV2 protocol and consolidates into PixelKitEvent
- Adds reflection-based error extraction to PixelKitEvent protocol
- Updates all pixel events to use PixelKitEvent instead of PixelKitEventV2

Overall changes to PixelKit
- Passing an error as parameter to the `fire(...)` function is not allowed anymore
- The correct way to add an error (preferably DDGError) to a pixel is now to add a parameter to the enum:
```
enum SomePixelEvent: PixelKitEvent {
	case eventWithDDGError(DDGError)
	case eventWithError(Error)
}
```

### Testing Steps

1. PixelKit behaviour shold be unchanged
2. If a Pixel containing an error is not covered by unit tests, we should test it manually (which one??)

### Impact and Risks

We could break some grafana board

title: Create NewTabPageActionsManager in UserScriptDependenciesProviding also if NTP per tab is disabled
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1211288771017411?focus=true

### Description
This change prevents issues with opening New Tab Page when `newTabPagePerTab` feature flag
was enabled in runtime. `NewTabPageActionsManager` is now always instantiated in
`UserScriptDependenciesProviding` (implemented by `AppDelegate`) and it’s used by UserScripts
to initialize `NewTabPageUserScript` if needed (when `newTabPagePerTab` gets enabled).
This change does not affect app runs when `newTabPagePerTab` was enabled at launch time.

### Testing Steps
1. Clean app data via `macOS/clean-app.sh debug`
2. Launch the app
3. Set internal user state
4. Open a new window
5. Verify that it didn’t crash on assertion and the NTP loaded correctly

### Impact and Risks
None, besides higher memory usage (2 NTP Actions Managers allocated) until we migrate users to NTP per tab.

body:

Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

This PR attempt to fix crashes when the AudioSession is created or set active by delaying its creation until the video gets loaded. This happens when we’re about to show PiP to the user.

### Testing Steps
**Scenario 1 - “Onboarding"**
1. Open Debug Menu.
2. Select ‘Onboarding’.
3. Tap ‘Preview Onboarding Intro’ button.
4. Progress linear onboarding till ‘Protections Activated!’ screen.
5. Tap ‘Choose Your Browser’ button.
6. Ensure that the app deeplinks to the settings and PiP Video is playing.
7. Go back to the App.
8. Ensure that the PiP video is not playing anymore and the onboarding flow has progressed to:
9. ‘Add me to your Dock’ screen for iPhone.
10. 'Choose App Icon color’ screen for iPad.
11. On the 'Add me to your Dock’ screen tap the ’Shoe Me How’ button.
12. Ensure the 'Add to Dock' video plays fine.
13. Send the app to the background and ensure NO pip video plays.

**Scenario 2 - “Settings"**
1. Open Settings Menu.
2. Tap ‘Default Browser’ button from ‘Privacy Protections’ section.
3. Ensure that the app deeplinks to the settings and PiP Video is playing.
4. Go back to the App.
5. Ensure that the PiP video is not playing anymore.

**Scenario 3 - “SAD Active Users”:**
1. In DefaultBrowserModalPresenter.swift comment line 43-46 and 48-50.
2. Launch the app
3. Once the modal show tap ’Set Default Browser’ button.
4. Ensure that the app deeplinks to the settings and PiP Video is playing.
5. Go back to the App.
6. Ensure that the PiP video is not playing anymore.

**Scenario 4 - “SAD Inactive Users”**

title: [iOS] [Meta] Reorganize Mock Files
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211302760150219?focus=true ### Description Previously, all mock files were placed under a single directory under `Mocks`: `SharedTestUtils > Mocks > ` This structure made it: - Difficult to locate mocks needed for testing: Mocks weren’t organized by domain or class. - Harder to maintain mocks after changes in the original classes: increasing the risk of outdated mocks. - Messy and error-prone: it’s easy to accidentally create duplicated mocks when one wasn’t found. - Slowed down testing workflows: devs had to search through an unorganized list before proceeding. **Updated Approach** Mocks are now organized according to the location of their original class, eg.: `SharedTestUtils > Mocks > DuckDuckGo > Application > AppSettingsMock` This improves: - Discoverability: devs can quickly find the relevant mock by following the same structure. - Maintainability: changes in the original class are easier to track and reflect in its mock. - Consistency: prevents duplicated mocks by making existing ones visible in context. - Efficiency: smoother testing workflow. ### Impact and Risks None. Change is limited to the organization of test mocks. It does not affect production code #### What could go wrong? - Team adjustment: Devs may need to adapt to the new file paths. Addressed by aligning the folder structure with the production code’s structure, making it intuitive. ### Quality Considerations - Edge cases: Confirmed that no mocks were lost or renamed incorrectly. - Monitoring: Standard CI test runs will catch missing imports or broken references. ### Notes to Reviewer --- ###### Internal references: [Definition of Done](https://app.asana.com/0/1202500774821704/1207634633537039/f) | [Engineering Expectations](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/199064865822552) | [Tech Design Template](https://app.asana.com/0/59792373528535/184709971311943)

### Description

### Testing Steps
- Build and run the app.
- With the app terminated, send an Inactivity notification and tap it.
    - App should launch without crashing.

title: iOS: New Search/duck.ai Input Metrics - Daily Retention
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211327117482768

### Description
This adds a basic daily retention metric for our new input enabled setting.

**Requirements Met**: 
* We want to distinguish between growth vs churn masked by new acquisitions - are we retaining users who enable the feature, or constantly replacing churned users with new ones?

**Change**: Daily pixel that fires only for users who had the feature enabled yesterday (or last used day) and return today, indicating whether they kept it enabled or disabled it.

### Daily Retention Testing Prerequisites 
**Testing Prereq Code Change**: For testing purposes, modify the 24-hour threshold to 10 seconds in `SwitchBarRetentionMetrics.swift`:
```swift
let twentyFourHoursInSeconds: Double = 10  // Changed from: 24 * 60 * 60
```

### Daily Retention Testing Steps
#### First Time User (No Previous State)
* **Prereqs**: Fresh install
* **Steps**: Launch app
* **Expected**: No retention pixel fires (first check, state persisted for future)

#### Daily Retention - Feature Still Enabled
* **Steps**: 
  1. Launch app (feature disabled)
  2. Enable experimental omnibar → Wait 10+ seconds → Background app
  3. Foreground app -> Wait 10+ seconds → Background app
  4. Foreground app
* **Expected**: `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_daily_retention` pixel fires with `still_enabled: "true"`

#### Daily Churn - Feature Disabled  
* **Steps**: 
  1. Launch app (feature enabled) 
  2. Disable experimental omnibar → Wait 10+ seconds → Background app
  2. Foreground app
* **Expected**: `m_aichat_experimental_omnibar_daily_retention` pixel fires with `still_enabled: "false"`

#### Previous Disabled State - No Pixel Fired
* **Prereqs**: Have disabled experimental omnibar previously (>10 seconds ago)
* **Steps**: Keep disabled → Launch/foreground app (after 10+ second gap)
* **Expected**: No retention pixel fires (wasn't eligible - feature was disabled during last check)

### Impact and Risks
Minor, pixels.

---

title: [macOS] Fix assertion failure pixel call
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201037661562251/task/1211368892557106?focus=true
Tech Design URL:
CC:

### Description

We use the `pixelAssertionFailure(_:file:line:)` global function to send an assertion_failure pixel. The issue arises when firing the pixel with `PixelKit.fire(DebugEvent(GeneralPixel.assertionFailure(message: message(), file: file, line: line)))`. In this case, the convenient initializer for DebugEvent sets the event type to custom, which prevents the assertion failure parameters from being sent.

This has been fixed by using the designated initializer for DebugEvent and explicitly passing the event type

### Testing Steps
1. In AppDelegate -> `applicationDidFinishLaunching` line 1013. add call `pixelAssertionFailure(“Test Fix”)`
2. Ensure parameters are printed in the console log.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Fixes assertion failure pixel missing parameters

1. Using an existing app build that has completed onboarding, has some passwords saved, has some autofill usage dates stored (i.e. have performed a fill event etc) and has Sync enabled
2. Launch the app and confirm the prompt does not appear (since Sync enabled)
3. Disable Sync, reset the prompt via the Debug menu. (Actions section > Reset Sync Prompt on Launch)
4. Launch the app and confirm the prompt still does not appear (since you have passwords saved)
5. Delete all saved password & reset the prompt
6. Launch the app and confirm the prompt still does not appear (since even though you don’t have passwords saved, the vault keychain was created some time ago so you must not be setting up a new device)
7. Go to Debug > Keychain Items > Delete All to delete all keychain entries & reset the prompt
8. Confirm that this time you are now presented with the prompt 😅 
9. Tap to Cancel the prompt, relaunch the app and confirm you are not prompted again
10. In `SyncRecoveryPromptService` comment out L102-104 to disable the prompt check to make it easier to test the prompt actions
11. On the first prompt, confirm tapping the big blue button takes you to Sync > QR code scanner
12. On the first prompt, confirm tapping the secondary button takes you the second prompt screen
13. On the second prompt, confirming tapping the big blue button takes you to Sync > QR code scanner
14. On the second prompt, confirming tapping the secondary button takes you to Sync > Sync and Back Up This Device flow

I was also asked to include the ability to segue users to the Sync screen from remote messages. To test:
1. Go to Debug > Configuration URLs and enter this for the RMF config: https://www.jsonblob.com/api/1417851802602364928
2. In the Debug screen go to Remote Messaging > Refresh Config
3. Open a new tab, and in the RMF message presented tap the “Go to Sync” button
4. Confirm you are navigated to Settings > Sync

### Impact and Risks
Low: More users than intended could end up getting the prompt

#### What could go wrong?
- Feature flag added (enabled by default) allows us to turn off remotely if users are being wrongly targeted
- Pixels added to allow us to see usage & act if numbers are unexpectedly high

body:
<!--

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1211370094007442?focus=true
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1210594645229050/task/1211246229562518?focus=true
CC: @bwaresiak 

### Description

This PR introduces a new GitHub workflow to interact with Smartling. Key points:
* `localization_tool.py`: Smartling API client written in Python
* `smartling.yml` the main workflow file. I tried to offload most work into scripts:
  * `smartling_download.sh`, `smartling_upload.sh`, `smartling_approve.sh`, `smartling_status.sh` for the possible actions
  * `smartling_messages.sh` for constructing a report (currently they are added to the step summary of the workflow)
* `check_translation_integrity.py` runs after import and will check;
  * if there are any deleted lines in the git diff
  * if there are value changes in the `.strings` and `.stringsdict` files
* `loc_tool.sh` is a “coordinator”. It interacts with the existing import/export scripts, and the Smartling client to perform the requested job

### Testing Steps
Before the workflow is merged into main, it can only be tested manually with the `gh` command line tool. Examples:
```
# Start upload
gh workflow run Smartling -f platform=iOS -f action=upload --ref jozsef/smartling-api-client

# Check status
gh workflow run Smartling -f platform=iOS -f action=status -f job-id=uyw9jwktorgi --ref jozsef/smartling-api-client

# Authorize translation job
gh workflow run Smartling -f platform=iOS -f action=approve -f job-id=uyw9jwktorgi --ref jozsef/smartling-api-client

# Start download (you can try this with any existing job-id from Smartling
gh workflow run Smartling -f platform=iOS -f action=download -f job-id=rkuqad25uz0f --ref jozsef/smartling-api-client
```

Results can be [checked here.](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/workflows/smartling.yml)

### Impact and Risks
None: Internal tooling

#### What could go wrong?
* when running `download` with `force=true`, it may produce a destructive import.

### Quality Considerations
For coding standards I used Shellcheck and pylint.

### Notes to Reviewer
I’m not a pro at shell scripts or Python, so I leaned pretty hard on LLM, search results, and GitHub Docs.

title: Fire a pixel for internal users when unified URL prediction differs from the native one
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1211396583578252?focus=true

### Description
This change adds a pixel that is fired only for internal users, when the unified URL prediction differs
from the native one.

### Testing Steps
1. Launch the app and set internal user state.
2. Enable `unifiedURLPrediction` and `unifiedURLPredictionMetrics` feature flags.
3. Filter logs for `m_mac_debug_unified`.
4. Navigate to a few URLs or type a few search phrases and verify that no pixels appear in the log.
5. Quit the app and comment lines 173-175 in URLExtension.swift:
```swift
if let addressBarUrl = URL(trimmedAddressBarString: trimmed), addressBarUrl.isValid {
    return addressBarUrl
}
```
6. Launch the app. Type a valid URL – note that if you’ve used that URL before, a first suggestion on the list may be highlighted so remove that highlight using the up arrow key before pressing Enter. Verify that you’ve navigated to the URL and that a pixel is fired with `prediction: navigate` parameter and the input containing the phrase typed in the address bar.
7. Disable `unifiedURLPredictionMetrics` feature flag, repeat the previous step and verify that no pixel has been sent.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

#### What could go wrong?
Metrics are gathered for external users. This is gated by 2 feature flags now when one of them (the metrics one) will remain hardcoded as `disabled` so won’t be able to get updated via the remote config.

title: Smartling automation: add support for PR labels
body:
<!--
Note: This template is a reminder of our Engineering Expectations and Definition of Done. Remove sections that don't apply to your changes.

⚠️ If you're an external contributor, please file an issue before working on a PR. Discussing your changes beforehand will help ensure they align with our roadmap and that your time is well spent.
