Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1210594645229050/task/1211443495906924
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/481882893211075/task/1211246229562518
CC: @bwaresiak 

### Description
As the continuation of #1981, this PR allows triggering Smartling workflows via PR labels:
* start ios translation - Uploads iOS translation files and creates a new Smartling job
* start macos translation - Uploads macOS translation files and creates a new Smartling job
* authorize translation - Approves a Smartling job for translation (requires job ID in PR comments)
* download translations - Downloads completed translations and imports them (requires job ID in PR comments)
* check translation status - Checks status (requires job ID in PR comments)

The workflow manages label transitions to provide status visibility:
  1. `needs translation authorization` is applied after successful upload
  2. `translation in progress` is applied after job authorization
  3. `check translation status` will set the label to:
    * `translations ready` if translations are ready to download
    * `needs translation authorization` if the job is not authorized
    * `translation in progress` if job is still in progress 

The workflow will also post PR comments with the step results.

### Testing Steps
* Try adding `start ios translation` or `start macos translation` labels to this PR
* You can also try `authorize translation` which will likely fail since there’s no new content to translate

### Impact and Risks
None: Internal tooling improvements

### Description
This change updates TLD.swift to source TLDs from Public Suffix List data provided by URLPredictor module.
Some test cases in TLDTests were removed because they are no longer valid (“example” is not a valid domain as per PSL). 

### Testing Steps
1. Verify that CI is green.
2. Install [iOS adhoc](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/18000420560) and [macOS review](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/actions/runs/18000414556) builds and verify that they don’t crash at startup. Also verify that the macOS build doesn’t crash when submitting a search query / url in the address bar.

### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

#### What could go wrong?
This change would introduce URLPredictor module (together with the Rust library) to the iOS app, so I’m derisking potential issues related to building a release app by making an adhoc build.
Also, URLPredictorRust.xcframework is actually a set of static libraries, so there’s no dynamic linking overhead to the app startup time.

body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1211397835604444
Tech Design URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201048563534612/task/1211442004321890?focus=true
CC:

### Description
This PR implements functionality to restore Duck.ai sidebar state if reopened within predefined time frame (via privacy config setting).

### Testing Steps
**Test when recent chats are ON**
1. Enable `aiChatKeepSession` feature flag
2. Make sure that within the Duck.ai settings recent chats are ON.
3. Open a tab and navigate to website
4. Open sidebar and start a conversation (wait until response completes)
5. Collapse sidebar
6. Reveal sidebar on same tab
7. Validate that the previous conversation was loaded
8. Repeat 5-7

**Test when recent chats are OFF**
1. Enable `aiChatKeepSession` feature flag
2. Make sure that within the Duck.ai settings recent chats are OFF.
3. Open a tab and navigate to website
4. Open sidebar and start a conversation (wait until response completes)
5. Collapse sidebar
6. Reveal sidebar on same tab
7. Validate that the previous conversation was loaded 
8. Repeat 5-7
Note: This won't now work due to a missing implementation on FE side, see https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203936086921904/task/1211457419239104?focus=true
Note2: You can alternatively use temporary dev instance and set custom Duck.ai URL to https://use-serp-dev-testing10.duck.co/?q=DuckDuckGo+AI+Chat&ia=chat&duckai=2

**Test old behaviour**
1. Disable `aiChatKeepSession` feature flag
2. Smoke test and ensure that sidebar always reopens to a new conversation.
3. Smoke test "Expand" button functionality when recent chats are ON
4. Smoke test "Expand" button functionality when recent chats are OFF
5. Open multiple tabs, on each tab open sidebar and have various conversations. Validate that state restoration works.


### Impact and Risks
Low: Minor visual changes, small bug fixes, improvement to existing features

Expand button functionality broken.

> [!NOTE]
> Exclude removed brokers from initial scan progress and maintenance next-scan data sent to the Web UI, while keeping resultsFound computation unchanged.
> 
> - **Core/UI Web**:
>   - **Initial Scan State (`DBPUIInitialScanState`)**:
>     - Filter out `dataBroker.isRemoved` before grouping and calculating `scanProgress` (current/total/scannedBrokers).
>     - Keep `resultsFound` based on non-deprecated queries, including removed brokers.
>   - **Maintenance State (`DBPUIScanAndOptOutMaintenanceState`)**:
>     - Compute `nextScan` (brokers and earliest date) from non-removed brokers only.
> - **Tests**:
>   - Add tests ensuring removed brokers are excluded from initial scan progress and maintenance next scans, but still present in `resultsFound`.
>   - Extend mocks to support `removedAt` on `DataBroker` and `BrokerProfileQueryData`.

title: Debounce macOS webkit termination pixel to deal with pixel bursts
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1211198745312534?focus=true

### Description

Debounce macOS webkit termination pixel to deal with pixel bursts.

Also added a new crash-testing option to make the tab crash multiple times in a row.

### Testing Steps

1. Enable Feature Flag > Other > `tabCrashDebugging`
2. Open a tab.
3. Right click on the tab title, select "Crash Tab"

```
👾[Daily and Count-Skipped] m_mac_debug_webkit_did_terminate_daily ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "available_diskspace": "5.03", "available_memory": "53", "d": "WKErrorDomain", "e": "2", "os_version": "15.7.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "ud": "WKErrorDomain", "ue": "2"]
👾[Daily and Count-Fired] m_mac_debug_webkit_did_terminate ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "available_diskspace": "5.03", "available_memory": "53", "d": "WKErrorDomain", "e": "2", "os_version": "15.7.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "ud": "WKErrorDomain", "ue": "2"]
```

4. If you trigger that again within 5 seconds, you'll get a different thing:

```
👾[Daily and Count-Fired] m_mac_webkit_termination_loop_daily ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg"]
👾[Daily and Count-Fired] m_mac_webkit_termination_loop ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg"]
👾[Daily and Count-Skipped] m_mac_debug_webkit_did_terminate_daily ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "available_diskspace": "5.03", "available_memory": "54", "d": "WKErrorDomain", "e": "2", "os_version": "15.7.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "ud": "WKErrorDomain", "ue": "2"]
👾[Daily and Count-Fired] m_mac_debug_webkit_did_terminate ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "available_diskspace": "5.03", "available_memory": "54", "d": "WKErrorDomain", "e": "2", "os_version": "15.7.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "ud": "WKErrorDomain", "ue": "2"]
```

5. At this point you might need to reload the web view if it's empty.
6. Wait 5 seconds.
7. Next thing select from the same menu "Crash multiple times".  You should see this (order might change):

```
👾[Daily and Count-Skipped] m_mac_debug_webkit_did_terminate_daily ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "available_diskspace": "5.03", "available_memory": "49", "d": "WKErrorDomain", "e": "2", "os_version": "15.7.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "ud": "WKErrorDomain", "ue": "2"]
👾[Daily and Count-Fired] m_mac_webkit_termination_loop_daily ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg"]
👾[Daily and Count-Fired] m_mac_debug_webkit_did_terminate ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "available_diskspace": "5.03", "available_memory": "49", "d": "WKErrorDomain", "e": "2", "os_version": "15.7.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg", "ud": "WKErrorDomain", "ue": "2"]
👾[Daily and Count-Fired] m_mac_webkit_termination_loop ["appVersion": "1.158.0", "pixelSource": "browser-dmg"]

```

### Impact and Risks

Low: just adding rate-limiting / leading-edge debouncing logic for a pixel.
